info.title: Crossly Seller API
info.description: The seller-facing Crossly API — listings, crossposting, orders, analytics. Authenticate with a Personal Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer crossly_pat_…`) or a seller OAuth token (`crossly_oat_…`), scoped `<domain>:<read|write>`. Buyer endpoints are a SEPARATE API with a separate principal — see the Crossly Buyer API.

message.description: The exact text to present for signing.

holders.description: Distinct people holding a live copy.

maxSupply.description: The design's edition cap. Null = open edition, never eligible (minting it means nothing).

resales.description: Copies resold between players (closed auction sales).

inUse.description: People wearing / placing it right now.

name.description: Which site this is for, e.g. "my Squarespace shop".

allowedOrigins.description: Origins permitted to use this key, e.g. ["https://shop.example.com"]. LEAVE EMPTY to allow any origin — necessary when embedding on a platform whose domain you do not control, and the reason this is not locked by default.

environment.description: Omit for this server's own: live on crossly.net, test on sandbox.crossly.net. The other one is refused.

changed.description: Field keys (see RuleTrace.field) a rule actually changed.

trimmed.description: Field keys that were cut to the platform's length limit after the rules ran.

estFeeCents.description: Simple interest for the full term at the line's APR, rounded to the cent.

CreateGamePackBreakPickResponseDataCoupo.description: The coupon this win earned (null on a loss, or past the daily coupon).

askCents.description: The lowest open ask when the pack was dealt, in cents.

stage.description: Which address decided a refusal: the buyer's, or the ship-together hub.

partial.description: The answer could change once a fuller address (state, ZIP) is known.

metroUnmapped.description: An include metro rule could not see this ZIP (it is not mapped to any metro).

services.description: What the buyer could pick; empty when the policy does not ship there.

policySource.description: Where the policy came from: the draft, a preset, or the seller's default.

complete.description: A full address, including a postal code where the country has one.

CreateGeoLocationCheckResponseFacts.description: The buyer address as the rules saw it.

complete.description: A full address, including a postal code where the country has one.

CreateGeoLocationCheckResponseHubFacts.description: The hub as the rules saw it, when consolidating.

minDays.description: Transit business days (handling time is added separately).

carrierService.description:
Buyer pays: calculated at checkout (shared policies/calculated-shipping.ts).
The Shippo servicelevel token this service buys: its price is that live
label rate for the parcel, plus `handlingFeeCents` once per shipment.
Never stored on a policy; domesticServices derives it from `domestic.calculated`.

grade.description: As the grader writes it in our grade vocabulary: '10', '8.5', 'Authentic'.

label.description: The grader's own label, e.g. 'GEM MT 10'.

description.description: What the grader says the item is: year, set, subject, number.

population.description: How many the grader has graded at this grade, and higher — when it publishes them.

note.description: Optional text sent with the offer; the marketplace shows it as a message of its own.

affected.description: Rows whose available stock actually changed.

skipped.description:
Ids that did not move. Either they were already at that number, or they
aren't this seller's. The two are deliberately not distinguished: telling
a caller "that id isn't yours" confirms the id exists.

bulkJobId.description: Watchable job for the marketplace fan-out, when one was started.

created.description: New items written — or, on a dry run, that WOULD be written.

updated.description: Existing items updated by SKU — or, on a dry run, that would be.

usable.description:
Rows that can be imported: `created + updated + skippedOverLimit`.
Zero means the file has nothing usable in it.

skippedOverLimit.description: New rows left out because the monthly item limit was reached.

dryRun.description: True when nothing was written — a preview pass.

limit.description: Items the plan allows per calendar month. `null` = unlimited.

used.description: Items already created this month, before this import.

remaining.description: New items this import may still add. `null` = unlimited.

line.description:
1-based, and counting the header — so it matches what the seller sees
in their spreadsheet. Off-by-one here makes every error unfindable.

aiGenerated.description: Always true — the image is recorded as AI-generated.

currency.description: ISO display currency for `price` (GBP for a UK-eBay store). NULL = USD.

videoUrl.description: Optional single product video (R2/CDN URL). Shown on the Crossly buyer page.

aiMediaUrls.description:
URLs among images/videoUrl that a generative model made (0495). The shop's
AI tag fires while any of them is still on the listing.

aiMediaDeclared.description: Seller's own declaration that the listing uses AI images/video (0495).

aiMediaDetectedUrls.description:
Images Crossly's AI-image detector flagged (0507; ai_media_detections,
kept in step by services/ai-images/detected.ts). Never client-written.

gradeKey.description:
Third-party grading, when the item is slabbed. Migration 0277.

Separate from `condition` on purpose and never derived from it: a grade
is a claim about what a GRADING COMPANY certified, and inferring "PSA 10"
from a coarse condition would be a false authenticity claim. It is also
never filled from our own AI estimate (`bulk_market_items.grade`), which
carries an explicit "not a professional grade" disclaimer.

`gradeKey` is the canonical form from `gradeKey()` in
shared/constants/graders.ts; `grading` holds the full GradingInfo
including the cert number and whether a cert lookup verified it.

material.description: Migration 0179 — see the matching fields on inventory_items above.

isDigital.description:
Physical good (false, the default) or digital one. Migration 0314.

The discriminator the whole physical/digital boundary is evaluated
against: physical items are CBX/cash only and NEVER reach the COSM
auction house, digital items may use either rail. Before this the
rule existed only as prose — nothing in schema/ could ask whether an
item was physical, so `docs/METAVERSE-ECONOMY-PLAN.md` §1 was
unenforceable by construction.

Why it is a fact about the LISTING: a listing is what gets sold
(`crossly_auctions` keys on a platform listing, the shop cart sells
listings), while inventory is what is owned, and the two are M:N —
so an inventory-side flag could not answer "is this sale digital"
for a multi-item listing, nor at all for the listings that have no
inventory row (external-sale stubs, bundle parents).

Why the default is false: fail closed. A row nobody classified is
barred from the auction house rather than admitted to it.

`scripts/check-auction-physical.mjs` (in `pnpm typecheck`) fails the
build on any code path that can carry a listing into COSM's
cosmetics/auction tables without gating on this column. Migration
0314 also adds UNIQUE (id, is_digital) so a future COSM-side table
can make the refusal a composite FK rather than a convention.

publishAt.description:
Scheduled go-live time. When set on a draft, the listing-scheduler
worker waits until this passes then dispatches the crosspost to
scheduledPlatforms and flips status from 'draft' to 'active'.

scheduledPlatforms.description:
Which platforms to publish to when publishAt fires. JSON array of
platform ids. Null/empty = scheduler skips (listing won't auto-
publish, even after publishAt — gives the seller an escape hatch).

parentListingId.description:
Parent listing when this row is a CHILD in a listing chain. Null =
standalone. What being a child means depends on the parent's
`groupKind` — see it.

groupKind.description:
What kind of chain this listing is the PARENT of. Null = not a parent.

`parentListingId` alone models "N listings chained under one" and that
shape is not bundle-specific — three features want it, differing only
in what happens when something sells:

  'bundle'     buy the whole thing as one unit. Children never publish
               on their own; the parent is what goes to marketplaces;
               selling the parent marks every child sold.
  'variation'  buy one of N (sizes, card conditions, vinyl pressings).
               Children DO publish — individually on single-axis
               platforms like Depop/Poshmark, as one group on
               eBay/Shopify/Etsy. Selling one child must NOT touch its
               siblings.
  'group'      buy N of these together under a purchase rule ("three
               $1 cards, or pair it with something") so shipping does
               not eat the margin.

A boolean could not express three, and the dangerous direction is
specific: `sale/detect/bundle-cascade.ts` reading `isBundle` on a
variation parent would mark every other size sold when one size sold.
That is why the cascade gates on this column, not on isBundle.

Chains are depth-1, enforced by a DB trigger (migration 0238) — every
consumer assumes two levels and discovering otherwise inside the sale
cascade costs a wrongly-delisted inventory.

automationAssignedRuleIds.description:
Per-listing automation overrides. See migration 0098.

 automationAssignedRuleIds  — force-include for these rules
 automationBlockedRuleIds   — exempt from these rules
 automationAssignedChainIds — force-include for these workflow chains
 automationBlockedChainIds  — exempt from these workflow chains

hsCode.description: Harmonised System customs code — international shipping declarations.

countryOfOrigin.description: Customs country of origin. Distinct from the seller's location.

priceFloorCents.description:
Never let a repricing rule go below this. On the ITEM because it is a
fact about the thing owned, not about any one rule — "this jacket never
goes below $45" should apply to every rule, and before this it was
expressible only as one rule per jacket. Listings inherit when null.

floorIsNet.description:
When true the floor is a TAKE-HOME target, converted to a per-platform
gross at reprice time. A gross floor is four different promises across
four platforms; this is the one number a seller actually cares about.

ebayAttributesEnrichedAt.description:
When the eBay per-item attribute back-fill (GetItem → condition/
category/item-specifics/…) last RAN for this listing — set whether or
not it found anything, so the background enrichment pass
(services/import-listings/ebay-attribute-enrich.ts) terminates and
resumes cleanly: it only picks up eBay listings where this is null.
The bulk import leaves it null (it only reads GetMyeBaySelling, which
carries none of those fields); null on a non-eBay listing is just
"n/a". See quota.ts for why this is decoupled from the import.

source.description:
Mirrors inventory_items.source. 'manual' for every seller-created
listing; external-stub.ts sets 'external_sale' on the synthetic
listing it fabricates for a sale detected on a platform id Crossly
never listed — those rows have no real photos/description of their
own (everything is lifted from the platform's sale payload) and are
otherwise indistinguishable from a real listing in the UI.

duplicateOfListingId.description:
Set when import's bin-packing (see _import-one.ts) created THIS
listing to hold a same-platform straggler it couldn't fit onto an
existing candidate listing for the same physical item — points at
the primary/first candidate. Purely informational: this listing
is a real, independently listable/delistable row, not a shadow.
Null for every ordinarily-created listing.

clientDraftId.description:
UUID minted on a seller's machine for a draft written offline.

The idempotency key for desktop sync. The failure it guards is a POST
that succeeds server-side whose reply is lost — the client cannot tell
that from a failure, retries, and one item becomes two live listings
against one piece of stock. Unique per user (partial index, migration
0268); null for every listing that did not come from an offline draft.

attributedOauthAppId.description:
The third-party OAuth app that created this listing (via its access
token), if any — the anchor for developer revenue-share: the app that
created the item earns a cut of its sales. Stamped once at create time
(first writer wins, never overwritten); null for the web app, a PAT, or
anything first-party. `attributedGrantId` pins the specific install whose
agreed terms apply. See services/developer-earnings/.

suggested.description:
What we'd offer to do about this match. A suggestion for which button to
feature — never a decision. All three actions stay available.

variationGroupId.description:
The variation group to ADD to, when the match already belongs to one.
Null means there is no group yet and choosing `variation` creates one from
the match plus the new listing. Without this the UI has to guess, and
guessing wrong means either a second group beside the first or a silent
no-op.

listingId.description:
The seller's existing listing this scan probably duplicates (null if the
match landed only on an inventory item with no listing row).

inventoryItemId.description:
The inventory item behind that listing, when linked. Drives the
"View inventory" button.

score.description: 0–1 confidence. Image matches report 1; title matches the similarity.

newQuantityAvailable.description: Stock on the keeper's item after summing.

unitsMoved.description: Units moved off the merged items.

delistJobsDispatched.description: Delist jobs dispatched for the merged listings' live platforms.

currency.description: ISO currency `price` is in, as the platform reported it (eBay UK → GBP).

marketplaceId.description:
The platform SITE this listing is on, for platforms that list one item
per site (eBay: EBAY_GB, EBAY_US, …). Drives the import site filter and
is stored on platform_listings.marketplace_id.

color.description:
Color(s) the platform's own response exposes (e.g. Poshmark's
`colors` array). Only set when actually present in the scrape.

stockLocation.description:
Where the goods physically are, when the platform tells us.

Only the consignment-aware marketplaces set it (Alias reports
`consigned`; POIZON's consignment listings are created that way). Absent
means 'seller', which is correct for every other platform.

category.description:
The platform's OWN category, as a top-down path (e.g. Poshmark's
["Kids", "Toys", "Dolls & Accessories"] from department → category →
feature). Only set when the platform's list/scrape response actually
carries this — never guessed. Mapped onto Crossly's category.main/
sub/sub2 (listings) or categoryMain/categorySub (inventory_items) at
create/enrich time.

categoryId.description:
The platform's raw numeric category id, same space as
overrides.<platform>.categoryId — distinct from `category`'s
human-readable path. Only set by platforms whose id space is directly
comparable to what we publish (currently eBay's drift-check second
call — see diff-fields/second-call.ts's ebayRemoteFields). eBay's own
CategoryName wording/depth is a different vocabulary from Crossly's
master taxonomy breadcrumb and will essentially never string-match
it, so drift-detection compares ids instead of names.

tags.description:
Tag-like strings the platform's own response exposes (e.g. Poshmark's
marketing "experience" tags). Distinct from a full search-tag
generator — just whatever real tag data the scrape already carries.

material.description:
Structured item aspects — the same shape the listing form's Item
Details section captures (and templates already persist), now sourced
from the platform's own data instead of only manual entry. Only set
when the platform's response genuinely carries a semantically-matching
field (eBay item specifics, Facebook attributes, Poshmark catalog,
Depop's detail-call ride-along) — never derived or guessed.

itemSpecifics.description:
Category-specific facets from a per-item DETAIL call (e.g. Facebook's
Age Range/Character/Age Group), keyed the same way eBay item-specifics
are: aspect name -> value array. Only set by platforms with a genuine
per-item attribute source — costs one extra call per listing, so
populated by a dedicated enrichment pass, not the main list mapper.
Maps onto listings.itemSpecifics; inventory_items has no equivalent
column.

listedAt.description:
When the listing was first published on the platform. Used by
the Advanced filter's listedAfter / listedBefore knobs. Optional
because not every platform returns it on the listing endpoint.

quantity.description:
Units this platform reports. Only meaningful for platforms
`PLATFORM_QUANTITY_SYNC` marks 'native' — relist platforms show one item
and say 1 forever, so they leave this undefined rather than voting with
a number they cannot actually express. See `_quantity.ts`.

accountSlot.description:
Which of the user's connected accounts on this platform this listing
was scraped from — stamped by fetchCookieListings as it loops each
connected account (see listActiveForPlatform in
user-platform-accounts/read.ts). Undefined for API-track platforms
(single connection, no multi-account concept) and for any cookie path
that hasn't been threaded yet; importOne treats undefined as slot 1,
matching the historical single-account default.

weightOz.description:
Total item weight in ounces (already summed, not split lb+oz —
the write path converts to the DB's weightLb+weightOz split).

handlingTimeDays.description:
Max days the platform's own listing commits to ship within (eBay's
DispatchTimeMax, Etsy's processing_max).

itemLocation.description:
Free text as the platform itself expresses it (e.g. eBay's `Location`
is a single seller-typed string like "Austin, TX", not a structured
address) — never parsed into city/state.

declaredShippingCost.description:
What the platform's OWN listing declares shipping costs — reference
only, distinct from a realized post-sale shipping cost.

aiAvailable.description:
False when the seller has no AI provider configured — `count: 0` then
means "nothing new could be resolved" rather than "already complete",
a distinction the caller (web's useMagicFill toast) needs but `count`
alone can't express. True whenever a provider IS configured, even if
the AI call itself failed for some other reason (network, bad key) —
that's a different problem than "connect a provider."

inventoryItemIds.description: Inventory items after the merge (for a stock reconcile).

jobs.description: One dispatched crosspost job per accepted platform.

skipped.description:
Platforms not dispatched, and why (category gate, dropship_not_allowed_on_platform, a dispatch
refusal such as validation_error "Add a weight before listing", ...). The listing itself was created.

warnings.description: Soft item-specifics problems (strictItemSpecifics off) and eBay fields accepted but mapped or ignored.

whipUrl.description: WHIP endpoint for publishing from a browser; null when the ingest has none.

topHits.description:
Unified top-10-globally list, ranked by CLIP visual similarity to
the seller's source photo. Each hit carries its origin platform.

ebayHits.description:
Legacy compat — UI's existing render. ebayHits now == visually-
validated eBay subset; otherMatches is re-grouped from topHits.

imageUrls.description: Every photo the seller uploaded for this scan, primary first.

visionAspects.description:
Vision-LLM aspects extracted across all photos. Populated only
when the seller has magic-list-vision-aspects enabled + a vision
provider configured. Empty otherwise.

possibleDuplicates.description:
The seller's OWN listings/inventory that this scan probably duplicates
(image + fuzzy-title self-dedup). Empty when nothing matched. Drives the
"you may already have this" prompt.

priceCents.description: Normalized cents. eBay returns string + currency on `price.value`.

categoryId.description: Top-level category eBay assigned to the match (id + path).

aspects.description:
Loosely-typed aspect bag — Brand, Color, Material, etc. when eBay
inlines them. Always inspected defensively by the synthesizer.

priceCents.description: Normalized cents. eBay returns string + currency on `price.value`.

categoryId.description: Top-level category eBay assigned to the match (id + path).

aspects.description:
Loosely-typed aspect bag — Brand, Color, Material, etc. when eBay
inlines them. Always inspected defensively by the synthesizer.

CreateMagicScanResponseEbayMatch.description:
Top eBay match (or null when eBay returned zero). Drives the
synthesize step's title/brand/price seed.

confidence.description: 0–1. What it is depends on `source`; see the rungs below.

reason.description: Human-readable, for a UI that has to explain why it prefilled a field.

CreateMagicScanResponsePhotoIdentifier.description:
A checksummed identifier established from the photo itself, or null.

── WHY THIS OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS RESULT ─────────────
The rest of a scan is RESEMBLANCE: eBay image search and CLIP ranking
find listings that look like the seller's photo, which is the right tool
when nothing better exists and is strictly worse than knowing what the
thing IS. A GTIN read off a barcode, or matched against a retailer's own
product shot, resolves to catalogue data, real comps and a price history
for THAT product rather than for products that photograph like it.

Null far more often than not, and deliberately so — see
`identify-from-photo.ts` for why the floors are set where they are. A
wrong identifier silently attaches a seller's listing to another
product's identity, which is worse than no identifier at all.

listingId.description:
The seller's existing listing this scan probably duplicates (null if the
match landed only on an inventory item with no listing row).

inventoryItemId.description:
The inventory item behind that listing, when linked. Drives the
"View inventory" button.

score.description: 0–1 confidence. Image matches report 1; title matches the similarity.

variationGroupId.description:
The variation group the matched listing already belongs to, if any.

This is what turns "you already have this" into something useful for a
seller scanning a size run. Scan the Medium, scan the Large, and the
second scan lands here — the honest answer is usually neither "it's the
same one" nor "it's different", it's "it's another size of that". Which
of the two offers to make depends entirely on this field:

  null      → offer to CREATE a group from the match and the new listing
  set       → offer to ADD the new listing to the group that exists

Without it the UI would have to guess, and guessing wrong means either a
second group beside the first or a silent no-op.

origin.description: Origin marker for the UI badge.

visualSim.description: CLIP cosine [0,1]; populated after the visual-rank pass.

state.description:
'active' = currently for sale; 'sold' = historical comp. UI
renders distinct badges so the seller can see both at a glance.

condition.description:
Master form enum value — one of new/like_new/good/fair/poor. The
heuristic synth maps eBay/Mercari/Poshmark condition strings into
this canonical form so the UI's <Select> finds a match.

priceCents.description:
Echoed user-selected price (cents). Set on every synthesize call
so the master form's defaultPrice input gets populated regardless
of which path (AI or heuristic) generated the rest.

sellerNote.description:
The seller's own words about this item — the pre-scan hint, or the
post-scan note that supersedes it (see synthesize/seller-note.ts).
Carried on the payload so the TAXONOMY resolvers see it too: category
and facet picking happen in their own LLM calls, which never saw the
note even after the main synthesis prompt did. A seller correcting the
variant was still getting the category of the wrong one.

priceLowCents.description:
Comp price band (cents), outlier-trimmed — low/median/high across the
matched comps. The UI surfaces the range so the seller prices
strategically instead of trusting one number; priceCents defaults to
the median when the seller hasn't picked.

quantity.description:
Echoed seller-supplied listable-unit count from Magic List. This is
the listing's ADVERTISED stock (how many of this listing to sell).
Hydrates the form's `quantity` field. Undefined = leave form default (1).

createInventoryItem.description:
Whether Magic List should turn this scan into a stock-tracked
inventory item on first save (the "Create an inventory item" toggle
on the results page). Undefined/true = create (historical default).

inventoryQuantity.description:
Physical units the seller actually has in stock — becomes the auto-
created inventory item's quantity/quantityAvailable. Distinct from
`quantity` (advertised stock) and `unitsPerListing` (composition).
Undefined = fall back to `quantity`.

unitsPerListing.description:
How many physical units are bundled inside ONE listing (composition;
e.g. a pack of 4). Becomes listing_inventory_items.quantity so the
multi-channel fulfillable = floor(inventoryQuantity / unitsPerListing).
Undefined = 1.

costBasisCents.description:
What the seller paid, per physical unit, in cents — the auto-created
inventory item's `costBasisCents`. Nothing wrote that column from any
create path, so every Magic List item had a NULL cost basis and every
sale of one reported its full sale price as profit. Undefined = unknown,
which stays NULL (0 would be a claim that the item was free).

imageUrls.description:
Every photo the seller uploaded for the source scan, primary
first. The NewListingPage hydrator drops these straight into the
form's images state so the seller doesn't have to re-upload.

department.description:
eBay item-specifics: Department/Gender/Style/Pattern/Type. These
drive the eBay-required aspects on the form's Item Details
section. Mostly only eBay matches have them.

upc.description:
Universal product code, when eBay's enriched detail surfaced it.
Hydrates the master form's UPC/GTIN field.

shippingPaidBy.description:
Seller-policy defaults. Reasonable picks based on category +
averages. Leave seller free to override.

itemSpecifics.description:
Master-level item specifics (JSON Record<string,string[]>). Item
specifics are now master-owned + fanned to every aspect platform, so the
form's shared Item-specifics editor prefills from this. Mirrored from the
richest resolved per-platform specifics blob (eBay after full-aspect
enrichment). Undefined = no specifics.

perPlatformOverrides.description:
Per-platform required-fields map — slotted directly into
platformOverrides when the form hydrates.

confidence.description:
AI's confidence in the synthesis (0-1). Surfaced to the seller
so they can decide whether to skim or trust + click.

notes.description:
AI's free-text rationale for the merge — what it pulled from
where. Helps the seller spot a bad merge before listing.

CreateMagicScanSynthesizeResponsePayload.description:
Category path — split into [main, sub, sub2] when present. eBay
categoryPath is the cleanest source.

energyLabel.description: EU energy-efficiency label (fridges, TVs, lighting, appliances).

CreateMagicScanSynthesizeResponsePayload.description:
Deterministic (NO-AI) applicability hint for the heavyweight optional
form sections (vehicle compatibility, EU EPR / energy label, hazmat).
Computed from the resolved category + seller region via
`applicableOptionalSections`; the form pre-checks each section's
"this item needs …" toggle from it. Additive + best-effort.

counterCents.description: Required when action is "counter". Your asking price for the set.

skipped.description:
Cancelled/refunded orders in the request that were left untouched
— reported so a caller can't mistake a partial success for "all
done" and miss that a closed order was in the batch.

platformCancel.description: The marketplace outcome, or already_cancelled when the order was cancelled before this call.

error.description:
The platform's error, VERBATIM. Deliberately not summarised — the
marketplace names what it objected to, and summarising throws that away.
eBay reason codes are now fetched per order via checkCancelEligibility
rather than guessed, but a rejection can still happen (order state changed
between the probe and the cancel), and this is how it gets diagnosed.

cancelledInCrossly.description: Always true — the Crossly-side status flip is unconditional.

platformResult.description: Platform payload (e.g. eBay's cancellationId) when it answered.

accountsStarted.description: Cookie track: number of account slots kicked off. API track: always 1.

alreadyVoided.description: False on a repeat call: the label had already been voided.

refundedCents.description: Credited back to the shipping wallet, in CENTS, markup included.

status.description:
The order's status now: needs_fulfillment for an order that was waiting
on the label; a cancelled order's label is refunded and it stays cancelled.

platformOrderUrl.description: The order on the marketplace, when we can link to it.

CreateOrderLabelVoidResponseTracking.description: What happens to the tracking the marketplace holds.

payoutsSupported.description: False when Stripe offers no way for Crossly to pay this account (see connect.ts).

days.description: null = All time (no limit); 0 = None; a positive integer = days.

source.description:
'override' = the listing's own price for this platform; 'ruled' = a rule
priced it; 'unruled' = the master price as-is; 'refused' = the rule cannot
price it (no FX rate / ≤ 0) and a publish would be refused.

CreatePriceRulePreviewResponse.description: The canonical collection envelope. The array is ALWAYS under `data`, never under the noun — so one accessor works for every list endpoint.

meta.description: Endpoint-specific extras that are NOT pagination — e.g. `pendingCents`, `basis`. Omitted when empty.

packaging.description: Free-text packaging note (kept for back-compat; prefer `box` for detail).

exteriorFinish.description: Exterior finish: matte / soft-touch / gloss / foil-stamped / embossed.

insert.description: Insert: none / foam / tissue / custom_tray / crinkle.

numberedCoa.description: A numbered certificate of authenticity in the box.

extras.description: Stickers, thank-you card, dust bag, etc.

CreateProductionDesignSpecResponsePrefsB.description: Full designer control of the box / presentation.

customHardware.description: Custom hardware / molds (zippers, buckles, outsoles…) — bumps tooling.

minMoq.description: The floor edition size for this category.

actionable.description: The seller can accept or decline it now (false once it is with Crossly).

channels.description: platform → the simulated marketplace's listing id

scale.description:
Uniform scale. Escape hatch for scenery only — stock is never rescaled,

serverTime.description:
The server's clock at the moment this was read.

There is no per-lot deadline to report and this deliberately does not
invent one: the session is AUCTIONEER-driven — a lot closes when a human
hits hammer, not when a timer expires. A countdown rendered from a
fabricated deadline would be a lie the room tells confidently, and the
honest alternative is to hand the client the server's own clock so it can
age "started 4 minutes ago" without trusting the visitor's wall clock.

itemModel.description:
The mesh one item is drawn as. See ItemModel — omit until a model exists,
and the renderer falls back to the photo quad.

itemModelVariants.description:
Other meshes items in this category may be drawn as, chosen PER ITEM.

One model per category is right for a card room, where every object is the
same object. It is wrong for a wardrobe: a rail holds tees and jeans and
jackets, and drawing all of them as a tee would be a worse lie than the
flat quad it replaced, because a wrong SHAPE reads as information.

The renderer picks from `[itemModel, ...itemModelVariants]` using the
item's title — the same heuristic `silhouetteFor` already uses to choose a
garment outline, and for the same reason: the title is the only signal
present on every item, and a wrong guess costs a slightly odd shape rather
than the wrong item. `itemModel` is the fallback when nothing matches.

Deliberately NOT fuzzy-matched against a catalog — this picks a SHAPE, not
an identity. See docs/IDENTIFIER-FIRST.md for where that line sits.

itemModelPool.description:
The shapes an item may be drawn as when its title names NONE — spread
across by a stable hash of the item id, so a wall of untitled pairs is not
forty clones and the same pair is always the same shape. Only shapes that
are a fair guess for ANY item in the category belong here: a runner, a
court shoe and a canvas low, never a clog.

containers.description:

gradedVariant.description:
A SEPARATE profile for graded/sealed copies of the same category.

This is not a flourish. Nobody puts a slabbed card in a binder — it does
not fit and it would be vandalism. Graded cards go on a wall, raw cards go
in pockets, and a space that ignores that is immediately wrong to the only
people who would use it. Same for CGC comics.

thumbUrl.description:
A small copy of `imageUrl`, when the catalog has one.

The room binds this for everything except the few items you are standing
in front of. A 600x600 original costs 1.83 MiB of VRAM; a 150x150 thumb
costs 0.11 MiB, and at more than a couple of metres they are the same
handful of pixels on screen. Null when the catalog never made one, which
the renderer treats as "use the original" rather than as "draw nothing".

because the key becomes a `/models/<key>.glb` path, and a per-item URL can
never be a member of a finite vocabulary.

instead, which for furniture is the difference between a sofa that fits
through the door and one that only looks like it does.

seller who spends an afternoon choosing a colour should be able to
recognise their own door in a directory, and customisation that stops at
the walls of a room nobody has entered yet is customisation nobody sees.

Null when the room has no cosmetics, which is most of them — the door then
keeps its default plaque rather than inventing a colour.

shopfront.description:
How this room's door presents itself in the hall — see SHOPFRONT_STYLES.

Null is "the seller never chose", NOT "bare opening". The hall resolves
null to `SHOPFRONT_DEFAULT`; `'none'` is the explicit bare opening. Those
are different answers and collapsing them here would take away the only
way to ask for a plain door.

shopfrontColour.description:

facade.description:
Which BUILDING this shop stands in — see FACADE_STYLES in shared.

A different axis from `shopfront`: that dresses the doorway, this is the
architecture the doorway is cut into. Both are sent because a seller picks
both, and the street composes this with the size their stake bought.

Null is "never chose", resolved to `FACADE_DEFAULT` by the renderer for
the same reason `shopfront` is not resolved here — a server that filled in
the default would make the stored value unreadable.

occupants.description:
How many people are standing in this room RIGHT NOW.

The single most metaverse-shaped number in this payload: a directory of
rooms is a menu, and a directory that says somebody is already inside one
is a place. `roomOccupancy` has been able to answer this since presence
shipped — nothing asked it.

Live, never stored: it comes from the socket table in `presence.ts`, so it
cannot drift the way a counter column does, and it is 0 for every room on
a process that holds no sockets for it.

closed.description:
The shop is shut — the seller is on vacation.

Sourced from `users.vacation_mode` / `vacation_ends_at` — Settings ›
Vacation mode, the same flag checkout blocks new orders on
(services/vacation/seller-vacation.ts, settings IA audit B3). The old
`seller_profiles.vacation_mode` copy had no writer any client used.

A closed room is still WALKABLE on purpose. Vacation pauses selling, it
does not hide a collection, and a door that refuses to open is a worse
answer than one that opens onto a shop with the shutter down — you can
still look, you just cannot buy.

The cheapest and dearest thing for sale, in cents.

A BAND, deliberately, and never a quote: `listPublicSceneOffers` is the

previewImages.description: Up to PREVIEW_IMAGES item images. Catalog art first, seller photo else.

updatedAt.description: Last time the room itself changed. ISO, or null if the row has no date.

visitorsWeek.description: People who walked it in the last 7 days (spatial_item_attention).

accentColour.description:
The room's accent colour, as a hex string, or null.

Its cove colour — described in `shared/spatial/cosmetics.ts` as the single
most character-defining knob a seller has. Sent so the HALL can use it: a
seller who spends an afternoon choosing a colour should be able to
recognise their own door in a directory, and customisation that stops at
the walls of a room nobody has entered yet is customisation nobody sees.

Null when the room has no cosmetics, which is most of them — the door then
keeps its default plaque rather than inventing a colour.

shopfront.description:
How this room's door presents itself in the hall — see SHOPFRONT_STYLES.

Null is "the seller never chose", NOT "bare opening". The hall resolves
null to `SHOPFRONT_DEFAULT`; `'none'` is the explicit bare opening. Those
are different answers and collapsing them here would take away the only
way to ask for a plain door.

shopfrontColour.description:
The awning's canvas colour as hex, or null. Distinct from accentColour:
the cove lights the inside, this is fabric seen from the street.

facade.description:
Which BUILDING this shop stands in — see FACADE_STYLES in shared.

A different axis from `shopfront`: that dresses the doorway, this is the
architecture the doorway is cut into. Both are sent because a seller picks
both, and the street composes this with the size their stake bought.

Null is "never chose", resolved to `FACADE_DEFAULT` by the renderer for
the same reason `shopfront` is not resolved here — a server that filled in
the default would make the stored value unreadable.

signStyle.description: How the name is lettered (shared shop-decor.ts SIGN_STYLES); null = painted.

signFont.description: The sign's typeface (shared sign-lettering.ts SIGN_FONTS); null = the style's own.

windowMood.description: The street window's lighting preset (shared WINDOW_MOODS); null = none.

occupants.description:
How many people are standing in this room RIGHT NOW.

The single most metaverse-shaped number in this payload: a directory of
rooms is a menu, and a directory that says somebody is already inside one
is a place. `roomOccupancy` has been able to answer this since presence
shipped — nothing asked it.

Live, never stored: it comes from the socket table in `presence.ts`, so it
cannot drift the way a counter column does, and it is 0 for every room on
a process that holds no sockets for it.

closed.description:
The shop is shut — the seller is on vacation.

Sourced from `users.vacation_mode` / `vacation_ends_at` — Settings ›

(services/vacation/seller-vacation.ts, settings IA audit B3). The old

get.summary: The rooms this account has.
get.description: The seller's ONE shop (kind `shop`, every display in one boutique) and their warehouse. Both are created on first read rather than requiring setup, so this call is safe to treat as the entry point. Older per-category rooms may also be listed as kind `collection`; they are no longer created or shown to visitors.

post.summary: Start a 3D room: a collection (your items on shelves) or a warehouse (racks you arrange). Private until you make it public.

get.summary: Public rooms anyone can walk into.
get.description: The directory behind world-hopping. A room becomes public when its owner shares it; this lists those, newest first, with enough to draw a doorway AND enough to choose one — name, slug, category, itemCount, up to four previewImages, forSaleCount, a priceFromCents/priceToCents band and updatedAt. The band is the cheapest and dearest thing for sale in the room, never a quote for one object: /api/public/spatial/{slug}/offers is the authority on that. Fetch the room itself from /api/public/spatial/{slug}. Rooms with no items are omitted: an empty room is not a destination.

get.summary: A shared room, as a visitor sees it.
get.description: The room behind a share link: container geometry in METRES matching the real physical object, the solved arrangement, and one row per object on the shelves. REDACTED relative to the owner's view — no cost, no storage location, no listing status — so do not expect the fields /v1/spatial/scenes/{id} returns. Each placement carries `pinned`: true means a HUMAN put it there and it will not move; false means a layout SOLVER chose, and it may choose differently once the stock changes, so an unpinned placement is never a statement about where something physically is. `solved.overflow` lists what did not fit — a non-empty array means the room is INCOMPLETE and `stats.itemCount` exceeds what is on screen. Resolves rooms shared as `unlisted` as well as `public`: holding the link is the permission.

get.summary: What is for sale in a shared room.
get.description: Price, stock, condition and grade for everything in the room its owner is actually selling. Correlate to the room by `itemId`, which is the SAME id the scene payload publishes per item — never by title. An item in the room with no row here is not for sale; an empty array means the owner is showing the collection rather than selling it, which is a different answer from a 404 (no such shared room). SEPARATE CALL ON PURPOSE: the room's geometry is stable for minutes, a price is not — it changes whenever the seller edits a listing. Re-read this before quoting, and do not cache a price alongside a cached room. `priceCents` is CENTS. `available` is remaining stock, or null when the listing declares none; null is unknown, not zero. Where an item sits inside more than one active listing, the offer quoted is the one for that item alone rather than a bundle it belongs to.

get.summary: A solved room: every item, where it sits, and why.
get.description: Returns the space profile (container geometry in METRES, matching the real physical object), the solved placements, and the items. Placements carry a `pinned` flag: true means a human put it there and the layout solver will not move it; false means the solver chose, and it may choose differently once the stock changes. `overflow` lists anything that did not fit — it is reported, never silently dropped.

get.summary: A warehouse room: your racks, where they stand, and what is on each.
get.description: For a room of kind `warehouse`. Racks are your own storage units (pallet racks, shelving, garment rails, floor totes) with their location `code` (the one written to each item's storage location when stock is placed), a floor position in METRES, and `capacity` / `stocked` / `fill`. `positioned: false` means you never stood the rack anywhere and it was laid out for you. Each rack lists the items on it with the full code of the level or bin they sit in. A non-warehouse room is a 400.

get.summary: Stock movements in a room over a time window.
get.description: One row per physical transition: which item, from which node, to which node, when, and of what kind (placed/moved/picked/shipped/received/removed). Nodes are referenced by id; the `fromCode`/`toCode` strings are display snapshots of the location code AT THE TIME and are not stable identifiers — correlate on the node ids. `since`/`until` are ISO timestamps, defaulting to the last seven days and clamped to 90. Movements are NOT attributed to individual team members on this surface: a token has no team role, so there is no honest way to decide whether its holder may see who did the work.

get.summary: Rooms of yours that are hosting an auction.
get.description: One row per room you OWN that currently has a live-auction session bound into it, with that session's title, status and schedule joined in so you do not have to fetch each one to find out whether anything is running. Empty is the ordinary answer: hosting nothing is the normal state of every room on the platform. This is deliberately not "rooms I could bid in" — that is the public directory at /api/v1/spatial/public, and enumerating every stranger's saleroom here would be a different endpoint wearing this one's name. `topics.auction` is the WebSocket topic the price moves on; `topics.room` is null until the room has been shared.

get.summary: What the rostrum says in this room, right now.
get.description: Serves whoever may ENTER the room, not only its owner — a saleroom restricted to the host would leave every visitor polling a 404 while standing in it. `hosting: false` with a null `auction` is a described empty answer, not an error. READ `currentLot.minimumNextBidCents`, never `currentBidCents + bidIncrementCents`: the first bid on a lot is floored at the START price rather than start + step, so deriving it locally raises the entry price on any lot with a real increment. All amounts are CENTS. `reserveMet` says whether the seller's floor has been cleared; the floor ITSELF is never published, because a crowd that can read it bids to it and stops. `serverTime` is this server's clock, handed over so you can age the session without trusting your own — there is no per-lot deadline to report, because a lot closes when a human drops the hammer and not when a timer expires. A room you may not enter answers 404, the same as one that does not exist.

get.summary: The catalogue: every lot in the session this room is hosting.
get.description: In lot-number order, which is the order the auctioneer reaches them. Each row carries the same fields as the current lot — `minimumNextBidCents` is the figure the bid transaction evaluates against, and every amount is CENTS. A lot with a `hammerAt` has been sold and one with `skipped: true` failed its reserve; neither takes further bids. The reserve AMOUNT is absent by design and `reserveMet` is the only thing said about it. Which lot is UP is not derivable from this list — the auctioneer is the authority and may skip ahead — so take that from the room state endpoint rather than from the lowest open lot number. A room hosting nothing answers an empty list, not a 404: 404 here means the room does not exist or you may not enter it.

get.summary: A shared saleroom, opened by its public share handle.
get.description: The bridge between the public room directory and this auction surface: /api/v1/spatial/public hands out SLUGS, while everything else here is keyed by scene id, and the two are deliberately not interchangeable. Resolves `public` rooms ONLY — an `unlisted` room is a bearer link, and crowd-shaped features stay off in those — so a slug that works on /api/v1/spatial/public/{slug} may still answer 404 here. The reply carries the `sceneId` you then pass to the room state, lots and bid endpoints. Same reading rules as the room state: amounts in CENTS, `minimumNextBidCents` rather than your own arithmetic, no reserve amount.

get.summary: How the shop employee in one of your rooms is configured.
get.description: Owner-only, and 404 for a room this account does not own — the same answer a room that does not exist gives, so this cannot be used to discover scene ids. `config: null` means the room has never had an employee configured, which is different from one that exists and is switched off (`enabled: false`). THE SIGNING SECRET IS NEVER RETURNED, here or anywhere else. It is encrypted at rest and handed back in plaintext exactly once, in the response to the PUT that minted it; `hasAgentSecret` is the only thing any read path will say about it, and re-reading it is impossible by construction rather than by omission. `suspendedAt` non-null means the employee is off the floor because a charge was refused — `suspendedReason` says which — and saving the config again clears it. `brainKind` is idle (stands there), rules (the list in `rules`, evaluated in order, first match wins) or agent (your own endpoint decides).

put.summary: Create or replace the shop employee in one of your rooms.
put.description: A full replace, not a patch: every field is written from this body, so read GET /api/v1/spatial/employee/config first and send it back changed. Owner-only — a room this account does not own answers 404, the same as one that does not exist. `brainKind` is idle (stands there), rules (`rules` evaluated in order, first match wins, max 12) or agent (your endpoint decides, and an endpoint URL is then required). A rule is `{ when, afterSeconds?, do: { act, line?, offerId?, itemId? } }`; `when` and `do.act` must come from the published vocabularies and anything else is a 400. NOTHING IN A RULE CARRIES A PRICE — `do.offerId` is a key into your own offers and the server prices it, so an employee can propose a discount it cannot grant. `displayName` and `do.line` must be printable ASCII: they are drawn in the room from a fixed glyph atlas and anything else renders as a floating box, so they are refused rather than silently rewritten. `agentEndpointUrl` is resolved and validated before it is stored — a public-looking hostname that answers with a private address is refused here rather than accepted and then never called. THE SIGNING SECRET IS RETURNED AT MOST ONCE, in the response that MINTS it: when you pass `rotateSecret: true`, or when you set an agent endpoint on a room that had no secret. Store it then — there is no read path that will ever return it again, and `hasAgentSecret` is all any GET will say. Send an Idempotency-Key if you might retry a rotation: without one, a retried rotate mints a SECOND secret and invalidates the one you just received. Saving anything also CLEARS a suspension — if the employee was paused for want of COSM it is back on the floor, and will be paused again by the next refused charge. Note what this endpoint cannot do: it cannot start a conversation. Engagements are emitted by the room as it is drawn, and they are what costs money.

get.summary: What your shop employees cost over a period, per room.
get.description: One row per room that had at least one conversation in the window; rooms with none are ABSENT rather than reported as zero. `since`/`until` are ISO 8601 and default to the last 30 days, and a window may span at most 366 days — longer is a 400, not a silently shortened period. Money: `billedCents` is COSM cents that were actually charged, and it is the figure to report. `burnBaseUnits` and `poolBaseUnits` are COSM base units as STRINGS because they are 64-bit integers — half the fee is destroyed and half moves to the employee-tax pool. `openConversations` are running right now: measured, not yet billed, and contributing 0 to every money field until they settle, so a total read mid-conversation is a floor rather than a final figure. `unpaidConversations` were settled WITHOUT payment — the seller was short of COSM or COSM is not live on this deployment — and each of those also suspended the employee in that room; they are not a debt and will never be retried. `meta.totals` is the same window summed in the database, not the sum of the rows. `meta.rate` restates the price so a figure can be checked by hand: billing is per STARTED minute, per CUSTOMER, only while somebody is engaged. An employee standing in an empty shop costs nothing.

get.summary: The itemised bill: one row per customer-conversation.
get.description: Newest first, filtered by `since`/`until` (ISO 8601, default 30 days, max 366) and optionally by `sceneId`. `unpaidOnly` narrows to the conversations that settled without payment. This is what makes a usage total checkable by hand: each row carries the interval it was priced from. `engagedMs` is SERVER-measured, from two timestamps this server wrote — no client reports its own duration anywhere in this feature — and it is null, not zero, while the conversation is still running. `settledAt` null with an `endedAt` set means billing has not yet run; `unpaidReason` set means it ran and moved nothing. Base units are STRINGS (64-bit integers). THE CUSTOMER IS NOT NAMED. Billing is per customer, but no row here carries a visitor identity — a bill is an account of what was spent, not a list of who walked in, and publishing the user ids of strangers through a seller API key is a different feature with a different consent question.
