Your Crossly World home: its address, privacy (open / friends / locked), theme, the room, the layout (each piece with what it shows -- things you no longer own are left out at read time) and the guestbook. Made on first read.

Your co-builders: friends you let rearrange your home in the world (move, turn, take out your things, add free furniture; never your bought pieces). Each: userId, name, friends (false once the friendship ended: listed but powerless).
Home of the week: open homes by how many different people signed their guestbook in the last 7 days, most first.
A home by its address, as you may see it: open homes to anybody, friends-only homes to mutual follows, locked homes to their owner. 404 when you may not enter.

Your Crossly World party: party is null when you are in none, else its id, leader and up to 8 members (each with the place and copy they are in right now, or null), plus the invites it has out. invites lists the invites waiting for you.

Your party's shared wishlist, newest first: each listing (title, price in cents, image, shop slug while it is live), who added it, and every member's thumb up or down with the totals. Empty when you are in no party.

Your market-game results, newest first: game (price_guess, price_guess_solo, hunt, speed_trade, break_host), the round/hunt/trade/break id, score, whether you won, Bucks prize in cents (0 while prizes are pins only) and detail. meta.unlocks lists the hunt coupons you earned (with their codes); meta.hits the break hits pulled for spots you bought, with the order each ships with.

Scavenger hunts running now in Crossly World shops and pop-up stalls, ending soonest first: title, shop (name and slug -- for a hunt at a stall, the street slug, with stall.bookingId set), how many tokens, what finishing unlocks ("10% off" -- never the code), when it ends and how many people have finished. Optional place filters to one shop or street slug.

Pack breaks staged on shop stages in Crossly World, live first then soonest: the break, its shop, start time, spots (taken or not, buyer masked), hits revealed so far, and buyUrl -- the break's page on crossly.net, the only place a spot is bought (null once every spot has sold).

Game leaderboards: for each of Price Guess (wins, then points), scavenger hunts (finished) and speed trades (won), the top ten this week (Monday 00:00 UTC on) under week and of all time under all -- rank, name, named, value and, for Price Guess, score. A name appears only for somebody who chose to be seen by name in Crossly World; everyone else is "A player" in their place.

Your Crossly World reputation: four tracks (trader, collector, seller, host) with points, level, what each level has unlocked and the next unlock, and how the points were earned (recency-weighted; a lost dispute or a failed authentication costs points). Earned from real activity only; nothing buys a level.
Somebody's public reputation levels by their storefront handle: the level on each track and their nameplate badge. 404 for an unknown handle.

Open shifts on the Crossly World Jobs board, soonest first: shop staff shifts in boutiques and grading-desk helper shifts, each with its window, place and pay. meta.payOn says whether Crossly is paying jobs yet.

Open price checks appraisers can answer (Collector level 3+ holding 3+ pieces in the category), newest first, optionally one market category. Each has its bounty; meta.payOn says whether bounties are paid yet.

Your Crossly World pets: every kind (cat, dog, slab bot) with whether you own it, when it was earned and the ways to earn it (a quest or a reputation level -- pets are never sold), plus the pet walking beside you and the one greeting visitors at your shop door.

The Crossly World Main Stage right now: the live show (title, kind, host lineup), the stream on its big screen while a lineup host is on air, how many people are there (it holds 64 per copy and opens copies as it fills) and what is on next.
Live and upcoming Main Stage events, soonest first: brand launches, creator meetups, talks, live sales and festival shows, each with its window and host lineup.

Crossly World's pulse, aggregated with no people in it: the public world shops that made a sale today (slugs only -- never counts, amounts or buyers), the times the world's shops passed each sales milestone today (each fires a fireworks show), and what Crossly Cares took in this month against the Commons fountain's mark.
Live and upcoming Crossly World festivals, soonest first: a weekend when every street wears one decor and the festival quest line (limited pins) counts. meta.live is the festival on now, if any.

Find an item on a shelf anywhere in Crossly World: what public rooms have for sale now, by title or catalogue name (q, 2+ characters). Each hit names the room (roomSlug) and the item (itemId); /c/<roomSlug>?item=<itemId> opens it there.
Where a Crossly listing sits on a shelf in a public room right now (roomSlug, roomName, itemId), or data:null when it is in no room.
The cheapest copy of a catalogue piece for sale on Crossly now, matched by the catalogue id (listingSlug, priceCents, and the room and item when it stands on a shelf), or data:null.

Your room's funnel over the last `days` (1-35, default 30): visitors (people, once a day), looks, items opened, checkouts started from the room, paid sales and revenueCents. Sales count only lines the room itself put in a cart.
Items your room shows but does not sell that visitors said they would buy ("I'd buy this"), most wanted first: itemId and how many people.
The people you blocked in Crossly World, as you saw them (label, never the account behind a pseudonym), oldest first. Blocks are made in a room, on the person.

Every balance you hold in Crossly World, read-only: bucksCents (Crossly Bucks, cents); cbx (available, decimals, and the three CBX balances kept apart as base-unit STRINGS -- granted (spend here only), earned (withdrawable once matured), connected (a delegation ceiling on your own wallet, not cash on hand) -- plus pendingCents of cashback not yet matured); cosm (available, decimals, baseUnits string). available:false means that currency is not provisioned on this deployment, not that you hold none.

Every world quest with your progress: key, the pin it earns, goal, target, count, done, colour. meta.wearing is the pin on your nameplate (or null); meta.streak your current and best daily visit streak. Progress only comes from what the server saw -- there is no write of it.

Your crew: data.crew is null when you are in none, else its name, tag, join code and whether you own it; data.members lists up to 30 members, each with the public room they are in right now when they chose to be seen by name (else null).
The game leaderboards (Price Guess, hunts, speed trades; this week and all time) ranked among your crew only, each member by the name the crew sees. 404 when you are in no crew.
Your crew chat: data.messages is the last 50 lines (from, name, text, at), kept in memory only, so it starts empty after a restart. 404 when you are in no crew.

post.summary: Say a line to your crew (body: text, up to 400 characters). Returns data.messages, the crew chat ring (the last 50 lines, kept in memory only), and data.said when your line went out; a blocked or too-quick line is dropped silently. 404 when you are in no crew.

get.summary: What you are wearing: the rig, its slots (avatar_head, avatar_body, avatar_outer -- a jacket over the top, avatar_legs, avatar_feet, avatar_back) and each worn entry -- a cosmetic or a real item -- with its verified-purchase mark. Carries no price, receipt id, seller or order.
What somebody else is wearing, with the verified-purchase mark on each real item -- public on purpose, since a check only its owner can see is not a check. No price, receipt id, seller or order.

Everything you can verifiably wear (your Crossly purchase receipts), newest first: receiptId, item title, brand, size, image, catalog sku/variant, quantity, purchasedAt. Pass a receiptId to POST /v1/world/avatar/equip to put one on. limit 1-200, offset for paging.
Items of your OWN inventory you could wear into a room as a walking storefront: inventoryItemId, title, image and the slot it would go on. Pass an inventoryItemId to POST /v1/world/avatar/equip.

Wearables you have authored as a designer: id, sku, name, slot, priceBaseUnits (COSM base units, a string), maxSupply, mintedCount, active (false until reviewed). meta.available is false when COSM is not provisioned here.

post.summary: Author a wearable for a body slot (a mesh profile and params, an asking price in COSM base units as a string). A submission: inactive until an operator approves it.

get.summary: Your COSM balance: baseUnits (a STRING -- COSM has 6 decimals and overflows a JSON number), decimals, available (false = COSM is not provisioned on this deployment, not a zero balance).

The active cosmetics catalogue, optionally by tier (premium | earned | stake_exclusive) or slot: sku, name, slot, tier, priceCents (premium only), priceBaseUnits (earned only, COSM base units string), supply, fusable, preview and what it unlocks. Read-only: cosmetics are bought on crossly.net. meta.available / meta.decimals.

Cosmetics you hold, newest first: ownershipId, cosmeticId, sku, name, slot, tier, how it was acquired, bound, edition number, acquiredAt and what it unlocks. Pass a cosmeticId to POST /v1/world/avatar/equip to wear one. meta.available.
Your open Trade Block trade listings a trade table can be opened on in the world, each with its items' names.
Your binder: unsold collection rows that are catalog items and may be laid on a trade mat -- key, variantId, condition, grade, portfolioId, name, image and valueCents (market value, cents).

Your friends (mutual follows), each with the PUBLIC room they are in right now when they chose to be seen by name there (else null), and their home address slug when they let friends visit. Invisible and anonymous friends are never located.

What your outfit is worth on the market: cents (sum of each catalogued piece's order-book price -- last sale, else lowest ask), pieces worn, how many were priced, and share (whether you show it on your card).
Your walking storefront, last 7 days: distinct people who tapped "Shop this" or "Offer" on what you wore, and how many of each. Counts only; nobody is identified.
This week's best-dressed board (Monday-based), top ten: name, profile username and loves. Only people still choosing to be seen by name.
The longest current daily visit streaks (2+ days), top ten: name and days. Only people still choosing to be seen by name.
Whether Crossly keeps a world shop for you automatically: enabled, and the shop (id, name, visibility, autoCreated, address, label) or null. Change it with PATCH /v1/world/auto-shop.

patch.summary: Turn your automatic world shop off ({ enabled: false } -- an auto-created shop is made private, never deleted) or back on. Answers the new status.

get.summary: Your saved outfits (up to 6, oldest first): id, name, appearance (skin, hair, hairColour, eyes, build) and items -- each worn thing as the door it goes back on by (slot, door: cosmetic | receipt | stock, id, label). Put one on with POST /v1/world/outfits/:id/apply.

post.summary: Save what you are wearing now as a named look: { name (1-32 chars), appearance? (skin, hair, hairColour, eyes, build -- unknown keys fall back to the default) }. Each worn thing is recorded as the door it goes back on by; one that no longer traces to something you own is listed in skipped and not saved. 409 when you already keep 6.

get.summary: Your Great Hunt: data.season (id, name, startsAt, endsAt, the title and how many earn it, live), started (you read the first clue), held (keys held, 0-3, always in the order copper, jade, crystal), keys (each with its name, colour, its riddle once it is yours to read, and when you picked it up), and cleared (your rank through the Gate this season, when, and whether you earned the title) or null. Keys are picked up by walking to them in Crossly World; nothing here takes one.

The Great Hunt Scoreboard, as the monolith in the Commons shows it: data.season (the running season, or the last one between seasons), finishers (the first ten through the Gate in order: rank, name, short, named, at, titled -- a name shows only for somebody who chose to be seen by name in the world, everyone else is "A player") and total (everybody through the Gate this season).

The Wishing Fountain in the Commons: data.day (today, UTC), today (wishes everyone has made today) and mine (madeToday, days -- how many days you have wished on, the Wishmaker pin comes at 7 -- and nextAt, when tomorrow's wish opens). One wish a day; a wish is made by tossing a coin at the fountain in Crossly World, never over the API, and nothing is spent.

Fireflies on the Commons lawn: data.day (today, UTC), today (fireflies everyone has caught today) and mine (today -- your catches today, up to perDay -- total, all your catches; the Firefly Catcher pin comes at 30 -- and perDay). Fireflies are caught by walking up to a lit one in Crossly World after dark, never over the API, and nothing is spent.

Sky lanterns in the Commons: data.day (today, UTC), today (lanterns everyone has released today) and mine (today -- yours today, up to perDay -- perDay, and days -- the days you have released one on; the Lantern lighter pin comes at 5). Lanterns are released at the lantern stand in Crossly World, never over the API, and nothing is spent.

Kites flown on the Commons lawn: data.day (today, UTC), today (kites everyone has flown today) and mine (today -- yours today, up to perDay -- perDay, and days -- the days you have flown one on; the Kite flyer pin comes at 5). Kites are flown by standing out on the lawn in Crossly World by day, never over the API, and nothing is spent.

The Hall of Grails in Crossly World: data.exhibition (key, title, blurb, endsAt -- a new one every Monday UTC -- and next, the coming one's title) and data.exhibits, up to twelve real catalogue items in slot order (skuId, name, brand, imageUrl, thumbUrl, retailCents, lowestAskCents, lastSaleCents: the live order book, null when the market has none). The first stands on the centre plinth. Buy, bid or watch an exhibit through the market endpoints with its skuId.

The Sales Aurora over the Commons in Crossly World: every real sale on Crossly in the last data.windowDays (30) days. data.total (sales in the window), data.families (key, label, colour, count per colour family: cards, coins, jewellery, electronics, media, fashion, toys, other) and data.sales (newest first, at most 48: family, ageHours, fresh -- sold in the last ten minutes, which shimmers). Aggregate only: no item, price, seller or platform. data.updatedAt is when it was read.

post.summary: Grail glints: send the ids on show somewhere (listingIds -- listings.id, inventoryIds, skuIds -- catalogue market SKUs; up to 400 each) and get back data.listingIds / data.inventoryIds / data.skuIds: the ones that are things you already want -- an open bid, a watched or wishlisted listing (or one selling the same SKU), a market watch, or a card your deck is missing. Read-only.

get.summary: Provenance trails: where in Crossly World your purchases were found, newest first (optionally ?listingIds=a,b -- platform listing ids). data: [{ platformListingId, slug (the listing public slug), kind (room | window | stall | space | drop | auction | worn | agent), place (its name, or null when gone), at, line -- e.g. "Found at The Sneaker Vault, Oct 2026" }]. Yours only.

The Commons chest: data.window (this 20-minute window, UTC), spot ([x, z] on the plaza), endsAt (when the next chest comes) and mine (openedThis, and opened -- how many windows you have opened one in; the Chest opener pin comes at 10). A chest is opened by walking up to it in Crossly World, never over the API.

Your Hoverboard Time Trials bests: data.week (its Monday, YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) and courses, each with course (id, name, parMs, rings, lengthM), week (your best lap this week in ms, your place on the weekly board, laps finished, and the split at each ring) or null, and allTime (your best ever in ms, your place on the all-time board, when) or null. Laps are timed by Crossly from where it saw you ride in the world; nothing here writes one.

A Time Trials course's boards, as the board beside it in the Commons shows them: data.course, week, weekly (this week's ten fastest: rank, name, short, named, ms, at) and allTime (the ten fastest ever, each person once). A name shows only for somebody who chose to be seen by name in the world; everyone else is "A player". 404 for an unknown course; course 1 is commons-loop.

The Arcade in Crossly World: data.cabinets (slot, where it stands, host -- piece, price_guess or empty --, game, title, blurb, the piece it hosts and where, record, packageId and thumbnail for a creator game from the Game Directory, players) and data.scores (the High Score wall: per game a title, kind -- leaderboard, record or top -- and up to five ASCII lines; a name shows only for somebody who chose to be seen by name, everyone else is "A player"), plus creatorGames (creator games with a cabinet now). Games are played in the world.

The Decor Shop: every active cosmetic grouped by surface (avatar | home | shop | stall | street) and slot -- name, tier, priceCents (premium: the dollar price, paid in CBX at spot) or priceBaseUnits (earned: COSM, base-unit string), edition supply and remaining, tint swatch, preview, what it unlocks, owned + your edition number, and buyWith. Read-only: buying and minting happen on crossly.net/shop/decor. meta.available, meta.mint {open, reason}, meta.cbx {open, reason} (CBX opens at mint), meta.balances (your COSM and CBX, base-unit strings), meta.surfaces. Never sold by card.

Decor you hold AND decor you have minted to your wallet, newest first: ownershipId, cosmeticId, sku, name, surface, slot, tier, acquiredVia, bound, editionNumber of maxSupply, mintState (held | minting | minted), mintAddress, mintable, and what it unlocks. meta.available, meta.mint.

Your decor as an INVENTORY. Decor is a quantity: every copy is one unit -- a placed prop (home_prop, prop) uses one per placement, a finish (wallpaper, floor, theme, shopfront, facade, sign style, street lamp/banner/paving/arch, booth canopy/pattern/lights/counter) one per space it dresses; free values are unlimited. Per item: key, value, pair (key:value), name, sku, surface, placeable, tint, owned, placed, available, placements [{ space { kind: home | shop | stall | street, id, name }, count }], copies [{ ownershipId, editionNumber }]. meta.available, meta.spaces (every space you dress). Read-only: placing and retracting happen in the app or on crossly.net.

Interactive objects: every piece that runs a shared script in a room (first-party and approved creator designs). Per item: model (the piece key a home layout or boutique prop stores), decorValue (the home_prop value its SKU claims), source (first_party | creator), name, blurb, size [x, z] metres, fallbackMesh, cosmeticId (the SKU on the Decor Shop, null when not on sale) and version (a creator design: the approved version every copy runs). Read-only: buying is on crossly.net/shop/decor.

Your interactive-object designs (MML documents you wrote), newest first: id, handle, name, footprint (s | m | l | f), tint, priceBaseUnits (COSM, base-unit string), maxSupply, model, decorValue, cosmeticId, liveVersion (the approved version every copy runs; null = none), withdrawnReason, archivedAt (you archived it: off sale, owned copies keep running; null = not archived), latestVersion { version, state: pending | approved | rejected | withdrawn | cancelled, decisionNote }, inReview. `archived`: exclude (default), include or only archived designs. Read-only: writing, previewing, submitting and archiving happen in the Creator Studio on crossly.net (/studio/creator/items/new/interactive).

post.summary: Create an interactive design: name, footprint (s, m, l or f), optional tint and description, an asking price in COSM base units (a string, six decimals) and optional max supply. Inactive until ops approve a submitted version.

get.summary: Browse open on-platform NFT listings (Crossly cosmetics for resale in CBX/SOL).

post.summary: List an NFT you own for resale on the Crossly marketplace.

get.summary: List your verified, linked wallets (EVM and Solana).
List the NFTs in your inventory, imported from your linked wallets.
Open NFT listings in the Crossly book — the cheapest per token.
Collections ranked by 30-day Crossly volume, with floor and listed count.
The Web3 directory's categories and chains, with how many collections each holds.
The NFT home's featured collections: chosen by Crossly, else the hottest.
Browse NFT collections by chain, category and name; sort hot (Crossly sales, listings, favourites), new, volume, floor or name.
Hot NFTs: what is for sale on Crossly first, then tokens from the hottest collections.
The latest NFT sales across the directory, from the chain (Seaport and Blur) and the Crossly book, newest first; page with `before`.
Collections by sales volume over 24h, 7d or 30d, in one coin: the ETH chains together, or Polygon / Solana on their own.
A collection: metadata and Crossly stats (floor, listed, volume, best collection offer).
On-chain insights for a collection: holders, trait counts across the whole collection, recent transfers and a 30-day activity series.
A collection's NFTs: filter by traits (repeat trait=Type:Value; OR within a type, AND across), search by name or token id, sort by id, rarity or Crossly price. Whole-collection once indexed.
Every trait type and value in a collection, with how many tokens have each.
A collection's chain and contract from its readable URL slug (e.g. eth / boredapeyachtclub).
One NFT: metadata, traits, owner, open listings and offers, activity.
Listings, offers, sales and cancels in the Crossly book, newest first.
Your orders in the Crossly book (listings and offers), any status.

post.summary: Place a signed Seaport 1.6 order (listing, offer or collection offer) in the Crossly book.

get.summary: Each marketplace's terms for listing a token: Crossly fee, OpenSea required fees and zone, Tensor availability.
Your collections the OpenSea conduit is approved to move, per linked wallet.
Token ids in a collection with one trait — what a trait offer commits to.
A wallet's public profile: NFTs held, open Crossly listings, and activity.
Find collections by contract address (every chain) or by name.
Find tokens by collection name and number: 'pudgy 42', 'Bored Ape #1234'.
The NFT behind an inventory item: its token, wallet, and open listings on every marketplace (null if it is not an NFT).
A collection's Crossly order book by price level — asks cheapest first, bids dearest first, with running totals — and the floor of every trait value.
Daily floor, sales, volume, holders and listed count for a collection, oldest first (up to 365 days).
Your NFTs with value (Crossly floor, else recent sales) and cost (what a linked wallet paid), realised sales, and USD totals at each day’s coin price.
NFTs your linked wallets bought — on Crossly or any marketplace the chain feed saw — newest first, with price and whether you still hold each.
Your collector perks: how many different NFTs you bought through Crossly, your Collector pin tier, relist rewards paid, and each NFT you still hold with the Bought on Crossly mark.
One calendar year of NFT disposals from your linked wallets as CSV text: acquired, sold, proceeds, cost basis, gain (coin and USD).
Product passports you registered (optionally for one Crossly listing): the code and URL each tag carries.

post.summary: Register a product passport for a Crossly listing you sell, optionally bound to an NFC tag UID (hex). Returns the URL to write to the NFC tag or print as a QR; ownership then follows the item’s paid sales.
Revoke a passport (a lost or misprinted tag). Refused once the item has sold — the passport is then part of its history.

Bind (or re-bind) a passport to the NFC tag you wrote its nfcUrl to: the tag UID (hex), and whether you locked the tag read-only. Refused once the item has sold, for a locked tag, or a tag already on another item.

put.summary: Set a live show’s lineup: your Crossly listings, in the order you will sell them. Buyers see it before they join; a sale of a lineup item while the show is live is recorded at its replay moment.

get.summary: Your show boxes: every buyer’s orders from one live show, to ship together.

post.summary: Buy ONE label for a show box, rated for all its orders packed together; every order takes its tracking and the buyer’s extra postage is refunded.
Ship a show box with your own label: every order is marked shipped with this tracking and the buyer’s extra postage is refunded.

get.summary: Your active story slides (newest run first, each run in play order), with their overlays: text, listing stickers, @mentions, links, emoji and drawing.

post.summary: Share a story: 1–10 slides played in order. Each slide is a photo or video plus optional overlays (positions are fractions of the 9:16 frame). Listing stickers must be your own Crossly listings and also tag the slide; @mentions must be real shops. audience: everyone | followers; expiresInHours: 6, 12, 24 or 48.

delete.summary: Take one story slide down before it expires.

get.summary: Your live shows, newest scheduled first: status, cover, category, connection method and peak viewers.

post.summary: Schedule a live show: title, start time, optional cover, category and the listings to feature (becomes the lineup, in order).

patch.summary: Edit a show that has not ended: title, description, cover, category, start time (not once live) or connection method (browser | phone | encoder).

post.summary: The show’s video connection, minted on first call and identical after: RTMP(S) server + stream key, SRT URL, WHIP URL for browser publishing (null where the ingest has none) and the HLS playback URL. configured=false (with a reason) when the deployment has no streaming provider.
Replace the show’s stream key (e.g. after it was shown on screen). Refused while the show is live.
Go live: the show’s status becomes live and followers are notified once. Idempotent while live; refused once ended.
End the show. Idempotent.

get.summary: The show’s numbers: duration, peak viewers, items sold and gross, tips, chat messages, auctions run, lineup size and the replay URL.

put.summary: Tag your listings at points on a story or lookbook photo (shop the look). Replaces that photo’s tags; at most 12.

get.summary: Your loyalty club: tiers and how many members are in each.

put.summary: Create or update your loyalty club: name, on/off, and up to 6 spend tiers each with a discount (≤ 30%) and perks.

get.summary: Your loyalty club’s members, by spend with you.

Selling options: own-price match (Crossly sells your items at your own lower price for the same item on another marketplace; dollar-priced copies only) and layaway (buyers may put items on layaway). Both on by default.

put.summary: Turn own-price match and/or layaway on or off for every one of your stores. One store: PUT /v1/storefronts/{id}/settings.

get.summary: Buyers asking for a video of your items. status: open (default), answered, declined or all.

post.summary: A presigned upload for a video answer: PUT the file to uploadUrl with the same Content-Type and exact Content-Length, then answer with publicUrl.
Answer a video request with a clip you uploaded (POST /v1/video-requests/upload-url, then PUT the file to uploadUrl). The buyer is notified and the clip shows on the listing.
Decline a video request, with an optional note to the buyer.

get.summary: Your items on layaway (active and paid off). Do not ship an active one: its order moves to needs_fulfillment when paid in full.
Rentals of your items, with the ship-to and the outbound label.
What you offer for rent.

put.summary: Offer a Crossly listing for rent: day rate, optional week rate, deposit, min/max days, turnaround buffer, rent-only (off sale while offered), seller approval, unavailable date ranges (blackoutRanges, inclusive YYYY-MM-DD) and a return policy. Keeps the listing’s own rental terms in step. Needs a ship-from address.

delete.summary: Stop offering a listing for rent (existing bookings stand).

post.summary: Buy both labels for a booked rental: outbound to the renter, and the return label they use.
Mark a booked rental shipped, with at least 2 photos of its condition as it leaves (URLs you uploaded) — the evidence any later claim is judged against.
Approve a requested rental (offers with requireApproval): the renter’s held card is charged.
Decline a requested rental: the hold on the renter’s card is released.
Mark a rental back with you. You then have 3 days to claim damage before the deposit goes back.
Cancel a booked rental that has not shipped: the renter is refunded in full.
Claim part or all of the deposit (cents, a note, photo URLs): within 3 days of the return, or 14 days after the end if it never came back.

get.summary: Your Sponsored Listings campaigns with status, pacing (spent today, daily cap reached), budgets, bids, placements and stats for the range (from/to, YYYY-MM-DD; default last 30 days).

post.summary: Create a Sponsored Listings campaign: name, dailyBudgetCents (≥100), optional totalBudgetCents, defaultBidCents (5–10000; the max bid under bidStrategy "auto"), placements (search, browse, product_page, home_rail), optional startsAt/endsAt, listings [{platformListingId, bidCents?}], keywords [{keyword, matchType broad|phrase|exact, negative?, bidCents?}], status active|draft. Clicks are charged from your CBX balance (granted first, then earned); with none it waits as out_of_budget.

get.summary: One campaign: settings, its listings (bid, suggested bid, live, per-listing stats) and keywords.

patch.summary: Edit a campaign. Any of the create fields; listings and keywords, when given, replace the current set. Raising the total budget resumes a campaign stopped by it.

post.summary: Set a campaign active (launch/resume), paused, or ended (final). Resuming with no CBX to pay for clicks leaves it out_of_budget until you top up.
Copy a campaign (settings, listings, keywords) as a new draft.

get.summary: Sponsored Listings report for a range: totals (spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, average CPC, attributed orders and revenue, ROAS), a zero-filled daily series and per-campaign rows. Orders are Crossly purchases of the advertised listing within 7 days of a click by the same buyer.

post.summary: Confirm a sent deploy transaction: the contract must be the Crossly launch contract with this draft’s settings; it then goes live.

delete.summary: Delete a launch draft that never went live. Returns `{ ok }`.

patch.summary: Edit a launch draft (or a failed deploy) before it deploys: any creation field except chain and owner. The schedule is re-checked; 409 once live.

get.summary: Your holder perks: percent off your Crossly shop for holders of an NFT collection, best first.

put.summary: Set the percent off (100–5000 bps) holders of a collection get across your Crossly shop; one perk per collection.

delete.summary: Remove a holder perk. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: Collections you are the creator of: your launches, and contracts you claimed by owning them.

post.summary: Claim an EVM collection as its creator: its owner() must be one of your verified wallets. Returns `{ chain, contract }`.

get.summary: A collection’s creator dashboard: sales by marketplace and day, estimated royalties, holders, and for a launch the mint revenue and what is waiting to be withdrawn (wei of the chain’s native currency).
Every CBX you have, in one read, with the three balances kept apart.
get.description: `credit`: EARNED (withdrawable once matured; `withdrawableBaseUnits` is earned minus anything staked) and GRANTED (in-platform spend only, never withdrawable). `connected`: headroom on your connected-wallet delegation, a ceiling on what Crossly may pull, never a balance. `wallets`: each linked wallet with its own on-chain CBX (`status` read / not_solana / not_live / unavailable). `totals.allBaseUnits` is credit + wallets and never adds the delegation headroom. Amounts are base-unit strings (`decimals`).

get.summary: Your CBX stake: what is locked, its tier, the tier ladder and your past positions.
get.description: A stake locks EARNED CBX; it moves nothing and pays no yield. Each tier buys a withdrawal-fee discount and an earn-rate boost on future purchases, and has a cooldown before an unstake releases.

post.summary: Lock earned CBX (`baseUnits`, a string) into the best tier it reaches. 409 while a stake or unstake is in progress.
Start unstaking: the earn boost stops now, the tokens release when the tier’s cooldown ends. Returns `{ unlocksAt, cooldownDays }`.

get.summary: What a linked wallet holds right now, each NFT marked `inInventory` or not. Reads the chain; writes nothing.

post.summary: Add picked NFTs (`tokens`: chain, contract, tokenId; up to 200) from a linked wallet to inventory. Tokens the wallet does not hold are counted in `notInWallet`, never added.

get.summary: A launch’s phase timeline, mint progress, proceeds (gross, Crossly’s cut, yours; airdrops excluded), allowlist and art counts, and recent mints.
A launch’s creator tools: allowlist size and root (and whether the contract has it yet), uploaded art and reveal, supply minted.

put.summary: Replace the early-phase allowlist (up to 10,000 wallets). EVM live launches get back `rootTx`, the setAllowlistRoot transaction for the owner wallet.

get.summary: The setAllowlistRoot transaction for the allowlist Crossly holds (EVM, live): `{ chain, from, to, data }`.

post.summary: Append per-token art (image URL, name, traits), up to the supply, before the reveal. Returns `{ count }`.
Reveal the art: one random offset maps every token to its asset for good. Returns `{ revealedAt }`.
Plan an airdrop (one free NFT each, up to 500) to `addresses` and/or the holders of `holdersOf`. Returns the transactions for the owner wallet; no payment moves.

get.summary: A Solana collection’s Tensor bids (collection-wide and by trait), best first; price in lamports. Needs your Tensor key.

post.summary: Build a Tensor collection bid (or trait bid with `trait`) for your Solana wallet to sign. Price in lamports.
Build the transaction that sells your NFT into a Tensor bid, never below `minLamports`.
Build the transaction that cancels your Tensor bid.

put.summary: Make your Space holders-only: only holders of an NFT collection join it (others can look in). Send null to open it again. Returns `{ gate }`.
Make your room holders-only (its collection rooms follow). Send null to open it again. Returns `{ gate }`.

get.summary: The NFT you wear on your nameplate in the world, or null.

put.summary: Wear an NFT you hold on your nameplate (null to take it off). Checked again each time you join a room.

post.summary: Pin one of your live NFT launches on your live show; viewers mint it from the stream. Returns `{ ok }`.

delete.summary: Unpin the launch from your live show. Returns `{ ok }`.

post.summary: Follow the creator of a launch: their launches are announced to you, and again when each opens. Returns `{ following }`.

delete.summary: Stop following the creator of a launch. Returns `{ following }`.

get.summary: A book key's depth (20 levels a side), last 50 trades, 24 h stats, mark and any halt, in one call.
The L2 depth ladder: price levels and units per side, best first; asks show how many units are authenticated vault stock.
The latest trades on a book key, newest first, with which side made and which took.
24 h open, high, low, last, volume and change on a book key.
OHLCV candles (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d) from the trades on a book key.
A long-lived text/event-stream for a book key: `snapshot` first, then `depth`, `trades`, `mark` and `halt` events as they change.

schema.description: Server-sent events; each `data:` line is one JSON object.

post.summary: Place an order on a vault book: limit, market (protected, IOC), stop or stop-limit; GTC, GTD, IOC or FOK; post-only; an iceberg `displayQuantity`; a TWAP or VWAP algo over a window. Idempotent on `clientOrderId`. `subaccountId` trades for a firm sub-account you may trade (your role, its KYB, its limits, no firm halt; buys pay from its custodian account and land in it).

get.summary: Your orders: open (default) or done, optionally on one book key, or only those booked to one sub-account (`subaccountId`).
One order with its full event log.

post.summary: Cancel an order; what filled stays filled.
Amend an order's price, stop or quantity (cancel-replace: it re-queues at its new price).
Cancel every open order, or every one on a book key. Returns `{ cancelled }`.

get.summary: Your order event log after a sequence number (new, leg, fill, replaced, cancelled, expired, done): a replayable drop copy.

post.summary: Market makers: set a two-sided post-only quote on a book key (replaces the last). With cancel-on-disconnect (default) heartbeat every 30 s or it is pulled.

get.summary: Your live quotes.

delete.summary: Pull your quote on a book key, or every quote. Returns `{ pulled }`.

post.summary: Keep your quotes alive (cancel-on-disconnect). Returns `{ quotes, at }`.

get.summary: Your daily market-maker liquidity rewards (paid in CBX).

post.summary: Give a unit in your vault to another Crossly user (by @username or email). It stays on its shelf; they have 7 days to accept. ID needed above $1,000 at the mark. Returns `{ id, expiresAt }`.

get.summary: Gifts you sent and received, newest first, with their status.

post.summary: Accept a gift: the unit becomes yours in place. Returns `{ status }`.
Decline a gift: the unit stays with the giver. Returns `{ status }`.
Cancel a gift you sent before it is accepted. Returns `{ status }`.
Give a unit to Crossly Cares (once the charity can receive; otherwise its gate message). Returns `{ id, markCents }`.

get.summary: Your tax year on the vault markets: units bought and sold with cost, proceeds, gain and term; lending fees, staking interest (estimate), market-maker rewards; closed positions. Links to the CSV and PDF.
The tax year as a CSV: one row per sale, purchase, gift, income line and closed position.

schema.description: CSV text with a header row.

get.summary: The tax year as a PDF summary.
Open vault auction events (weekly, ending Sunday; premier, units marked $10,000+) and their lots, soonest ending first.
Lots you consigned (with your reserve) and lots you bid on (with your maximum and whether you lead).
One lot: the price showing, the next minimum bid, whether a reserve exists and is met, the end (extended by late bids), the bid history and your standing.

post.summary: Consign a stored, authenticated unit to the next weekly or premier event, with an optional opening price and reserve. The unit is held until the close. Returns `{ lotId, eventId, endsAt }`.
Withdraw your lot before any bid; the unit goes back on your shelf. Returns `{ ok }`.

Leave or raise your maximum on a lot; the system bids for you up to it. A bid in the last 2 minutes extends the lot by 2 minutes. The winner's saved card is charged at the close through the order book. ID needed above $10,000.
Feature an open lot on your live show (or `lotId: null` to take it off). Viewers hear LIVE_PIN_CHANGED. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: The market around a vault unit: its mark and source, the best bid that could take it, the Instant Exit price (the best bid) and a pack pull's own sell-back credit.

post.summary: Sell one unit of this item now into the best bid (Instant Exit: an immediate-or-cancel pro order), never below `minCents`. Returns `{ status: filled | missed, filledCents, quote, order }`.

get.summary: Your vault loans and advances (live by default): what is owed, interest accrued, loan-to-value, the liquidation line and the collateral value it is called at.
One loan or advance with its pledged units and its money log (draws, interest, repayments, sale proceeds).

post.summary: Repay from your custodian account, interest first. Omit `amountCents` to repay everything; pass `requestId` to make a retry safe. Repaid in full, the items are free.

get.summary: How much you can borrow against vault units (`vaultItemIds`, comma-separated; none = every stored unit you hold): each unit's tier, mark and limit, the pool's rate and yours.

post.summary: Borrow against stored vault units: they are pledged (no listing, lending or withdrawal) and the market pool lends `amountCents` into your custodian account. Needs a verified ID.

get.summary: Units you lent: rate, fees earned, recall due.

post.summary: Pledge more stored units to a loan (answers a loan call, or makes room).
Free one pledged unit, if what is owed still fits inside the other units' limit.

get.summary: The lowest price a pledged unit can be sold at to repay its loan: after the sale (less the vault fee and storage) what is still owed must fit inside the other units' limit.

post.summary: Sell a pledged unit to repay its loan: it is listed at `priceCents` (at least the sale floor) and stays pledged until it sells; the proceeds repay the loan first and the rest is yours. Calling it again re-prices it.

get.summary: What an advance on a vault unit for sale could be: up to half of the lower of its mark and asking price, free for 60 days.

post.summary: Take an advance against a vault unit that is listed for sale: paid into your custodian account, netted from the sale. Free for 60 days, then the pool rate. Needs a verified ID.
Relist an advance's unit at a new price (never so low its sale could not repay the advance).

get.summary: Indexes over book keys: per category, per top brand, the Crossly 50 and your own. Each with its level now (base 1000 at inception) and change since the last daily close.

post.summary: Make an index of your own: 1 to 50 book keys, weighted by mark or equally. Up to 10 per account.

get.summary: The built-in indexes that moved most since their last daily close.
One index with its daily closes (oldest first) and its level now.

patch.summary: Rename, re-weight, share or change the keys of an index of your own; its level carries on.

delete.summary: Delete an index of your own. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: The book keys in an index with their weight, move since the last close and contribution to the index's move (basis points).

post.summary: Buy the basket: one limit buy per key in the index for 1-5 whole units each, at most `maxBpsOverMark` over each key's mark, IOC or GTC. Every unit is a real item that lands in your vault. Idempotent on `clientBasketId`; returns a result per key.

get.summary: Your watched book keys with mark, 24 h and 7 d change, and the last 30 daily marks (sparkline).

post.summary: Watch a book key. Returns `{ bookKey, watching }`.

delete.summary: Stop watching a book key (`?bookKey=`). Returns `{ bookKey, watching }`.

get.summary: Up to 5 book keys and/or index slugs (`items`, comma-separated) as daily series on the same days, each rebased to 100.
Your Vault Markets value by day at the marks (vault units, units on loan, positions) and today's return against yesterday's close.

For a raw book key: the marks of the same item's graded keys, the spread over raw, grading cost per grader, the margin tier grading lifts it to, your raw vault units it pays to grade, and where to act.
A book key's units in the vault and authentications passed, by day (oldest first, today live).
The Instant Exit quote for one vault unit you hold: the best resting bid on its book key (anyone's, dealers' included), its share of the mark, the bid depth, and whether it can be taken now.

post.summary: Sell a unit now at the quoted price: a sell IOC at `priceCents` through the pro engine. Refused, with the new quote, if the best bid dropped below it. Crossly never buys or funds it.

get.summary: Instant Exit quotes for everything you hold in the vault, one per book key, with units held and which are free to sell.
Your Instant Exits, newest first: quoted price, mark, and whether it filled.
The offers inbox: for each book key you hold, the best bid from someone else, units at it, the top bid levels, the mark, and your alert.

put.summary: Set (or clear with null) the bid price that should always notify you on a key you hold, and mute or unmute offer notices on it.

get.summary: Your recurring buys: key, schedule, price cap, payment, auto-lend, next run.

post.summary: Start a recurring buy: one whole unit of a key every week, two weeks or month, at no more than `maxPriceCents` and/or the mark plus `capBpsOverMark`; card (with an optional backup) or custodian; optional auto-lend.

patch.summary: Change a recurring buy's schedule, caps, cards or auto-lend, or pause / resume it.

delete.summary: Stop a recurring buy for good; its history stays.

get.summary: One recurring buy's runs: filled, skipped (with the reason, e.g. the price was over the cap) or failed.
Every run of all your recurring buys, newest first.

post.summary: A buy order with a take-profit and/or stop-loss attached; the exits arm as an OCO pair for what the entry fills.
Two orders on one key, one cancels the other: when one fills or its stop triggers, the other is cancelled (a partial fill shrinks it).
A trailing stop: its stop follows the best price since it was placed, `trailBps` or `trailCents` behind (under the high for a sell, over the low for a buy).

get.summary: Your linked orders (brackets, OCO pairs, trailing stops, position exits): live (default) or done.

post.summary: Cancel a linked order: its open child orders come off; a bracket's entry stays.

get.summary: A position's take-profit / stop-loss, if set.

put.summary: Set a position's take-profit / stop-loss: a long is closed, a short covered, when the last trade reaches one. Both null clears them.

get.summary: For each live position: its tier, health, margin state, the mark at which it is called and the mark at which it is liquidated, and the distance to it.
One position's call and liquidation marks.
Daily borrow APR (lent units) and pool APR on a book key, with the pool as a whole, oldest first.
Your dealer status (applied, approved, revoked) and your Instant Exit bands.

post.summary: Apply to be a dealer (ID check first). Ops review; approved dealers get raised limits and their bids show as dealer bids.

get.summary: Your standing dealer bids: open (default) or all.

post.summary: Place a standing dealer bid: a resting GTC/GTD limit buy, flagged as a dealer bid. Approved dealers only.

get.summary: Your Instant Exit bands and whether each is being kept now.

put.summary: Commit to an Instant Exit band on a key: a standing bid for `units` kept at `bandBps` of the mark, never above `maxPriceCents`, re-quoted as the mark moves.

delete.summary: Stop a band on a key; its standing bid comes off.

get.summary: Your vault units sent to grading: where each card is in its run, and the grade once it is back.

post.summary: Send a raw vault unit on the grading hub's shelf to a Grading Run (`runId`). It is held until it comes back, graded, to the same vault item. The slot is free; your saved card is charged only if the run locks.
Pull a vault unit out of its run before the run locks (nothing was charged). It goes back on the shelf.

get.summary: Your Vault Markets channel switches: Telegram alerts and digest, the daily cap on vault nudges by push (default 5), whether a Telegram chat is linked, and how many nudges went out today.

put.summary: Change the switches: `telegramAlerts`, `telegramDigest`, `pushCapPerDay` (0 to 20). Margin calls and recalls are never capped. Returns the new view.

get.summary: This week's vault digest as it would go out: units at the display marks (unmarked units counted, not valued), the like-for-like change from a week ago, offers on your units, watched keys that got a first mark, and one Learn card.
Past weekly digests: week, status (sent / skipped / failed), the channels used and a summary.

A catalogue item's vault book keys (`?skuId=`, optional `variantId`): each key's display mark with quality and n, units in the vault, the Instant Exit price a holder would get now, and whether it can be shipped in (ungraded keys).
Your collection valued at the display marks: rows on a vault book key with a mark are summed; rows with no mark or no key are counted, never valued.

post.summary: Watch every collection item that sits on a vault book key (up to the watchlist cap). Returns `{ watched, skipped }`.

Open a ship-in deposit for an ungraded catalogue item (`skuId`, `variantId`, `condition` DS / VNDS / Used). It is inbound until the vault receives and checks it, then stored in your name. Returns `{ vaultItem: { id, status } }`.

Send inventory items matched to a catalogue variant to the vault as one box: each becomes an inbound vault unit, and the box gets one prepaid inbound label (a PDF to print). Optional: auto-list each unit in the vault book at a share of the mark once stored, and lend when idle. Items that cannot go say why. Crosslisted listings stay live.

get.summary: Your units sent to the vault, newest first, each with its state and its key's Instant Exit line ("Instant Exit now: $X (N% of mark)" or "No market yet"). Filter with `inventoryItemIds` (comma-separated).

patch.summary: Change a deposit's toggles: `autoListBps` (list at that share of the mark once stored; null = do not) and `lendWhenIdle`.

get.summary: A box sent to the vault: its prepaid label and tracking, or why it has no label.

post.summary: Buy a box's prepaid label again after it failed (for example once a ship-from address is saved). A box that has a label keeps it.

get.summary: Everything you own in the Crossly vault, newest activity first: each unit with its status (inbound, stored, listed, withdraw_requested…) and situation (lent, pledged, in_grading…), what it is worth (`valueCents` with `valueSource` mark | last_sale | declared | none), declared and insured value, storage owed, its open ask, the deposit toggles when you sent it in, and what you may do with it now (`actions`). Units sold or shipped home in the last 90 days have `past: true`. `meta` carries the totals (units, value, declared, insured, storage owed), your recent boxes and their labels, the ship-home prices and the lending gate.

What shipping one unit you own home would charge now, for `standard` and `expedited`: shipping, the storage it owes and the early-withdrawal fee (within 90 days of arriving), and the total. Read-only; ship it home with POST /api/v1/buyer/vault/:id/withdraw.
Your seller round-up: the share of each payout that sets a vault buy's budget, the budget so far and what it is doing. `roundUp` is null when none is set.

put.summary: Set the round-up: `shareBps` (1%-50%) of each payout released to you adds to a budget; when it covers the cheapest vault unit on `bookKey`, one unit is bought with your saved card, never above the budget.

delete.summary: Stop the round-up (its history stays; an armed buy is cancelled).

get.summary: Market Open invites to you as a dealer: keys Crossly is opening and asks you to quote.

post.summary: Accept or decline a Market Open invite (`accept`).

get.summary: Keys opening soon on the vault book (and just opened): units on the shelf, dealers quoting, the waitlist, the mark when the book has one, and your place.
One opening key.

post.summary: Join a key's waitlist, optionally with a friend's invite code (`ref`). Inviting moves you up the queue; nobody is paid. Returns your place and your own code.

delete.summary: Leave a key's waitlist.

get.summary: Your Vault Drop-off Partnership (null when you never applied): status, partner code, fee share and cap, totals and batches.

post.summary: Apply as a Vault Drop-off Partner (a card shop that takes walk-ins for the vault). Needs the one-time ID check; ops approve.

An approved partner sends walk-ins in under its code: each item (catalogue variant, condition, grade, photos) becomes an inbound vault unit; the box gets one prepaid label. The partner earns a capped share of Crossly's fee on each unit's first sale.

get.summary: Your partner fee shares, newest first: accrued on a unit's first sale, paid in Bucks once the sale is final, void if it was refunded.
Your share cards (not taken down), each as the public sees it.

post.summary: Make a verified share card of a position, a vault unit, a public index or your portfolio (`kind`, `refId`). The % on it is the price move since your real fill; amounts stay hidden unless `showAmounts`.

get.summary: One share card as the public sees it, with its image and link paths.

patch.summary: Show or hide the dollar amounts on one of your share cards (`showAmounts`).

delete.summary: Take a share card down: its link and image stop working. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: Your public vault profile switch: on or off, whether followers see new buys, your profile URL and follower count.

put.summary: Turn your public vault profile on or off (`isPublic`) and whether followers see your new buys (`showBuys`). It shows weights by market, never dollars.

get.summary: Someone's public vault: each market's weight (bps of the marked value), followers, whether you follow, their recent buys (no prices).

post.summary: Follow someone with a public vault: their new vault buys appear in your feed. No copy trading.

delete.summary: Stop following someone.

get.summary: New vault buys by the people you follow who share them, newest first (no prices). Page with `before` (the last item's `at`).
The Learn hub: each concept with whether you passed its quiz. Passing earns cosmetic pins only.
One Learn concept: its sections and quiz questions (no answers).

post.summary: Answer a concept's quiz (`answers`: the chosen choice index per question). Graded on the server; 5 tries an hour.

get.summary: The quarterly Crossly Vault Report (`quarter` like 2026-q3; default the latest): index levels, top movers, most-lent markets, grade premiums. Book data only.
The press kit: each built-in index with level, quality, n, CSV link and a "cite as" line, plus the methodology links.
An index's daily closes (up to 5 years), oldest first.
What the <crossly-index> widget shows: level, closes, quality, n, as-of, or `insufficient`.
What the <crossly-mark> widget shows for `bookKey`: mark, quality, trades over 30 days, as-of, sparkline, or `insufficient`.
Everything derived about one book key in one read: the Crossly Estimate, the liquidity score, risk statistics and the gem rate. A part that cannot be read is `{ error }`.

The Crossly Estimate for a book key — a model, not a price. Method (own trades, index-adjusted last trade, grade ratio), cents with 68% and 95% bands, High/Medium/Low from the walk-forward backtest's FSD, and n. Hidden (`available: false`) under 50 backtested trades or when FSD > 0.30. Never used for margin, loans or settlement.
The Crossly Estimate's track record: walk-forward backtest n, FSD and bias per method, category and liquidity bucket, and whether estimates in that cell are shown.

The liquidity score (0-100) of a book key and every component behind it: trades in 30/90 days, distinct counterparties, median days between trades, time-weighted quoted spread, two-sided share and depth within 5% (hourly book snapshots), Amihud and Roll. Each component is a percentile within the category. No score under the data threshold.

Risk statistics for a book key (weekly returns from A-quality marks only) or an index slug (its closes): annualised volatility raw and Geltner-desmoothed (labelled), max drawdown and beta to the Composite. Needs 26 weekly returns, else no numbers.
The correlation matrix of the sector indexes' weekly returns over `weeks` (default 52), pairwise-complete, with n per pair; a pair under 26 shared weeks has no number.

The Crossly gem rate: of cards graded through Crossly, the share that came back at each grader's gem grade, for this item and its category, with a Wilson 95% band. 10 returns per grader or no number. Not a grader population report.

How a book key trades: its liquidity tier (A continuous, B call auction every 15 minutes, C daily call, D listings only), the call collecting now with its indicative price and volume and nominal close, the next call, the LULD band and any limit state, pause or halt.
Recent call-auction uncrosses on a book key: kind (open, reopen, periodic, daily, buy-in, sell-off), clearing price in cents and units.

The index method in machine-readable form: version (semver), inputs, weightings and caps, the family and its screens, the engines and their publication gate, revisions and the settlement series, the calendar, governance and limitations.

The next four quarterly reviews: reference day (2nd Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec), announcement day, last close under the old membership and the effective day; June and December also review the Blue-chip 50.
Every index event, newest first: add, delete, rebalance, method, correction, halt; each with when it was announced, when it takes effect, the detail and the reason. Filter by `kind`.
The expert-judgment log: every Index Committee action (halt, resume, exclude a key, void a trade, restate, retire) with its written reason.
One index's events, newest first.

An index's published levels. `engine=chain` (default): daily closes. `engine=tpd|repeat_sales`: weekly (else monthly) model estimates with a 95% band and n; labelled, never a price. `series=settlement` returns each value as first published (never restated). Below the data gate `data` is empty and `notice` explains.

The members of an index on a day (`asOf`, default today) with their weights, shares, moves and contributions; for a past day, the inputs stored with that day's close and each member's effective dates.
Published Index Committee minutes, newest first: attendees (names and roles), quorum, agenda, minutes and decisions.
Consultations on index method changes (open for at least 30 days), newest first. Filter by `status`.
One consultation with its proposal, versions, dates, outcome and the public comments.

post.summary: Comment on an open consultation (5 to 5,000 characters; up to 5 per person). Comments are published without your name. Returns `{ ok }`.
File a complaint about an index or the method (`slug` optional). Every complaint is answered. Returns `{ id, status, createdAt }`.

get.summary: Your complaints and their answers, newest first.

The published unit list (bar-list equivalent): every unit on a vault shelf with its warehouse receipt number (when receipts are registered), book key, shelf location code, insured value, status, pledged / on-loan flags and a per-receipt hashed holder (never a name or id). Filter with `bookKey`; pages with `page` / `limit`.
Your warehouse receipts (documents of title for your vault units), live first. meta.receipts says whether receipts are registered (VAULT_WAREHOUSE_ISSUER) and their terms version.
One of your receipts with its full hash chain (issued, transferred, pledged, released, surrendered), re-verified on read: `chain.ok` is false if any event was altered.

Vault attestations: independent physical counts, the insurance certificate (with a warning when insured value in the vault exceeds its aggregate or per-occurrence limit), SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 reports. Each carries its signed document.

Proof of reserves: the latest daily Merkle root over every unit in custody (leaf count, stored / listed / grading / withdrawing, pledged, on loan, open loans, receipts, insured value), its Solana memo anchor when VAULT_POR_ANCHOR_KEY is set, the last `days` roots, and the exact hashing method.

Your inclusion proofs for a day (latest by default): each of your units' leaf fields, salt, owner commitment, leaf hash and sibling path. Verify with your OWN user id: commitment = SHA-256(JSON["crossly-por-owner-v1", userId, salt]); then the leaf; then climb the path to the published root.
One day's proof-of-reserves snapshot (root, counts, anchor).
One day's leaf hashes in tree order, a page at a time: enough to recount the units and rebuild the root yourself. Leaves are salted, so they name no owner.

A locate quote: how many units of `key` (a book key) you could borrow now (up to `qty`), the indicative rate (APR bps; `termDays` 30 or 90 for a fixed-rate term loan), and the collateral they need (150%, or 175% for units whose lenders elected return in kind only). Holds nothing; POST to hold.

post.summary: Hold up to `qty` lendable units of `bookKey` for 15 minutes so a short can open against them (`termDays` 30/90 for a term loan). Needs lending (VAULT_LENDING_TERMS_VERSION) and the ID check. Returns the locate with how many units it holds.

get.summary: Your locates, newest first (held / used / released / expired).

delete.summary: Release a live locate before it lapses.

get.summary: Your lender election: `returnInKind` (shorts post 175% collateral, a 14-day buy-in, never cash-settled) and `allowTerm` (your units may go out on 30/90-day fixed-rate term loans, not recallable before term).

put.summary: Change your lender election (applies to loans opened after the change). Needs lending.

get.summary: Your daily collateral statement as a lender (today live, or `day`): per open loan the mark and its quality, fees owed to you, the short's collateral share at the custodian and its coverage against 105% of mark + fees. A unit without a mark usable for risk shows no coverage number.
The days you have stored collateral statements for, newest first, with their summary.
Your lender programme report: lendable units, units out, utilisation, fee revenue (accrued / paid), term loans and return-in-kind loans in force, and each loan's rate against the key's rate today.

The licensed index feed for one built-in index (needs VAULT_INDEX_DCM + VAULT_INDEX_FEED_SECRET): the level now (intraday from A/B marks, or the last close below 50% constituent coverage), the last close, the frozen 7-day TWAP settlement value and every constituent with its mark source, quality and trade count. Signed: `x-crossly-signature: t=<ms>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, t + "." + body)>`. Every read is logged for the licence. Crossly is the licensor and data feed only.
The frozen 7-day TWAP settlement series for a licensed index (written once a day, never restated), with the closes behind each value. Signed like the feed.

Reference funding for a perpetual-style future on the index: your premium `premiumBps` (TWAP of (impact mid - index)/index) through F = P + clamp(I - P, ±0.05%) per 8 h, |F| capped at 0.5%/day, with the index level it is relative to. The partner DCM computes and settles funding; this is the reference math.
Your index feed licences (the indexes each covers, or all), as ops recorded them. No licence: the feed answers 403 not_a_licensee.
Your licensed index feed reads over `days`, per index and endpoint (licence-usage report).

put.summary: Admin: elect USD for the entity (`usdOnly`). Its sub-accounts then post collateral in USD only and pay every fee in USD, and any CBX reward paid to one of them is converted to USD by the custodian in that account. Audited; it can be turned off again.

get.summary: The custodian's CBX-to-USD reward conversions for an entity that elected USD, newest first, with their status.

post.summary: Place a block buy for an entity: one order booked to the first sub-account in `plan` (it pays from its custodian account), split across every sub-account in the plan at the average price, fees included, once it is done and the custodian confirmed each payment. Each share's cash moves between the entity's own custodian accounts; its units move only after that settles. Every sub-account must be one you may trade, and its share must fit its limits.

get.summary: An entity's block orders, newest first, each with its plan and how it was allocated.
One block order: its order, plan lines (planned and allocated units, average price, cash share, status).

put.summary: Post-trade allocation: set or replace the plan for a buy you placed for one of the entity's sub-accounts (that sub-account leads). Refused once any share has moved.

post.summary: Allocate a done block now (the keeper does it too). Returns `{ outcome, block }`: allocated, waiting (a payment or transfer is not settled yet), nothing_filled or none.

get.summary: Every account you can act on: your own, and each sub-account your entity memberships reach, with your role.
The entities (funds, LLCs, trusts, SPVs) you belong to, and invitations waiting for you.

post.summary: Open an entity account: you become its admin and the custodian partner starts KYB (its own flow; Crossly keeps only its reference). Needs a verified ID and the custodian (503 names what is missing).

get.summary: One entity: members and roles, sub-accounts with their limits, firm halts, caps.

post.summary: Refresh the entity's KYB status from the custodian (and its onboarding link while KYB is open).
Admin: record the entity's attestation that it is an eligible contract participant. Raising its caps is still an ops decision.
Accept or decline an invitation (`accept`). Trading, admin and risk roles need a verified ID to accept.
Admin: invite a Crossly user by email as admin, trader, risk, ops or viewer (a viewer can never place an order), with optional limits and sub-accounts.

patch.summary: Admin: change a member's role, limits or sub-accounts. The last admin cannot be demoted.

delete.summary: Admin: remove a member (or leave, yourself). An entity always keeps one admin.

post.summary: Admin: open a sub-account once the custodian approved the entity; its limits are held to the entity's caps.

put.summary: Admin: set a sub-account's limits (per-order notional, units per key, gross, net, leverage), held to the entity's caps. `limits: null` clears them.

post.summary: Admin: close a sub-account that holds nothing and has no open orders.
Admin or risk: the firm kill switch. Halts the entity (no `subaccountId`) or one sub-account: open orders on it are cancelled and no new ones are placed until cleared.
Admin or risk: lift a firm halt.

get.summary: The entity's audit trail, newest first: hash-chained rows with actor, account, API key, IP, session and source.

Mark NAV, bid NAV (the resting bids) and liquidation NAV (the bids at 20% of ADV for 10 days), holding by holding, each with its ASC 820 level, mark quality and source, and your administrator's price when uploaded.
Daily NAV snapshots (mark, bid, liquidation, Level 2 / Level 3).
The NAV as a csv, pdf or json file.

200.description: The file in the requested `format`: a CSV file, a PDF document or the JSON document.

schema.description: CSV text with a header row.

post.summary: Upload your fund administrator's prices (`administrator`, `marks: [{ bookKey, day, cents }]`). Shown beside Crossly's marks and labelled as yours; they never change a Crossly figure.

get.summary: Historical VaR 95/99 1d/10d and Bangia LVaR (model figures: labelled, with n and a band, null below the data threshold), stress scenarios (category −30%, CBX −50%, books thin to 25%, index drawdowns), concentration and counterparty exposure.

Capacity from the book: `bookKey` (+ `units`) gives ADV, depth within ±5% of the mark, vault stock, lendable units and days to liquidate at 20% of ADV; `index` + `notional` (cents) gives how much of the basket the asks fill now and the days the rest needs.
Your pro orders in a window (`from`, `to`; default 90 days) with arrival mark and mid, average fill, implementation shortfall, slippage, fill rate and time to fill.
One order's TCA, including slippage against the VWAP of eligible trades while it worked.

The quarterly execution-quality report (Rule 605 style): fill rates, speed, effective vs quoted spread and shortfall by order type and size, and the busiest keys. `quarter` like 2026-Q4; the current quarter is provisional.
How orders are handled (the 606/607-style disclosure): one book, self-trade prevention, protected market orders, liquidations by auction, halts, dealers and fees.
Trade confirmations for your fills in a window (default 31 days): price, sale fee, maker or taker, order, vault unit and warehouse receipt.
One trade confirmation.
One trade confirmation as a PDF.
The last 24 months with whether each statement is issued (frozen, with its sha256).

A monthly statement (`month` like 2026-10): units held at month end, loans, pledges, positions, fills, fees, storage, and cash quoted from the custodian and labelled as its record. Issued (frozen) once the month ends.
A monthly statement as a csv, pdf or json file.

200.description: The file in the requested `format`: a CSV file, a PDF document or the JSON document.

schema.description: CSV text with a header row.

get.summary: The fee schedule by role: maker and taker rates for retail, 30-day volume, Registered LPs and DMMs, the CBX discount, the referral share and the 2% net floor Crossly always keeps.

Your fee for an order at a price: as maker (the order rests) and as taker (it fills at once), with the programme that sets your rate and any Crossly One trim. A buyer's fee is added to the price; a seller's comes out of the proceeds.

post.summary: Ask for a quote on a block: dealers, the key's DMM and LPs, and holders are told, anonymously. Answers are firm for 60 s. Your limit is never shown.

get.summary: Your quote requests, newest first.
Open quote requests you were sent (as a dealer, DMM, LP or holder), with your live answer.
Open quote requests on one key (all-to-all: anyone with ID may answer). Anonymous.
One quote request: the requester sees every answer (anonymous); a responder sees the request and their own answer.

post.summary: Answer a quote request for the full quantity with a firm price, good for 60 s. Selling needs the units free in your vault; buying pays from your Vault Markets custodian account.
Take one answer: it fills as a block through the normal fill path (fees by role, self-trade prevention, halts, LULD).
Cancel your open quote request.
Withdraw your live answer to a quote request.

get.summary: Your midpoint block orders.

post.summary: A hidden block order that trades only at the firm-book midpoint, with another midpoint order of at least your minimum size.
Cancel a midpoint order.

get.summary: Your market-maker programmes, the last 30 days of obligations, rebates earned (paid only from fees already taken), and the rules.

post.summary: Join a key as a Registered Liquidity Provider (ID needed). Meeting coverage earns the LP rates.
Apply to be the designated market maker on a tier B or C key. Ops approves; one per key.
Leave a market-maker programme.

get.summary: A key's designated market maker (by the name it chose) and how many LPs quote it.
Your market-maker protection: the fill trigger, the freeze, and whether you are frozen now.

put.summary: Set market-maker protection: N units or $X filled on your quotes within T seconds pulls every quote and freezes quoting for a set time.

post.summary: End a market-maker protection freeze early.
Cancel every open order (one key, or only quotes) and every resting leg in one statement: nothing fills between the first cancel and the last.

get.summary: The insurance fund (booked and free to draw), the most one event may draw before auto-deleveraging (ADL) starts, the loss waterfall in order, and the latest ADL events (no user or position ids). Money in cents.
Your live positions, each with its place in its item ADL queue: lights 5 (first in line) to 1 (last), 0 when not in the queue (only profitable positions are), ranked by P&L% x effective leverage.
One of your positions with its ADL lights (0 once it has ended).
The ADL events your positions were part of, newest first: role bankrupt (yours went under water) or counterparty (yours was first in line), the price both closed at and the transfer status.
Your curve pools: open (default) or all, each with its curve, spot, units, buy budget, running totals, the ladder it shows and its live legs.

post.summary: Open a curve pool on a key (approved dealers, ID checked): linear (delta in cents) or exponential (delta in bps), spot, fee, levels per side, units it may sell, and a buy budget from your custodian account. Its ladder goes up at once.
The bids and asks a set of curve settings would show, and why each side stops where it does. Places nothing.

get.summary: One of your curve pools, with its ladder and live legs.

patch.summary: Change a curve pool: spot, step, fee, levels, units, buy budget, floor, ceiling, or pause / resume. Re-quoted at once.

post.summary: Close a curve pool: its legs come off the book; what filled stays filled.

get.summary: A curve pool's fills, newest first: side, price and spot after.

Bullion key families (metal, form, size, mint or any mint): members, vault units, best resting bid and ask across their books, and spot as a labelled reference with what one unit of metal is worth at it. Spot is never a Crossly price.
One bullion key family: its catalogue products, every live book key with best bid, best ask, vault units and its mark (from the book only), live pegged quote counts, and spot as a labelled reference.
The bullion key families one book key belongs to, with spot for its metal as a labelled reference and its melt value at that spot. Empty families when the item is not keyed bullion.
The price a spot-pegged quote would rest at now (spot plus a premium in cents or basis points, clamped to floor and cap). No price when spot is stale or missing: such a quote waits off the book.
Your spot-pegged quotes (live, or all with status=all): side, units, the peg, the order it rests as, the last price and spot it was priced from, and why it is pulled when it is.

post.summary: Set a spot-pegged maker quote on a bullion book key: "spot plus or minus N cents" or "plus or minus N basis points", with an optional floor and cap. It rests as a pro limit order re-priced every spot tick and is pulled while spot is stale. Replaces your live quote on the same key and side. ID required.

delete.summary: Stop a spot-pegged quote: its resting order comes off the book; what filled stays filled.

get.summary: Your family-wide spot-pegged quotes (live, or all with status=all): one quote resting across a bullion family books at one condition, with units left, the peg, its status and every leg (the pegged quote on each book).

post.summary: Set a family-wide spot-pegged quote: one "any 1 oz gold coin" quote resting on each product book of a bullion family at the chosen condition (DS, VNDS or Used). When any leg fills it comes off the others and goes back on only for what is left; two fills at once are settled one at a time against what is left. A bid pays from your custodian account. Replaces your live family quote on the same family, condition and side. ID required.

delete.summary: Stop a family-wide quote: every leg order comes off the book; what filled stays filled.

get.summary: Peer-to-peer vault loans at a glance: what you owe as a borrower and are owed as a lender (principal + interest to the second), daily interest, called loans, your open offers, the gates and the rules (auction hours, rate ceiling, size bounds, call grace).

The open P2P loan offers book, lowest rate first: cents offered per loan, APR (bps), loans left, and the item (book key) or unit each lends against. `bookKey` narrows to one item. Lender identities are never shown.

post.summary: Offer to lend: `principalCents` per loan at `aprBps` a year against an item (`bookKey`) or one unit (`vaultItemId`), for up to `maxLoans` loans, lasting `expiresInDays` (default 90). Nothing is held: the custodian pays from your own account when a borrower takes it. Needs a verified ID, an active account and the current lending terms.

get.summary: Your P2P loan offers, newest first, with how many loans each has funded.

post.summary: Withdraw one of your open offers. Loans already taken from it carry on.

Borrow: take an offer against one of your stored vault units (`vaultItemId`). The unit is pledged (no listing, lending or withdrawal) and the principal is paid into your custodian account. Interest accrues by the second; repay any time. Pass `requestId` to make a retry safe.

get.summary: Your vault units for P2P borrowing: whether each can be pledged now (and why not), the best offers covering it, and its loan when it has one.

Your P2P loans as borrower and/or lender (`role`), live by default (`status`): what is owed now, daily interest, the refinancing auction when called, and the item mark for information only (it never triggers anything).
One P2P loan with its money log (fund, repay, refinance). A loan in a running refinancing auction can be read by any lender, without the log.

post.summary: Borrower: repay from your custodian account to the lender. Without `amountCents`, in full (principal plus interest to the second; the unit is free once the custodian has it). With `amountCents` below what is owed, a part payment: interest first, then principal, at least the interest owed now and at least $1; the loan stays open on the principal left. Pass `requestId` to make a retry safe.

Lender: call the loan (once it is a day old). A refinancing auction runs for about 30 hours, the rate a new lender gets climbing to the ceiling; repaid or refinanced, you are paid in full; neither by the end, the unit moves to your vault.
Lender: take back your call before any other lender has taken the loan over. The refinancing auction stops and the loan carries on as before on its terms.

Borrower: look for a cheaper lender. A refinancing auction runs for `hours` (1-72, default 24); the rate a new lender gets climbs from `startAprBps` (default half the loan rate) to just under the loan rate now. The first lender to take it pays your lender off and the loan carries on at that lower rate. Nobody by the end: nothing changes.
Borrower: stop looking for a cheaper lender before anyone has taken the loan over. The loan carries on unchanged.

get.summary: Running refinancing auctions, soonest to end first: lenders calls (`auction`) and borrowers looking for a cheaper lender (`refiAuction`). The payoff now, the rate a new lender gets now, when it ends, and the item.

post.summary: Take over a loan in a refinancing auction (a lender call or a borrower search for a cheaper lender): you pay the old lender everything owed now (refused above `maxPayoffCents`), which becomes your loan to the same borrower at the auction rate now. Needs a verified ID, an active account and the current lending terms. Pass `requestId` to make a retry safe.

get.summary: Your vault units with their warehouse receipt and receipt-token state (not exported, waiting for a signature, in a wallet, frozen, redeemed), whether each can be exported now and why not. meta.state is the gate (open, missing envs, program id, authority, terms version, cluster); meta.history is your last 50 exports.
Your verified Solana wallets and whether each is on the receipt-token allow-list (receipt tokens move only between allow-listed wallets). meta.state is the gate.

post.summary: Put one of your verified Solana wallets (`wallet`) on the receipt-token allow-list so it can hold and receive receipt tokens. Returns a base64 transaction already signed by the receipts authority: the wallet pays the small rent (about 0.001 SOL) and must sign and send it within about two minutes. Needs a verified ID and a wallet that passes the sanctions screen.
