get.summary: What a Solana mint is: the warehouse receipt number and item it stands for, and whether the token is live, frozen (unit pledged or lent) or burned, and whether the unit is still on a vault shelf. Names no person and no wallet.
One receipt token (yours, or on a unit you own now) with its chain log: built, minted, frozen, thawed, new holder seen, redeem built, burned, with explorer links.

post.summary: Send one unit (`vaultItemId`) warehouse receipt to one of your verified Solana wallets (`wallet`) as a token, accepting the current terms (`acceptTerms`). Returns a base64 transaction already signed by the new mint and the receipts authority: your wallet pays the rent and must sign and send it within about two minutes, then call confirm. Nothing is minted until it does. Needs a verified ID; the unit must be stored, unpledged, not lent and not for sale.
After your wallet sent the export: read the chain and mark the token live once its one token exists. Pass the `signature` your wallet returned to record it (kept only if it landed).

Redeem a receipt token held in one of your verified Solana wallets (`wallet`): returns an unsigned base64 burn your wallet signs and sends (it also closes the token account and returns its rent to you). Once it lands, call redeem/confirm and the unit is yours in the vault. Refused while the token is frozen.
After your wallet sent the redeem: read the chain; once the token is burned the unit moves into your vault (if it was not yours already). Pass the `signature` to record it.

get.summary: One book key mark with everything behind it: the price in cents, its quality (A trade-anchored, B firm two-sided, C indicative, none), its confidence in bps and the band in cents, when it was computed, whether risk may act on it (judged for margin), the related key it was implied from (impliedFrom: a grade, the model median of the other sizes, or an index; null when none), every stored input, and the learned relations it may be implied from.

Portfolio margin for a firm sub-account (`subaccountId`): eligibility with every reason (ECP, KYB, minimum equity $500k or $100k with evidenced intraday monitoring), whether it is enrolled, the latest requirement, equity, excess and state (healthy, call or buy_in), the breakdown by category and item, the partner index futures counted, and the policy. Before enrolling, a live preview.

The 5-minute portfolio margin recalculations for a firm sub-account over the last `hours` (default 24, at most 720), newest first: equity, requirement, excess, scenario and floor figures, gross and state.

post.summary: Admin: put a firm sub-account under portfolio margin. Needs VAULT_LEVERAGE_VENUE, your ID, an ECP-attested entity that passed KYB, and the minimum equity. Its positions are then margined on the whole account, recalculated every 5 minutes; calls and auctions are unchanged. Audited.
Admin: take a firm sub-account off portfolio margin. Each position is then held to its own tier floors again and may be called at once. Audited.
The portfolio margin requirement of a firm sub-account before and after a trade (`bookKey`, `side` buy or sell, `units`), at the Crossly mark with fees left out. Changes nothing.

get.summary: Crossly as an oracle publisher (needs CROSSLY_ORACLE_PUBLISHER_KEY + CROSSLY_ORACLE_NETWORK): the network (pyth or switchboard), the ed25519 key every value is signed with, each published index feed with its latest attempt, and 24 h counts of published, skipped and failed. Only built-in indexes priced from A/B marks are published; Crossly never reads its own feed back.

The latest published oracle value for an index: level, fixed-point price and confidence at the feed exponent, confidence in bps, staleness in seconds, coverage, the exact signed message and its ed25519 signature with the signer key, and whether it is fresh.

Recent publish attempts for an index over 30 days, newest first: published, skipped (with the reason: too few items priced, stale marks, confidence too wide...) or failed (with the error). Filter with `status`, cap with `limit` (default 100).

The partner exchange (DCM) that lists and clears futures and options on Crossly indexes (needs VAULT_INDEX_DCM + VAULT_INDEX_DCM_API_URL + VAULT_INDEX_DCM_API_KEY), and its contracts as last read: perps, futures and options with the index each settles on, multiplier, tick, expiry and strike. Read-only: Crossly is the licensor and data provider, never the venue.
One partner contract: its spec, its funding prints (newest first; the partner computes and settles funding), annualised funding over the last 21 prints, and the Crossly index level it settles on.

The partner exchange live order book for a contract (cached 5 seconds), with mark, index, last, open interest, 24 h volume, spread in bps and the basis of its mark over the Crossly index in bps. Prices are index points.

Options inputs for an index (indexes only, never a single item): Crossly realised volatility (raw and Geltner-desmoothed, from weekly returns), the forward (the partner future mark, else the Crossly close), Black-76 greeks on a strike x expiry grid and on every option the partner lists on the index. Model inputs, not quotes.

The partner exchange account linked to your account (or to the firm sub-account `subaccountId`) and its positions, read-only (cached 15 seconds); index futures on category indexes count as portfolio-margin hedges for that account: contracts, side, entry and mark price, unrealised P&L and margin in cents, liquidation price and notional in cents. Not linked: `linked: false`.

post.summary: Link a partner exchange account to your account (or to a firm sub-account you manage, `subaccountId`) so Crossly can show its positions: `accountRef` (the account id there) and `code` (the one-time link code it gave you). The partner must confirm the code; the code is never stored. Read-only: Crossly never trades on it.
Unlink the partner exchange account from your account (or the firm sub-account `subaccountId`): Crossly stops reading it and its hedges leave portfolio margin.

get.summary: Your large-trader reports (with any linked accounts, as one party): due first, then filed, then cleared in the last 90 days. Each has `action`: file | amend | refile | none.

post.summary: File (or amend, or refile) a large-trader report: why you hold it (purpose), who you act for, other accounts you control, whether you plan to add, and a statement of 20+ characters. Returns the report.

get.summary: Market Open events in the Crossly World Commons: keys opening soon and those that opened in the last few hours, live first then soonest, each with its board line, units on the shelf, dealers quoting and the launch show when there is one. Never a prompt to trade.

The Vault Holders Lounge: the rule to join (held value at reliable marks, or a unit count), whether you may join now and what you hold toward it. Anyone may look in; only holders are seen there. No perks, nothing to trade.
Verified creators whose public vault shelf is a world room: title, the creator, the room link and the disclosure. Rooms show each market share of the shelf, never amounts.

The Vault Markets creator programme: the share of the fee Crossly keeps that a creator earns, the per-fill and lifetime caps (cents), the attribution window in days, the 2% net floor it sits under, and the disclosure words.
The creator who brought you to Vault Markets, when one did: when it started and ends, whether it still earns, and the disclosure. Your prices and fees are the same either way.

post.summary: Use a creator code: the creator earns a capped share of the fee Crossly keeps on your Vault Markets trades for a limited window (paid by Crossly, never by you). Only for people new to Vault Markets, once, and never your own code.

get.summary: For creators: whether you joined the programme, each of your codes with traders attributed and still earning (counts only), shares accrued, paid and voided (cents) and the latest shares.
For creators: your vault shelf room (applied, verified, rejected or paused) and whether your public vault profile is on, which the room needs.

The vault-holder door on a Crossly World room or Space, by its presence slug (a room share slug, or space-<slug>): the rule (minValueCents held at reliable A/B marks and/or minUnits units, mode any or all, optionally one product, bullion family or category), the rule in words, and whether you may join now with what you hold toward it. gate is null when the place has no vault door. Anyone may look in; only holders join.

put.summary: Set the vault-holder door on your own room (its collection rooms follow): visitors must hold minValueCents (cents, at reliable A/B marks) and/or minUnits units in the Crossly vault, mode any (either) or all (both), optionally only one product (scope kind product, ref the catalogue product id), bullion family (bullion, the family slug) or category (category, the slug). Send null to open it again. Returns `{ gate }`. Moves no money.

Set the vault-holder door on a Space you host: the same rule as a room (minValueCents at reliable marks and/or minUnits, mode, optional scope). Send null to open it again. Returns `{ gate }`. Moves no money.

get.summary: Market Open launch shows a verified creator co-hosts that are on now or opening soon: the key, its phase, the show, the creator (named only while their vault profile is public), their room link and, when the creator is in the creator programme, the disclosure that they may earn a share of the fee Crossly keeps. Never a prompt to trade.
For creators: your invites from Crossly to co-host a Market Open launch show (invited, accepted, declined or withdrawn), each with the key, its show and the guidance for co-hosts.

post.summary: For creators: accept or decline an invite to co-host a Market Open launch show (`accept` true or false). Accepting needs your vault room verified and adds you to the show as a co-host; your room and the Commons then say you co-host it, with the creator-programme disclosure when it applies.

get.summary: Your Grade to Vault flows, newest first, each brought up to date: its step, the grading submission, the unit, the grade, the market for it, and the ask once listed. `live=1` for those still going.

post.summary: Start Grade to Vault on one item (`source` inventory or vault_unit). With `runId` the grading slot is booked at once (free; your saved card is charged only if the run locks). Nothing is listed until you confirm a price after the grade.

get.summary: What you can start Grade to Vault on: raw inventory matched to a catalogue item, and raw vault units on the grading hub shelf; plus whether Grading Runs are open.
One Grade to Vault flow, brought up to date with its submission and unit.

post.summary: Book (or re-book) the grading slot of a flow still at "picked". Answers 503 naming GRADING_HUB_ADDRESS when runs are not open.
You mailed the card to the grading hub (an inventory card, once its run locked).

Confirm the price for the grade the unit came back with (`confirm: true`, `gradeKey` must match the unit). Pre-trade risk, the price band and the ID line apply, then one shelf ask is placed on the Crossly order book.
Keep the graded unit in your vault without listing it. The flow ends; list it any time from the vault.
Stop the flow before the card goes to the grader (still picked, or its slot only reserved: nothing was charged).

get.summary: Evidence on a vault unit:its 3D scans (model, texture, listing photos) and its grade report (grader, grade, cert, verified against the grader record, hub intake photos). No owner identity.

post.summary: Add a finished scan of your own (`captureId`, of the same catalogue item) to your vault unit. Shown as added by the owner, not as intake evidence.

delete.summary: Take back a scan you added to your vault unit (intake evidence stays).

get.summary: The vault units lent to this week's Hall of Grails exhibition and on show now, in plinth order: the item (skuId, name, imageUrl, grade), the lender as the plate names them (a display name, or "a collector"), the plate lines and how many exhibitions the unit has stood in. meta.exhibition is the week (key, title, endsAt). Names no ids and no amounts.

Your Hall of Grails desk: this week's exhibition, the rules (maxLive loans, shownPerHolder per exhibition, repPoints per exhibition shown), reputation (exhibitions finished), your loans (status active, ending or ended; onShowNow, showingUntil, exhibitions, the next exhibition it fits, the Lent to the Hall badge) and the vault units you could lend (canLend, or the blocker in words, and the next exhibition each fits). Display only.

post.summary: Lend a unit in your Crossly vault to the Hall of Grails: { vaultItemId, credit: 'name' | 'anonymous' }. A standing loan of display rights only: the unit goes on a plinth, under a plate naming you (or "a collector"), in every weekly exhibition whose category it fits. It never moves and stays yours to list, sell or withdraw. Earns reputation per exhibition shown; no cash. Resumes a loan you opted out of while it still shows.
Opt a Hall of Grails loan out, at any time. A unit on a plinth this week finishes this exhibition (status ending, showingUntil); otherwise the loan ends now (status ended).
Change how the plate on a lent unit's plinth names you, from now: { credit: 'name' } (your display name) or { credit: 'anonymous' } ("a collector").

get.summary: Your price watches on book keys (best bid, lowest ask, last trade or market price, in cents), live ones first. `?live=true` for live only.

post.summary: Watch a book key: tell me once when its best bid, lowest ask, last trade or market price crosses a price (cents). Leave out direction for "crosses" (whichever way it has to move). Never trades. At most 50 live, each for 90 days.

delete.summary: Cancel a live price watch. Returns the watch.

get.summary: Limit orders the shopping agent drafted for you, newest first. A draft places nothing: send its orderBody to POST /api/v1/vault-markets/pro/orders to place it.
One drafted order: item, side, units, limit (cents), the book when drafted, status, and the orderBody that places it.

post.summary: Throw a drafted order away (only while it is still a draft). Returns { ok, draft }.

get.summary: Your paper-trading missions (play money only): each mission with what to do, your count toward its target, whether it is done and when, plus a suggested market for the "Read the mark" mission. Progress is observed by the server from your paper orders and fills, price watches, set goals and graded mark checks. Missions earn world quest progress and cosmetic pins, never money.

post.summary: Answer the "Read the mark" mission: the quality letter (A, B or C) you read on a market page, checked against the stored mark. One answer per market, 10 a day. Returns `{ bookKey, answer, correct, quality, mission, next }`.

get.summary: Your paper trading account (play money only, never real or convertible; opened at $10,000 the first time): play cash, buying power, paper positions at the real marks, P&L, working paper orders, recent paper fills and this week on the leaderboard.
Your paper orders since your last reset, newest first: working, done (filled, cancelled, expired) or all. Play money only.

post.summary: Place a paper order (play money only). It takes visible real liquidity now at book prices with the taker fee simulated; a GTC limit rests the rest with a queue-position estimate, filled later as the real tape reaches it. Sells only paper units you hold (no paper shorts). Never touches the real book. Returns `{ order, fills }`.

get.summary: Your paper fills since your last reset, newest first: price, simulated fee, taker or maker, and whether a visible real order (book) or a real trade (tape) filled it. Play money only.

What a paper order would fill against the real book now, without placing it: units fillable inside the limit (a market order uses the 5% protection band around the mark), average price, simulated fee, and the queue ahead of any rest.

post.summary: Cancel a working paper order: the play cash or paper units it held come back. Returns `{ order }`.
Reset your paper account to $10,000 of play money: working paper orders are cancelled, paper positions cleared, and your leaderboard week starts again. Once a day.

get.summary: The weekly paper trading leaderboard (opt-in, display names only): best return on play equity this week (or a past `week`, its Monday as YYYY-MM-DD), with your own line. Nothing is won or paid.

put.summary: Join or leave the weekly paper leaderboard. Joining needs a display name (2 to 24 letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes or underscores), never your real name. Returns `{ optIn, displayName }`.

get.summary: Your Vault Markets mode: simple (buy, sell and what it is worth) or pro (the full terminal), whether you chose it or it was set for you (new people start in simple; people already trading start in pro), and when.

put.summary: Choose your Vault Markets mode: `mode` simple or pro. Remembered for you on the web and in the app. A display preference only: it places nothing and moves no money.

get.summary: What one book key (variantId:condition:gradeKey, `bookKey`) is worth: the mark in cents with its quality (A from trades, B from firm quotes, C indicative, none) and band, what Instant Exit would pay for one unit now from the best resting bid (yours left out), and your units: how many you hold, how many are free to sell, their value at the mark and what selling every free one now would fetch from today’s bids. Plain-words `headline` and `lines`. Read only.

What your whole vault is worth now: value at the marks split into reliable and indicative marks, cost and P&L, today’s change, and an estimate of what the units free to sell would fetch from the bids resting on the book now. Read only.

One vault unit's story, oldest first: intake (with scan and grade evidence when it has some), grades, owners, sales at their prices, loans, pledges, Hall of Grails exhibitions, receipt-token exports and redemptions, and each warehouse-receipt hash-chain step (re-verified on read: chain.ok). People are named only while their public vault profile is on; others are 'A collector'.
The vault units of one of your positions that you hold (a leveraged long's collateral), each with its story link.

Your vault alert settings: every kind (price, fill, margin_call, adl, p2p_loan, auction, market_open, receipt_token, set_goal, follow, account), every channel (push, telegram, terminal, email, webhook) with whether it is set up, the full on/off grid, the locked switches (a critical kind always pushes) and quiet hours.

put.summary: Change vault alert settings: `matrix` ({ kind: { channel: true|false } }, merged onto what is set), `quietHours` ({ start: "HH:MM", end: "HH:MM", tz } or null to clear) and `telegram` (the Telegram master switch). Locked switches are ignored. Returns the new settings.

post.summary: Send yourself one test alert of a `kind` through your own switches. Returns `{ sent, kind, plan }`, where plan says per channel: send, off, quiet (held by quiet hours) or unavailable.

get.summary: What the alerts hub did with your recent vault alerts (`?limit=` 1 to 200, default 50): kind, title, the channels it went to, what was held (channel:reason) and the email digest state.
Your sharing switches: the public vault profile, new buys, units sent in, sales, Hall loans, bids and asks for copy-watchers, and the leaderboards. All off until you turn them on.

put.summary: Turn sharing switches on or off (`isPublic`, `showBuys`, `deposits`, `sales`, `hallLoans`, `orders`, `leaderboard`). A switch shows only what happens after it goes on; all but the profile itself need the profile public.

get.summary: The collectors you follow who have a public vault: what each shares and whether you copy-watch them.
Public vault activity of the collectors you follow (buys, units sent in, sales, Hall loans), newest first, never a price. Filter with `kinds`; page with `before`.
One collector public vault activity, newest first, never a price. 404 when their vault is not public.
An opt-in return leaderboard (`period` 30d, 90d or 365d; `category` all or a category slug), ranked by risk-adjusted return from the book A/B marks. Percent and risk only: no dollars, no volume.
The collectors you copy-watch and whether each still shares bids and asks.

put.summary: Copy-watch a collector who shares bids and asks: you get an alert when they rest a new one. It never places an order for you.

delete.summary: Stop copy-watching a collector.

get.summary: Your copy-watch alerts, newest first: who, bid or ask, quantity, limit price, market, and whether it still rests. Page with `before`.

post.summary: Mark every copy-watch alert read. Returns `{ marked }`.

get.summary: The Trading Floor in Crossly World: trades (the newest trades on every vault book in the last day, at most 40, newest first: bookKey, name, priceCents, priceText, side -- buy when a buyer took an ask, sell when a seller hit a bid, cross for an auction -- and ageS), tickers (the big board: the most-traded markets, each with its last trade price, the change from the last trade before today in basis points, trades today and the display mark with its quality), bell (Market Open: ringing for ten minutes after a new key opens, with the key and its market link, and what opens next) and trades24h. Every price is a trade on the Crossly order book; it never shows who traded. Nothing can be traded in the room.

The Trading Floor boards for the round-13 products: odds (the probability ladder: the busiest open "Will it hit?" markets with probabilityBps, the market’s own price as a probability, display only), heat (option-chain heat: per listed underlying, open interest and the last day’s volume in milli-contracts in strike buckets around the underlying, a 0..1 heat per bucket and the at-the-money implied vol, display only) and shares (Vault Shares tickers: last share price in cents, changeBps from the last fill before today, shares traded today and the implied item value, display only). quality is always C: none of these is ever a mark. It never shows who traded.

Sets to start a goal on. With q (2+ characters): a word-start search of every catalogue set. Without: the sets you hold pieces of in the vault, then the collections you are building. Each with your live goal on it, if any.
Your set goals: the set, the target a piece must meet, pieces held of the total (from your vault), and the working basket bid.

post.summary: Start a goal on a catalogue set (category, brandSlug, modelSlug from the set search), optionally with a target: one condition, and any grade, ungraded, or one exact grade. One live goal per set.

get.summary: One set goal: every piece in the set order, held (with the vault unit) or missing (with the cheapest marked book key that meets the target and its mark), the conditions and grades seen, and the working basket bid with its legs.

patch.summary: Change what a piece must be to count (condition, grade mode, grade). Refused while a basket bid works: cancel it first.

delete.summary: Remove a set goal. A working basket bid is cancelled first; what filled stays in your vault.

get.summary: What a basket bid would place now, without placing it: one leg per missing piece (cheapest first, the mark plus maxBpsOverMark as the limit), the pieces skipped and why, and the most it can cost (limits plus the worst-case buyer fee), never more than budgetCents.

post.summary: Place the "complete my set" basket bid: one GTC limit buy per missing piece, under a hard budget, paid by one of your saved cards or your custodian account. Every leg passes pre-trade risk and the ID line like any order. Idempotent on clientBasketId. One working basket per goal; its legs are cancelled once the set is complete.
Cancel the goal working basket bid: every working leg comes off the book; what already filled stays in your vault.

get.summary: A set goal basket bids, newest first, each with its budget, what it committed and spent, and every leg (piece, book key, limit, pro order id, status).

An insurance or appraisal statement for a day (purpose, asOf YYYY-MM-DD, default today), built but not issued: every unit you held that day at its mark, with quality, last trade, grade and cert, and the total. No id, no hash.

post.summary: Issue an insurance or appraisal statement for a day: frozen with the sha256 of its record, sealed in the Crossly audit chain, with a public verify link. preparedFor and policyRef are printed on it and never shown on verify. Moves no money.

get.summary: The insurance and appraisal statements you issued, newest first: purpose, date, units, total at the marks, hash and verify link.
One statement you issued: every unit, the totals by mark quality, the methodology, its sha256, its audit-chain seal and the verify link.
One statement you issued as a PDF.

Check any issued statement by its id, as an insurer would: purpose, date, totals by mark quality and the sha256; intact (the stored record still hashes to it), seal.ok (its audit-chain entry still carries it) and, with ?hash=, whether yours matches. Never the holder or the units.
Your joint vaults and the invitations waiting for you, with the gate (open, missing env), the joint terms in words and what each right allows. A JointVaultsHome object, not a collection.

post.summary: Open a joint vault (ID first): you hold full rights and accept the current joint terms. `invite` sends invitations (@username or email, each with view, trade or full rights). Returns `{ id, status, invited }`.

get.summary: One joint vault (active members only): members and rights, the units in it at the mark with each owner of record, totals, recent joint trades, and the activity from the audit trail.

post.summary: Invite a Crossly user (full rights only). They have 14 days and show ID to join. Returns `{ userId, rights, expiresAt }`.
Accept (ID first; accepts the current joint terms) or decline an invitation. Returns `{ status }`.
Accept the current joint terms (needed to trade after the terms version changes). Returns `{ termsVersion }`.
Set a member rights to view, trade or full (full rights only; the vault always keeps a full member). Returns `{ userId, rights }`.
Remove a member (full rights), or leave when userId is you. Their units go back to their own account and their joint orders are cancelled. Returns `{ userId, status, unitsReturned, jointStatus }`.
Put units you own into the joint vault (each stored and free). They keep you as owner of record and stay on the shelf. Returns `{ added, vaultItemIds }`.
Take units out of the joint vault, back to their owner own account (yours at any rights; anyone else with full rights). Returns `{ removed, vaultItemIds }`.

get.summary: The joint vault trades, newest first: side, book key, limit, who started it, whose account the order sits on, and the order standing on the book.

post.summary: Place a limit order for the joint vault (trade or full rights, ID shown). A buy (bookKey) is placed on you, paid from your own Vault Markets account, and what it buys is booked to the joint vault. A sell (vaultItemId of a unit in it) is placed on the unit owner of record, who gets the proceeds; pre-trade checks run against you too. Returns `{ tradeId, side, bookKey, ownerUserId, order }`.
Cancel a working joint order (trade or full rights); what filled stays filled. Returns `{ tradeId, order }`.
Close the joint vault (full rights): open joint orders are cancelled and every unit goes back to its owner. Returns `{ status, unitsReturned }`.

get.summary: Your transfer-on-death setup: the gate and terms, whether you accepted them, your beneficiaries and shares, units with their designations and who the plan gives them to today, and open claims on your account (which you can stop). A TodOverview object, not a collection.

post.summary: Accept the current transfer-on-death terms. Returns `{ termsVersion }`.

put.summary: Replace your beneficiary list (keep an id to edit one): full name, contact (email or @username), relationship, and share in basis points; shares add up to 10000. Returns `{ beneficiaries, removed }`.
Leave one of your units to one beneficiary (beneficiaryId null clears it; the unit then follows the shares). Returns `{ vaultItemId, beneficiaryId }`.

post.summary: Stop a transfer-on-death claim made on your own account. Returns `{ id, status, estateUnlocked }`.

get.summary: Claims you filed as a beneficiary: status in words, documents sent (names only), the waiting period, and units moved or held. A TodMyClaims object, not a collection.

post.summary: Start a claim as a named beneficiary (ID first), naming the account holder by @username or email. It stays a draft until you add documents and submit. Returns `{ id, status, existing }`.

Add one document to a draft claim (or one ops asked more of): kind, filename and the file as base64 (PDF, JPEG or PNG, up to 8 MB). Kept privately for ops review. Returns `{ id, kind, label, filename, bytes }`.
Send a claim for ops review (it needs a death certificate). The account holder is told and can stop it. Returns `{ id, status }`.
Withdraw a claim before it is released. Returns `{ id, status }`.

get.summary: What to send to the vault: your inventory items whose book key has a liquid vault market (tier A, B or C), best first. Each has a score (0 to 100) and its reasons, the market (tier, mark and its quality, best bid, best vault ask, spread), Instant Exit now, your list price, days listed without selling, and the vault fee. `meta.summary` counts what was left out and why. Inform only; send with POST /api/v1/vault-markets/supply/send.
One inventory item: its vault suggestion, or in plain words why there is none (`status`: suggested, not_found, no_stock, not_matched, in_vault or no_market).

Portfolio health of your vault holdings at Crossly marks: concentration by single item, category, grade and grader (shares, HHI on 0 to 10000, its band and effective number of holdings), value by liquidity tier, the stress grid (each category and everything down 10, 20 and 30 percent), value by mark quality, plain observations, and the held items a what-if can run on. Information only, not advice.

What if one held item moved by moveBps (-10000 to 10000 basis points of its mark): the item, your vault total, the item and its category share of the vault, and the single-item HHI, before and after. A scenario on the mark, not a price you could sell at.

Tax-loss suggestions: the units you hold whose mark is below your cost, each with its lot (acquired when and how, cost in cents), short or long term if sold today and the day a short lot turns long, the estimated loss at the mark before selling fees, mark quality, what stops a sale, and a link to the ordinary sell ticket. With totals by term, the gains realised so far this year, and a not-tax-advice disclosure. Never sells.

Your fractional options tax lots for a calendar year (`year`, default this year): FIFO disposals (closed or settled) with proceeds, cost, gain in cents and holding term, each flagged as a possible Section 1256 contract, the totals with the 60/40 split, and the positions open at year end. Real fills only; practice never appears. Not tax advice.

Your Vault Shares tax lots for a calendar year (`year`): disposals (share-book sales, exit payouts) with holding periods, proceeds, cost and gain in cents, the open lots and the totals. The broker-dealer issues the 1099-B; not tax advice.

Your prediction-market results for a calendar year (`year`), as the venue reports them: each settled or voided real-money position with its venue, cost, fees, payout, refund, closing-trade gains and net in cents, and the totals. Practice never appears. Not tax advice.

"Show my vault": the vault units you hold, the ones standing in your Crossly World home first. Each: vaultItemId, title, grade, imageUrl, bookKey (its market), inHome, visitors (visitors to your home see it). Also your home (slug, privacy, path), max units one home shows, shown, visitorsSee and a note on who sees what. Your home is made on first read. No prices.

put.summary: Show exactly these vault units in your Crossly World home: { units: [{ vaultItemId, visitors }] }. Units left out come out of their cases; units already standing stay where they are; new ones go into a free display-case or shelf slot, else a glass case of their own along a wall. visitors: true lets people who may enter your home see that unit (default false: only you). Returns placed, unplaced (no free case: the home is full), refused (with why) and the desk. Display only: nothing moves.

get.summary: A vault unit as an AR model, for "See it in your room" (the web's /ar/vault-<id> page hands it to Scene Viewer, WebXR or Quick Look): title, model (a path under /models, without .glb, at real size), scanUrl (the unit's own captured mesh, when it has one), imageUrl, art, tint, scale, bookKey, backPath and mine. Your own units always; somebody else's only while they show it to visitors in a home you may enter (else 404).
Your price widgets, newest first, each with its iframe and script-tag snippets. `meta.codes` lists your affiliate codes a widget can link through; `meta.max` is the cap on live widgets.

post.summary: Make a price widget for one vault market (`kind` mark + `bookKey`) or one public index (`kind` index + `indexSlug`): range, layout (compact or chart), theme (auto, light, dark), optionally your own affiliate code for the link back and the sites allowed to show it (empty = any). Returns the widget with its snippets.
What a widget would show before you save it: `view` (value, move, quality, n, as-of, link back) and `html`, the exact page the iframe serves. Nothing is stored.

get.summary: One of your price widgets, with its iframe and script-tag snippets and URLs.

patch.summary: Change a widget: name, range, layout, theme, affiliate code (null for none) or allowed sites. The market or index it shows never changes: make a new widget for another.

delete.summary: Delete a widget. Pages that still paste it show that it is no longer available. Returns `{ id, archived }`.

get.summary: Grading population report for one market (`bookKey`): focus (on a graded market: its grade, pop = copies graded at exactly that grade, higher = copies graded better by the same grader, total, asOf and source), graders (each grader ladder for the card, best grade first, from one report: the newest, the population feed over a hand entry on the same date), provider.connected, and status (ok, not_synced, no_report or no_source) with explain, which says in plain words what is missing. source is provider (the population feed) or ops (entered by Crossly from the grader published report). Counts only, never a price.

parameters.name: bookKey
parameters.description: variantId:condition:gradeKey, grade "-" when ungraded.

get.summary: The home-screen widget summary: portfolio value at the mark with its move since the previous marks (cents and bps) and the share resting on reliable A/B marks, the three biggest movers among what you hold (the market movers when you hold nothing; `movers.source` says which), and one watchlist key (`?key=` a book key on your watchlist; else your newest watch) with a 14-day sparkline. Every price is from the Crossly order book and carries its mark quality (A, B, C or none). Cached for five minutes.
Your live home-screen widget tokens, one per phone: id, name (the phone), public prefix, created and last used. The secret is never returned again.

post.summary: Mint a widget token for one phone (`deviceName`, `installId`); minting again with the same pair replaces that phone token. The token reads the widget summary and nothing else, and is returned once. At most five phones.

delete.summary: Turn the widget off on every phone: revokes all your widget tokens. Returns `{ revoked }`, how many.
Turn the widget off on one phone: revokes that widget token at once. Only a widget token can be revoked here.

get.summary: Vault Shares at a glance: the venue mode in force (self, partner or paper) and the env it still needs, the rules (about $5 a share, 100 to 100,000 shares, originator keeps 0-50%, 3% origination, maker 0 / taker 100 bps, 90-day lockup, buyouts at the mark x 1.10 with a two-thirds vote) and the disclosure.

Vault Shares series: open offerings first, then trading, then the rest. `status` and `bookKey` narrow it. Each with its terms, progress, last share price and implied item value (display only, never a mark), and your holding.

post.summary: Propose a Vault Shares series for one of your units (`vaultItemId`), keeping `retainedShares` (0-50%), with an optional minimum raise, offering length (7-60 days) and reserve. Ops then qualify it, attach the offering circular and open the offering. With no venue it is a practice series. Pass `requestId` to make a retry safe.

get.summary: One series: the offering, the share book depth, the latest fills, holders as share percentages (nobody named), buyouts and your vote, your orders and subscriptions.
A share book’s depth: whole shares per price level (integer cents a share), best first.
The latest fills on a share book, newest first, with which side made the market.
Your Vault Shares: shares and percent of each item, cost, implied value at the last price, your subscriptions and the payouts you were sent.
The world vault home’s fractional tiles: each item you own a share of, with "you own 3.2%".
Your offering subscriptions, newest first, with where each stands (pending, escrowed, allocated, refunded).
Your investor account at the venue in force: its status, the investor terms you accepted, and your Reg A+ limit for one offering (10% of the greater of income and net worth unless accredited).

post.summary: Open or update your investor account at the venue: accept the current investor terms (`acceptTerms`), and state accredited status or your annual income and net worth for the Reg A+ limit. Needs a verified ID.

get.summary: Fractionalize instead: whether one of your vault units can become a Vault Shares series now (stored, tier A or B, reliable mark of $1,000 or more, declared and insured, free) and the offering terms it would get.

post.summary: Withdraw your own proposal before its offering opens.

Subscribe for whole `shares` in an open offering at its fixed price. The money goes into the venue’s escrow in your own name and is refunded if the offering misses its minimum. Reg A+ limits apply. A joint vault member with trade rights may pass `jointVaultId`. Pass `requestId` to make a retry safe.
Cancel an escrowed subscription while its offering is still open: the escrow is refunded.

get.summary: Your share-book orders, newest first; `seriesId` and `open` narrow it.

post.summary: Place an order on a series’ share book: `side`, `type` limit or market (immediate-or-cancel inside a 10% band), `tif` gtc / gtd (`expiresAt`) / ioc, whole `shares` or a buy’s `amountCents` (turned into whole shares at the most it could pay), integer `limitCents` a share, `postOnly`. Fees: maker 0, taker 100 bps plus the broker-dealer pass-through. Self-trades are prevented. Pass `requestId` to make a retry safe.
Cancel one of your open share-book orders.

Bid for the whole item (`offerCents`, at least the mark x 1.10). The bid is escrowed at the venue, then holders vote by shares: two-thirds yes accepts, a majority against rejects, 14 days with no majority against accepts. Accepted, the item is yours and the price is paid out pro rata after storage and insurance.
Vote `yes` or `no` on a buyout with the shares you held when the vote opened. You can change your vote while it is open.
Your whole-unit bid reached the reserve: fund the price through your investor account within 72 hours to buy the item from its holders (no vote).
Withdraw your buyout bid before its vote opens; the escrow is refunded.
You hold every share: take the item back whole. With `withdraw`, it ships home at once (any receipt token is burned as it leaves). Storage and insurance the series owed stay with the unit.

get.summary: Your practice account for Vault Shares (play money only, never real, never convertible): cash, practice holdings, open practice orders, recent practice fills.
A series’ practice book: practice orders and the house quote 1% either side of the reference price.

post.summary: Place a practice order (play money) with the same rules as the real share book.
Cancel an open practice order.
Subscribe with play money to a practice series’ offering.
Start the practice account over with fresh play money (once a day).

get.summary: The Vault Shares drops calendar: announced and open offerings, soonest first, each with its phase (announced, early_access, requests, open), the countdown, the allocation (fcfs, pro_rata or lottery with a per-person cap), your Crossly One early-access time (it moves when you may ask, never the price) and whether you asked to be told.

post.summary: Ask to be told about a drop (`kind` notify: when your early access opens and when it opens to everyone) or join the waitlist of a sold-out first-come offering (`kind` waitlist, with the `shares` you want).
Stop being told about a drop (`kind` notify) or leave its waitlist (`kind` waitlist).

get.summary: A series’ full price history: OHLC candles of every share-book fill (`interval` 1h, 1d or 1w), the offering price, the change since the offering, and the appraisal history beside it. Share prices are display only, never a mark.
The item’s appraisal history: the offering valuation (sealed valuation statement), independent and insurance appraisals, and any buyout or exit price.
The item’s story, provenance, condition reports, appraisals and exhibitions, newest first. Holders also see holders-only updates.

post.summary: Post an update on your own item’s series (you are its originator): `kind` story, provenance, condition, appraisal, exhibition or event, a `title`, a `body`, an optional https `mediaUrl`, `holdersOnly`. Holders are told.

get.summary: Holder perks on a series: whether you hold it, your holder badge, the links to visit the item in the world vault room and in AR, the viewing days with places left and your bookings.
The holder room for a series (shareholders only): posts newest first under per-series aliases, never account names. `before` pages back.

post.summary: Post in the holder room (shareholders only), up to 1,000 characters.
Take down one of your own holder-room posts (`reason`).
Book a place on a viewing day (shareholders only), with up to the day’s `guests`. Bookings close a day before; booking again changes your guests.
Cancel your viewing-day booking.

get.summary: Your share gifts, sent and received, newest first, with where each stands (offered, instructed, settled, declined, cancelled, expired, rejected).

post.summary: Give whole `shares` of a series to someone (`to`: their @handle, email or user id), with an optional `message`. The shares are set aside until they accept (14 days). On acceptance the broker-dealer or transfer agent verifies them and moves the shares on the register: no money moves, and your cost basis and holding date carry over.
Accept a share gift. Needs your own verified Vault Shares investor account; the venue then moves the shares to you on the register.
Decline a share gift offered to you.
Cancel a gift you offered, before it is accepted: the shares are free again.

get.summary: Your recurring auto-invest plans: amount, weekly or monthly, the series and weights or the basket, what rolled over (budget too small for a whole share; your money stays at the venue), the next run.

post.summary: Start auto-invest: `amountCents` ($5-$10,000) `every` week or month into `seriesIds` (equal weights) or `targets` (seriesId + weightBps summing to 10,000) or a `basketId` (with `rebalance` to keep your own shares on its weights). Whole shares only; the rest rolls over. Offerings are subscribed at their price; trading books are bought at the best ask up to `maxPremiumBps` over the indicative value. `practice` runs it on paper.
Change a plan (amount, cadence, series or weights, cap, rebalance) or set its `status` active, paused or cancelled.
Run a plan now (once a minute at most); the schedule does not move.

get.summary: A plan’s runs, newest first: the budget, what each series bought, what was spent and what rolled over; rebalances too.
Theme baskets: curated model portfolios of Vault Shares series with target weights. You buy and own every share directly in your own name; a basket is never a fund.
One theme basket (id or slug): its series, target and live weights, prices, and your own holdings against the weights.

post.summary: Buy a basket once: `amountCents` split by its live weights into whole shares of each series, in your own name (offerings subscribed, trading books at the best ask up to `maxPremiumBps`). `practice` buys on paper.

get.summary: Fractional options: the venue mode (self = Crossly is the venue and clearing house, partner = routed to the index DCM, paper = practice only) with the env each mode still needs, the active series and the rule book in force.
Every options series: its underlying (a Crossly index, or a tier A item key with 90 days of reliable marks), status and the eligibility snapshot it last passed. `status`: active (default) or all.

The option chain for an underlying (index slug or book key): its expiries, and for one expiry (`expiry`, default the nearest) each strike's call and put with best bid / ask, last, open interest, the theoretical price at the reference vol, the implied vol of the mid (display only, never a mark) and the Greeks. Prices are cents per contract.
The at-the-money implied volatility of the nearest expiry on an underlying, for display on its page: derived from the options book, quality C, never written as a mark.

One option contract: its terms, the self-venue book and tape, its published daily settlement prices and, once settled, its settlement (value, source, flagged, and the hash chained to the previous settlement).
A contract's order book on the Crossly venue (`levels`, default 20): bids and asks by price with milli-contract sizes, and the last 50 prints.

A contract's published daily settlement prices, newest first (`days`, default 30): the price, how it was set (volume-weighted fills, the mid, or Black-Scholes at the reference vol), its implied vol, the underlying, open interest and volume, and each row's chain hash.

A settled contract's settlement: the value (cents per unit of the underlying), its source (the index's frozen 7-day TWAP, the item's expiry-day A/B mark, or the last reliable value, flagged), and the hash chained to the previous settlement. Null until it settles.

post.summary: Price a ticket without placing it: give a price per contract or an implied vol (`quoteMode`), get the other back, the premium and fee, the Greeks for your size, the payoff at expiry and the margin it would need on your account (authoritative on the Crossly venue, an estimate when the partner clears). A bad entry is reported, not thrown.

Place an options order: `contractId`, `side`, `quantity` in contracts (three decimals), a `priceCents` or an `iv` (`quoteMode`), `tif` gtc / gtd (with `expiresAt`) / ioc, `postOnly`. Idempotent on `clientOrderId`. On the Crossly venue it matches price-time with self-trade prevention after a scenario-margin check; on the partner venue it routes to the partner (accept its `termsVersion`). `subaccountId` trades for a firm sub-account you may trade.

get.summary: Your options orders, newest first: `status` working (default) / done / all, `limit`, `subaccountId`.

post.summary: Cancel a working options order (on the partner venue it is cancelled there first). A liquidation order cannot be cancelled.

get.summary: Your options positions: signed milli-contracts, average open price, the price it is settled to (Crossly venue), the theoretical mark, unrealised and realised P&L in cents, the Greeks for your size, the protective-put flag and your auto-deleveraging queue lights. `status` open (default) / all, `subaccountId`.
Your whole options position on one `underlying` at expiry: the P&L curve over 50%..150% of spot, breakevens, and the maximum gain and loss (null when unbounded).

Your options margin: the scenario requirement (worst loss over a +/-40% price x +/-50% vol grid, with offsets from vault units and positions you hold), initial margin, equity and state (ok / call / liquidate) per underlying. Authoritative on the Crossly venue; on the partner venue the partner's figure decides and this is an estimate.
Your hedges: long puts protecting vault units you hold (protective puts) and the vault units locked as collateral for calls you wrote (covered calls).

post.summary: Write a covered call: lock a stored vault unit (`vaultItemId`) as collateral and sell up to one call on its own key (`contractId`, `quantity` <= 1) at a price or an implied vol. The unit cannot be sold, moved, lent or withdrawn until the call is bought back or expires; if assigned you pay cash, or the unit sells at the vault auction to cover.
Free a covered call's vault unit once the call it covers is closed (or covered by other units).

get.summary: Your options practice account (play money only, $10,000 to start): cash, positions at the practice maker's price, equity and P&L.

post.summary: Place a practice options order (the same ticket as a real one; fills against the practice maker at the reference vol). Play money only.

get.summary: Your practice options orders: `status` working (default) / done / all, `limit`.

post.summary: Cancel a working practice options order.

get.summary: Your practice options fills, newest first (`limit`).

post.summary: Start the options practice account again with $10,000: positions and working orders are cleared.

get.summary: Your two-sided option quotes: the contract, the bid and ask orders behind them, cancel-on-disconnect and the last heartbeat.

post.summary: Set (replace) a two-sided quote on an option contract: `bid` and / or `ask` each { priceCents, quantity in contracts }, posted as post-only GTC orders on the Crossly venue. Market-maker protection counts their fills; a quote inside 20% of its mid earns liquidity rewards (CBX).
Pull your option quotes on one contract (`contractId`) or all of them.
Keep your option quotes alive (cancel-on-disconnect pulls them after 30 s without a heartbeat).

Ask for a quote on an option contract: `side`, `quantity` in contracts, an optional `limitCents` (never shown). Makers quoting the series, the underlying's DMM and LPs and approved dealers are told anonymously; answers are firm for 60 s.

get.summary: Your option quote requests, newest first.
Open option quote requests you can answer.
One option quote request: yours with every answer, or one you were sent with your own answer.

post.summary: Answer an option quote request with a firm price per contract for its full size (good for 60 s; a new answer replaces your last).
Take a live answer (`responseId`) to your option quote request: it trades through the options book at that price or better, with margin and self-trade prevention.
Cancel your open option quote request.
Withdraw your live answer to an option quote request.

get.summary: One expiry of a series (an event): its markets, what you hold in each, the real worst and best case of your holdings across them (what your limit counts), and, for a full bucket set, how many sets you could merge. `venue` paper or live.
Your bucket-set conversions (split, merge, convert), newest first.

post.summary: Split ($1 a set buys one Yes in every bucket of an expiry), merge (one Yes in every bucket gives back $1 a set before settlement) or convert (No in one bucket becomes Yes in every other) on a full bucket set. `venue` paper or live. Returns the conversion and the event after it.

get.summary: Open combo requests makers can answer: legs, size and the legs' own combined price; never who asked. Your own answers are shown on them.

post.summary: Ask makers for a price on a combo: 2 to 6 legs (a market and a side each) on different underlyings, a size, and an optional limit makers never see. Pays $1 a contract if every leg comes true. `venue` paper or live.

get.summary: One combo request: its legs and size, and the answers you can see (all of them if you asked; yours if you quoted).

post.summary: Answer a combo request with a firm price a contract for the full size (good for 30 seconds; a new answer replaces yours). Real money needs an active prediction maker programme or approved dealer status.
Take one live, firm answer to your combo request (`quoteId`): both stakes are locked and the combo opens. Returns the combo.
Withdraw your combo request; its answers are withdrawn too.

get.summary: Your combos, as buyer or maker: legs and their outcomes, stakes, the pot, any reprice after a voided leg, and how each settled.
Your combo requests with every answer they got.
One of your combos.

post.summary: Check a market proposal without sending it: whether the underlying may carry markets (a built-in index or a tier A key), and what is wrong with the strike or expiry.

get.summary: Your market proposals and where each stands (pending, listed, rejected, withdrawn).

post.summary: Propose a market: an index slug or a book key, a shape (close at or above / at or below, between, touch), its strike(s) and an expiry. Ops review it; once listed you earn the creator share of Crossly's take on its fees.
Withdraw a proposal still waiting for review.

get.summary: The markets you proposed that are listed: volume, status and what the creator share has earned you.
A discussion thread on a market (`marketId`) or a series (`seriesId`): comments newest first with their replies. A commenter's side shows only when their forecaster profile is public.

post.summary: Comment on a market or a series, or reply to a comment (`parentId`). Moderated like every comment on Crossly.

patch.summary: Edit your comment.

delete.summary: Delete your comment.

post.summary: Report a comment with a reason; enough reports hide it until ops look.

get.summary: Your forecaster profile: display name, whether it is public (opt-in) and since when, and your followers.

put.summary: Go public under a display name (`public: true`), rename, or go private (`public: false`: nothing is shown again).

get.summary: Your forecasts (a probability you attached to a market, money or not) and how the markets came out.

post.summary: Forecast a market: `probabilityPercent` 0 to 100. The one standing when trading closes is scored (Brier).

get.summary: How many people forecast a market and their median probability (no names).
Opt-in forecaster leaderboards: `period` week, month or all; `metric` pnl, accuracy or brier; `venue` live or paper (practice has its own board).
A public forecaster: scores (all time and this month), open sides (never sizes), recent settled calls, followers. 404 when private.

post.summary: Follow a public forecaster: you are told when they open a position or forecast (copy-watch only; nothing is ever traded for you).

delete.summary: Stop following a forecaster.

get.summary: The forecasters you follow.
A market's history: probability points (display only, never a mark), candles on the Yes price, volume and open interest over `range` 1d, 1w, 1m or all; `venue` live or paper.
The trade tape, newest first: Yes price, size, which side took, venue. Page with `before` (the last `seq`).

post.summary: Amend a resting order's price (in its own terms) and/or whole size. It keeps its place in the queue only when the size goes down at the same price; otherwise it is re-queued and may trade at once. Returns the order with `keptPriority`.
Place up to 20 orders in one call; each answers on its own (`results[]`), one refused never stops the rest.
Cancel up to 20 orders in one call; each answers on its own.
Close a position: your resting sells on the market are cancelled and everything you hold is sold now (market, 10-cent band) or at `priceCents`. Returns the sell order.
Sell all: close every open position on a venue, or only one event's (`eventId`). Each answers on its own.

get.summary: A server-sent event stream for up to 50 markets (`markets`=id,id): `ready`, then `pm_depth`, `pm_trades`, `pm_probability`, `pm_status` and `pm_settlement`, each carrying its marketId.

schema.description: Server-sent events; each `data:` line is one JSON object.

get.summary: A server-sent event stream of your own prediction events: `pm_order` (placed, filled, amended, cancelled, expired), `pm_fill` (your side, price and fee), `pm_position`, `pm_combo` and `pm_conversion`.

schema.description: Server-sent events; each `data:` line is one JSON object.

get.summary: The prediction markets home: the busiest and soonest-expiring "Will it hit?" markets with their probability (each market's own price, display only), the underlyings with markets, which venue is live, and how many positions you hold.

Prediction markets, filtered by a book key, an index slug, an underlying kind (index | book_key | category_pair), a status (open | closed | settled | all), an expiry day or text. Each with its strike, expiry, best Yes bid and ask, last price, volume, open interest and probability.

One prediction market: its terms, the Yes ladder of the live venue and of the practice book, recent trades, settlement history (outcome, value, hash, review), the series rules text and hash, and your positions in it.
A server-sent event stream for one prediction market: `snapshot` first, then `pm_depth`, `pm_trades`, `pm_probability`, `pm_status` and `pm_settlement` as they change.

schema.description: Server-sent events; each `data:` line is one JSON object.

get.summary: The "Will it hit?" panel for a key (`bookKey`) or an index (`index` slug): its open markets grouped by expiry, each with its probability. `eligible` is false when nothing is listed on it.
The prediction board the Trading Floor and the Market Open plank show: the busiest open markets and their odds. Anonymous: never who holds what.

What an order would do now without placing it: contracts fillable inside the limit (a market order uses the 10-cent band), average price, estimated fee (Kalshi's formula), the money it would lock, and the most it could pay out.

Which prediction venue is live: self (Crossly as the DCM, money at the segregated settlement bank), partner (a partner DCM) or paper (practice only), who runs the book, where money sits, and the env each real mode still needs.
The prediction venue's rule book now and every version, each hashed and chained to the one before (`chainOk`).

The published daily settlement price of every listed market for a day (default yesterday): the last hour's volume-weighted Yes price, else the book mid, else the prior day's, with volume and open interest.

Your prediction-market account: the live venue, your account there and the terms you accepted, whether you may trade real money (region, age, self-exclusion) and why not, your self-set limits, and the practice account line.

post.summary: Open your account at the live prediction venue (the partner DCM, or your own segregated account at the settlement bank). Returns `{ venue, status, opened }`.
Accept the current prediction-market contract terms (PREDICTION_TERMS_VERSION), needed for every real-money order. Returns `{ termsVersion, venue }`.

get.summary: Your self-set prediction limits: daily loss limit, self-exclusion, a raise waiting its 24 hours, and any hold the venue placed.

put.summary: Set your daily loss limit (`dailyLossLimitCents`, null = none) or exclude yourself (`excludeDays`, `excludedUntil` or "forever"). Tighter takes effect at once; looser waits 24 hours.

get.summary: Your prediction positions (practice, live or all; open, settled or all): side, contracts, cost, value at the last price, fees, realised P&L, payout or refund once settled, and the share card if you made one.
Your prediction orders, newest first: working, done or all; practice, live or all.

post.summary: Place a prediction order: buy_yes, sell_yes, buy_no or sell_no; limit (priceCents 1-99 in the action's own terms) or market (IOC 10 cents through the best price); GTC, GTD (expiresAt) or IOC; post-only. Sells only what you hold. `venue` paper (practice) or live (503 until a venue is registered). Returns the order with its fills.
Cancel a working prediction order; the money (or practice money) it locked comes back. Returns the order.
Cancel every working prediction order you have, or only those on one market (`marketId`). Returns `{ cancelled }`.
Dispute a settlement inside its 24-hour review window (you must hold a position in the market). Payout waits for the venue's decision. Returns `{ settlementId, status }`.

get.summary: Your probability alerts: a market, a level (percent) and a direction; each fires once through the alerts hub (kind prediction_odds).

post.summary: Tell me when a market's probability crosses a level: `{ marketId, levelPercent, direction }`. Returns the alert.

delete.summary: Remove a probability alert. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: Your practice prediction account (play money only, $1,000 to start, never real or convertible): cash, money locked by working orders, positions and working orders.

post.summary: Reset your practice prediction account to $1,000 of play money: working practice orders cancelled, practice positions cleared. Once a day.

get.summary: The two "Will it hit?" practice missions (your first call; see one settle), whether the server saw each done, and the pin they lead to. Pins only.

post.summary: Make an "I called it" share card for a position of yours that settled in your favour (`showAmounts` to include what you paid and won). Returns the card with its public URL.

delete.summary: Take an "I called it" card down; its link stops working. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: Your prediction maker programme applications and their status (applied, active, suspended, revoked) and rebate.

post.summary: Apply to make markets in prediction ladders (one series, or all with `seriesId` null). Needs the ID check; ops approve. Returns the application.

Mass quote: replace your resting maker quotes on up to 50 markets with one Yes bid and one Yes ask each (post-only; an ask rests as a No bid at 100 minus it). Live quotes need an active maker programme. Returns what rests.

get.summary: The strategies the picker builds (vertical, calendar, diagonal, straddle, strangle, butterfly, iron condor, collar): how many strikes and expiries each takes, whether it needs calls or puts, and what it does in plain words.

post.summary: Preview a strategy before placing it: by template (underlying, kind, direction, strikes, expiries) or by legs. Returns each leg at its bid / ask, the net per unit (+ debit, - credit), the payoff at the first expiry, max profit and max loss (null = unbounded), breakevens, net Greeks, and the scenario margin of the whole strategy next to its legs margined one by one.

Place a strategy: 2 to 4 legs on one underlying with ratios, a quantity (units, three decimals) and ONE signed net limit per unit (+ the most you pay, - the least credit you take). Margined on the combined scenario loss of all its legs; matched against the combo book, then the legs' own books; every leg fills at once or none does. Crossly venue only (409 combos_self_venue_only on the partner venue).

get.summary: Your strategies: `status` working (default), done or all, with their legs as you hold them, net per unit, filled size and status.

post.summary: Cancel a working strategy.

get.summary: One strategy's combo book by its canonical key (`key`, from the preview or an order): bids and asks by net price and recent strategy trades.

post.summary: Ask makers for a firm net price on a whole strategy (legs, quantity, an optional limit that is never shown). Crossly venue only.

get.summary: Your strategy quote requests, newest first.
Open strategy quote requests you may answer (never your own; the requester stays anonymous).
One strategy quote request and its answers (all of them to the requester, your own to a responder).

post.summary: Answer a strategy quote request with a firm net price per unit in the canonical terms, good for 60 seconds; a new answer replaces your last.
Take a live, firm answer: both strategies go through the normal path (margin, pre-trade risk), every leg at once.
Cancel your open strategy quote request.
Withdraw your live answer to a strategy quote request.

get.summary: Options analytics on an underlying: the vol surface (expiry x moneyness) and one expiry's smile (`expiry`), IV rank and percentile against the series' own year, open interest and volume by strike and expiry, put/call ratios, the expected move to each expiry, and the historical vol of the underlying's own published series. Every implied vol is derived and display only.

Your options portfolio's Greeks (per underlying and total, with dollar delta and 1% gamma), a scenario's P&L (`priceShift`, `volShift`, `daysForward`), a price x vol P&L grid, and the beta-weighted delta against an index (`betaIndex`, default the deepest). `book` live (default) or practice.

post.summary: Roll a position to another contract as one strategy order at one net price (+ you pay, - you receive): the close and the open fill together or not at all. `practice` rolls a practice position.

get.summary: Your auto-close rule: close positions (or only in-the-money ones) a set time before expiry with a marketable limit.

put.summary: Set your auto-close rule: `enabled`, `minutesBefore` (30 to 10080), `onlyItm`, `maxSlippageBps` (0 to 2000).

get.summary: Your options notices, newest first: expiry warnings, auto-closes, exercises (a long settled in the money), assignments (a short settled in the money), expiries worthless and rolls.

post.summary: A practice strategy (play money): the same ticket as a real one, filled at the practice maker's quotes when the net is inside the limit.

get.summary: Your practice strategies.
Vault items with the biggest 24 h moves in their market price (from the order book), with units in the vault.
One book key (variantId:condition:gradeKey): its mark and history, lending depth and borrow rate, open interest and live auctions.
Which Vault Markets registrations are live (and the env each waits on), your custodian account, limits and balances.

post.summary: Open your account at the custodian partner (once). Returns `{ status }`; the custodian verifies it before it is active.
Start (or resume) the one-time ID check the money features and larger orders need. Returns `{ url }` to open, or `{ alreadyVerified: true }`.
Accept the current lending terms (needed to lend or short). Returns `{ termsVersion }`.

get.summary: Your vault holdings at the market price, with cost and P&L, and units you have out on loan.

post.summary: Turn lending on or off for a unit you own in the vault, optionally with your minimum borrow rate (APR in basis points). Returns `{ lendEnabled, minAprBps }`.
Recall a lent unit: the short has 3 days to return one. Returns `{ recallDueAt }`.

get.summary: Your positions, live (default) or closed.
One position with its loans, auctions and custodian instruction log.

post.summary: Short a book key: borrow `units` lent units (default 1; at most 25/10/3/1 by liquidity tier A/B/C/D) and sell each at `limitCents` or better, posting collateral for all of them (50% of the mark each; CBX counts at half, up to 30%). All units are borrowed or none unless `allowPartial`. A partial sale opens with the units sold. Returns `{ positionId, matched, units }`.

Buy `units` units (default 1; at most 25/10/3/1 by liquidity tier A/B/C/D) into your vault with leverage (up to 2x) from the market staking pool, paying up to `maxCents` each. A partial fill opens with the units bought and the rest is cancelled. Returns `{ positionId, matched, units }`.
Cover a short: all its units, or `units` of them, each buying any unit of the key into the vault for up to `maxCents`; each goes back to its lender.
Close a leveraged long: all its units, or `units` of them, each sold for at least `minCents`; each sale repays the pool first.
Answer a margin call: a short posts more collateral (USD, or CBX at half value); a leveraged long pays down its pool loan. Returns the position.
Cancel the working order: an unfilled opening order cancels the position; an unfilled cover or close leaves it open. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: Your price alerts on book keys.

post.summary: Alert me when a key's market price goes above or below a price (fires once).

delete.summary: Delete a price alert. Returns `{ ok }`.

get.summary: The CBX market staking pool: size, value, what it lends, utilisation, rate, insurance fund.
Your stakes in the market pool and what each redeems for now.

post.summary: Stake CBX you hold at the custodian into the market pool (base units, as a string). Returns `{ stakeId, shares }`.
Unstake: paid out after the 7-day cooldown. Returns `{ cooldownUntil }`.

get.summary: A token's phygital: the physical item it can be redeemed for, and whether it has been.
Phygitals you linked (with each redemption and its shipping address) and ones you redeemed.

post.summary: Make an NFT you hold redeemable for one of your physical inventory items.
Redeem a phygital you hold (checked on-chain) for its physical item, with a shipping address. Once per phygital.
Mark a redemption shipped with its carrier and tracking number; the redeemer is notified.
Build a bid on a Solana NFT on Crossly's book for your linked wallet to sign; the SOL goes into your Auction House escrow.
Record a sent bid; it is recorded only once its trade state exists on chain.
Build the cancel of your bid: the SOL your other bids do not need comes back.
Build the sale into a bid from your linked wallet that holds the NFT (sell + execute_sale, one transaction).
Apply a sent accept or cancel once the chain shows the bid closed.

patch.summary: Update a price rule.

delete.summary: Delete a price rule.

put.summary: Save your trade profile. Omitted fields are unchanged. directoryListed, directoryCategories, directoryBlurb, shipsFromRegion and requiresBusinessVerification are store-wide: saving them writes them onto every active catalog. paymentTermsOffered ["card","net_terms"] — without net_terms no buyer can pay on account.

get.summary: Your wholesale catalogs with item, buyer-grant and pending-request counts.

post.summary: Create a catalog. visibility public | link (anyone with the URL) | private (named buyers only); requiresBusinessVerification adds the trade gate; listed advertises it in the wholesale directory (never its prices).

patch.summary: Edit a catalog: name, slug, description, cover image, visibility, opening-order minimum, trade gate, directory listing, active.

delete.summary: Delete a catalog with its items, grants and access requests. Orders and invoices are untouched.

get.summary: A catalog's items in merchandising order, each with its retail price, trade price, minimum order quantity, case pack and quantity breaks.

post.summary: Add your Crossly listings to a catalog (up to 500), each with an optional wholesalePriceCents, minOrderQuantity and casePack. Items already in the catalog have their terms updated.

patch.summary: Change one item's trade price, minimum order quantity or case pack in this catalog. null clears.

delete.summary: Take an item out of a catalog. The listing itself is untouched.

get.summary: The catalog's line sheet: your company details and terms, then every item with retail and trade price, minimum, case pack and quantity breaks.

put.summary: Replace one listing's quantity breaks: [{ minQuantity ≥ 2, unitPriceCents }], each cheaper than the last and than the list price. An empty list removes them. Applies to every buyer at checkout.

post.summary: One ladder for many listings: breaks as [{ minQuantity, discountBps }] off each listing's own price. Returns how many were updated and which were skipped and why.

post.summary: Invite a buyer by email to one or more of your catalogs. Binds to their account now if they have one, or when they sign up.
Revoke every catalog grant a buyer (or invited email) has with you. Their terms and invoices are kept.

patch.summary: Rename a group, change its discount, or pause it (active=false).

post.summary: Add a buyer to a group by account id or by the email of an existing Crossly account.

delete.summary: Take a buyer out of a group.

get.summary: Wholesale orders: Crossly orders priced through your trade terms (catalog price, quantity break or account rate) or placed on account. Fulfil them like any order.
On-account invoices, newest first, with balance due. ?status=unpaid for open, partial and overdue together.
One invoice with its lines, PO reference, payments and whether Crossly dues on it are collected.

post.summary: Record a payment the buyer made to you directly: method ach | check | wire | card | other, a reference, and amountCents (omit for the whole balance). When the invoice is settled, Crossly's fee and the tax it remits are charged to your billing card.
Email the invoice to the buyer again (an overdue one goes as an overdue notice), with the link to pay it.
