post.summary: Make a share link for someone without a Crossly login: role view, comment or edit; expires after ttlHours (1 to 2160, default 168). The url is shown once.

get.summary: Your BYOK email providers (SMTP, Mailgun, SendGrid, SES, Resend, Postmark, Brevo, Mailjet, SparkPost, MailerSend, Mandrill, Plunk and more): label, from address, default, last test. Secrets are never returned.

post.summary: Preview a lookbook email campaign without sending: how many of the audience can receive it (opted in, not suppressed) and the rendered HTML/text.

Email a lookbook to customers now or at scheduledAt. Audience kind subscribers | all | repeat | segment {filters} | handles {handles}; only people with marketing consent who have not unsubscribed receive it.

get.summary: Your lookbook campaigns, newest first, with sent / failed / skipped / opened / clicked / bounced / unsubscribed counts.
One lookbook campaign and its counts.
Per-recipient results for a campaign: status (queued, sent, failed, skipped + reason), provider message id, opens, clicks, bounce, unsubscribe.

post.summary: Cancel a scheduled campaign or stop one that is sending (emails already sent stay sent).

get.summary: Print-and-mail jobs (beta): provider, format, pieces, estimate, status and per-piece results.

post.summary: Draft a printed lookbook mailing (beta): renders the print-ready PDF with bleed and estimates the cost from your per-piece price. Mails nothing until confirmed.
Confirm a drafted print job: acknowledgeCharges must be true and pieces must equal the job's piece count. Your Lob or PostGrid account is billed.

get.summary: Your drop-partner terms (fee, promotion tier, monthly allowance, whether you may schedule without review) and how many drops you have created this month. partner is null when you are not an approved partner — apply at crossly.net/drops/apply.
Your brand drops, newest start time first. Filter with ?status=draft|pending_review|scheduled|live|sold_out|ended|cancelled. Empty when you are not a partner.

post.summary: Create a brand drop as a draft (name, dropAt in the future, optional description, cover image and Crossly platform-listing ids). Approved partners only (403 drop_partner_required); counts against your monthly allowance (403 drop_quota_exhausted).

get.summary: One of your brand drops, with its status and any note from Crossly’s review.

patch.summary: Edit a brand drop and/or change its status: draft (withdraw / unschedule), pending_review (submit for review), scheduled (only with canSelfPublish — 403 drop_review_required otherwise), cancelled. Editing name, time or description of a reviewed drop sends it back to review. Live and finished drops cannot be changed.

get.summary: The listings a brand drop releases when it goes live.

put.summary: Replace the listings a brand drop releases, by master listing id (up to 100). Each must already be listed on Crossly — otherwise 400 listing_not_on_crossly naming them. Not allowed once the drop is live or finished.

get.summary: Your publishable keys.
get.description: Publishable keys are safe to put in a public web page — they can read your own active listings and start a checkout, and nothing else. The key is shown in full because it is not a secret.

post.summary: Mint a publishable key for a site.

delete.summary: Revoke a publishable key.
delete.description: Takes effect immediately. Any site still using it will show an empty catalog, so replace the key in the page before revoking the old one.

204.description: No Content — the request succeeded and there is no body.

post.summary: Bid on the lot currently up in a room.
post.description: Bids on whatever the auctioneer has up RIGHT NOW. Pass `lotId` to say which lot you believe that is: it is checked against the rostrum rather than used in its place, and a mismatch answers 409 with the lot that is actually up, so a stale catalogue cannot buy you something you never looked at. `amountCents` is CENTS and must be at least the room state's `minimumNextBidCents` — do not compute that yourself, because the opening bid on a lot is floored at the START price rather than start + step. Below it you get 400 `bid_too_low` carrying `details.minimumNextBidCents`, which is the figure the transaction itself used; raise to that and retry. THIS AUCTION HOUSE SELLS DIGITAL GOODS ONLY. A physical lot is refused 403 `forbidden` with `details.reason: "physical_lot"`, checked against the listing on every single bid rather than once when the room was set up. Bids by one person on one lot are throttled to a few per second — 429 `bidding_too_fast` carries `retryInSeconds`. A hammered or skipped lot answers 409 `lot_closed`. A room you may not enter answers 404, the same as one that does not exist. Success is the bid RECORDED, not the lot won: the reply names the topic the price moves on, and somebody may outbid you on the next frame.

get.summary: Every street in the world.
get.description: Active streets with `plotCount` and how many plots are `occupied`. `platform: true` is Crossly's own street (Main Street), where every public shop has a plot.

get.summary: A street: every plot and the shop open on each.
get.description: Plots in order from the entrance. Each has its `index` (0-based), house `number` (1-based), `address` (`<street>/<number>`, stable for as long as the shop stands there) and `label` ("12 Main Street"). `shop` is the open shop's directory entry, or null for a vacant plot; `shuttered: true` is a plot whose shop is not public right now — it keeps its address. `reserved` plots are newcomer plots: occupiable, never sold or leased. Each open shop's plot carries `life`: `soldToday` (the seller's sales today, America/New_York) and `window` (up to three live listings: listingId, slug, title, priceCents, imageUrl). The street carries `life.billboards` (promoted listings, paid per sale, then Crossly house ads) and `life.buskers` (shop owners on it who are live now).

get.summary: The shop at an address.
get.description: Resolves `<street>/<number>` to the shop's `publicSlug` and `name`. 404 when the plot is vacant or its shop is not public.

get.summary: Your shop's addresses.
get.description: One per street your shop stands on, Main Street first.

post.summary: Put your shop on a street.
post.description: Seats your shop on the lowest vacant plot of an OPEN street and returns its `index` and `address`; calling it again returns the plot you already have. Your shop must be public (400 otherwise). A street that takes shops by application or invitation answers 400; a full street you do not own answers 409. Main Street grows instead of filling.

delete.summary: Take your shop off a street.
delete.description: The plot goes vacant and its address may be taken by another shop. `left: false` when your shop was not on it.

get.summary: What a plot costs.
get.description: Price in CENTS (paid in CBX at spot), weekly maintenance in cents, weeks included with a purchase, and whether it can be bought now. Newcomer plots (1-2) are never sold.

get.summary: Your plots and tenancies.
get.description: Each deed with its address, price, weekly maintenance, `paidThrough`, `status` (active, grace, delinquent — a delinquent owner cannot collect rent; past three weeks late a deed is foreclosed) and any lease; plus the leases you rent as a tenant.

post.summary: Buy a vacant plot from Crossly, in CBX.
post.description: Pays the quoted price from your EARNED CBX at spot and moves your shop onto the plot. Includes the first weeks of maintenance. 409 if the plot is taken or was just bought; 403 while property is not open.

post.summary: Pay a plot's maintenance forward.
post.description: Body `{ weeks }` (1-12). Extends `paidThrough` from the later of now and the current date.

post.summary: Offer your plot for lease.
post.description: Body `{ rentWeeklyCents }` ($1-$5,000). The plot must be vacant and its maintenance current. Terms freeze when a tenant accepts.

post.summary: Take a plot on lease.
post.description: Pays the first week to the owner from your EARNED CBX and moves your (public) shop onto the plot.

post.summary: Pay rent forward.
post.description: Body `{ weeks }` (1-12). While the owner's deed is delinquent rent is WAIVED (`waived: true`), never collected.

get.summary: Plots for resale.
get.description: Live resale listings, cheapest first: address, `priceCents` (paid in CBX at spot), Crossly's `feeCents` (the 2% CBX skim), weekly maintenance, and the deed's `status` and `paidThrough` — a buyer inherits the maintenance clock. `?street=` narrows to one street.

post.summary: List your plot for resale.
post.description: Body `{ priceCents }` ($1-$100,000). The deed's maintenance must be current. A lease on it carries on with the buyer.

post.summary: Take your plot off the market.
post.description: Only a listing nobody is buying right now.

post.summary: Buy a plot on the resale market, in CBX.
post.description: Pays the asking price from your EARNED CBX to the seller (Crossly takes the 2% skim). The deed, its maintenance clock and any lease pass to you; your shop moves onto the plot if it is vacant. 409 if it has just sold.

post.summary: End a lease (owner or tenant).
post.description: The tenant's shop gets a free Main Street address again.

get.summary: What founding a street costs.
get.description: The founding premium `priceCents` (paid in CBX at spot, from EARNED balance), weekly upkeep `maintenanceWeeklyCents`, `includedWeeks` of upkeep included, `plots` on a founded street, `maxPerOwner`, the `admissions` an owner may pick (open | apply | invite), `cbx` {open, reason} -- closed until mint -- and, for the token owner, `refusal`: why they cannot ask yet (no public shop, already holding a street), or null.

get.summary: Your streets.
get.description: Streets you hold or asked to found, newest first: `status` (pending review, approved, founding, active, dormant, rejected, released), `upkeep` (active, grace, delinquent -- a delinquent owner collects no stall rent; three weeks late the street is foreclosed and closed), `paidThrough`, `admission`, `occupied` of `plotCount`, `pendingApplications`, and Crossly's `reviewNote`.

post.summary: Ask to found a street.
post.description: Body `{ name, slug?, admission? }`. Free: the name (3-32 letters, numbers, spaces and ' & . -) and its web address (derived from the name when omitted) are held for Crossly's review. Crossly's own streets and room addresses are never available. You need a public shop, and hold one street at most. 409 when the address is taken or you already hold one.

post.summary: Found an approved street, in CBX.
post.description: Pays the founding premium from your EARNED CBX at spot and opens the street: its plots exist, the first weeks of upkeep are included, and your shop stands on it. 403 "CBX opens at mint" until the token is live; 409 before approval.

post.summary: Pay a street's upkeep forward.
post.description: Body `{ weeks }` (1-12). Extends `paidThrough` from the later of now and the current date.

get.summary: Your shop's staff and their wages.
get.description: Staff are people holding a `staff` grant on your shop (invite them through the room-sharing flow). They may arrange the shop and move its stock, nothing else. `wageWeeklyCents` is paid by you in CBX; `pending` is an invite not yet accepted.

get.summary: Shops you work in.
get.description: Each shop you hold a live staff grant on, with your wage.

put.summary: Set a staff member's weekly wage.
put.description: Body `{ wageWeeklyCents }` ($1-$2,000), or null to clear it.

post.summary: Pay a staff member's wage forward.
post.description: Body `{ weeks }` (1-4). Paid from your EARNED CBX to theirs. 403 while paying staff is not open.

put.summary: Set the co-builders of your home: { userIds } -- friends (mutual follows) only, at most 4, replacing the list ([] clears it). They may rearrange your home in the world with your things and add free furniture, never your bought pieces. New co-builders get a world notice.
Wear a pin you EARNED from a quest on your nameplate, or { pin: null } to wear none. 403 for a pin you have not earned. Shows from the next room you walk into.

post.summary: Start a crew you own: { name (2-32 chars), tag (2-5 letters or digits, shown on members' nameplates) }. Answers its id and join code. 409 when you are already in a crew.
Join a crew by the code a member gave you. 404 for an unknown code, 409 when you are already in a crew or it is full (30).
Leave your crew. If you own it, the crew is disbanded. Idempotent: leaving when in none succeeds.

"Join me": send one friend (a mutual follow) a notification with a link to the PUBLIC room you name by slug. 404 when they are not a friend or the room is not public; 429 when you invited them in the last minute.

Wear something you already own -- exactly ONE of { cosmeticId } (a cosmetic you hold), { receiptId } (a Crossly purchase from your closet) or { inventoryItemId } (your own stock). The slot comes from the thing itself; slot is only a fallback for an item with no catalog shape. Replaces whatever was in that slot. Moves no money. Answers the slot and your loadout after the change.
Take off whatever is in one slot. Idempotent: an empty slot answers removed:false. Answers your loadout after the change.

patch.summary: Rename a saved look: { name (1-32 chars) }. 404 when it is not yours.

delete.summary: Delete a saved look. 404 when it is not yours.

post.summary: Put a saved look on. Every item goes through the same equip as POST /v1/world/avatar/equip, so ownership still holds: something you no longer own is listed in skipped with the reason and not worn. Slots the look left empty are emptied (cleared). Answers the appearance of the look (for your character -- appearance lives on your device), applied, skipped and cleared. Moves no money.

get.summary: Your friends (mutual follows) for direct messages: each with userId, name, the last line between you (text, at, mine) or null, and how many of theirs you have not read; most recent first.
Your direct-message thread with one friend, oldest first (the last 100 lines: id, from, text, at, mine). Reading it marks their lines read.

post.summary: Send a direct message to a friend (a mutual follow; never across a block), up to 400 characters, through the world chat guard. 403 when they are not a friend, 429 when sent too quickly.

get.summary: Everybody you follow in Crossly World, newest first, each with mutual: true when they follow you back (a friend).

post.summary: Follow somebody. When they follow you back you are friends (friends-here, invites, messages). Idempotent.

delete.summary: Unfollow somebody. Idempotent.

get.summary: The public rooms of people you follow, to walk into.
The jobs board: open staff shifts you could claim, your claimed shifts and open price checks (appraisals), as the world shows them.
Shifts you posted for your rooms, with who claimed each and how it went.

put.summary: Arrange your emote wheel: up to 8 slots, each an emote id, a moment slot or null. Returns the saved wheel (locked or unknown ids are dropped).
Walk one of your pets with you in the world, or none (kind: null).

post.summary: Rename one of your rooms.
Make one of your rooms private, unlisted (anyone with the link) or public (in the lobby and searchable).

patch.summary: How one of your rooms is laid out and lit: grouping and sort keys, theme, overlay and the arrival camera. Cosmetics and the shop layout have their own writers.

get.summary: Conventions open to sellers now or soon: title, room, dates, and how to get a table (invite, free, fee or revenue share).

post.summary: Host a convention in one of your rooms: title, dates, tables and how sellers get one (invite, free, a fee in cents, or a revenue share in basis points).

get.summary: Conventions you host and conventions you are exhibiting at.
One convention. 404 for an unknown or malformed id alike.
The host roster: who applied, who was invited, who is coming (by shop handle). Host only; 404 otherwise.

put.summary: Open, start, end or cancel a convention you host.

post.summary: Invite a seller (by shop handle) to a convention you host.
Ask for a table at a convention.
Accept: your own invitation (no body), or, as host, an application (username).
Withdraw your table or decline your invitation; as host, decline someone (username).
As host, record that a seller (username) paid their table fee off-platform. Moves no money.

get.summary: What is for sale in a public room: price, condition and stock, with market references. 404 when no such room is shared.
The shop whose public room this is (username and name), or null.
The owner's bundle deals mapped onto this room's items (itemIds null = any N from the shop). The discount is decided at checkout.
The owner's next drop (name, cover, time, live) and how many people are waiting in the room.
Items in this room open to trades, each with its trade post path.
The owner's live sale: their stream and the lot on the block, or null.
The shop's pet kind, or null.
The owner's collection rooms: one per category, brand and model they collect.
One collection room: every piece of the set, owned or missing. 404 for an unknown room or set.
How many people looked at one item in this room today.
What you have that someone here wants, and what is here that you want: matched on catalog ids.
The open trade tables in a place: who is sitting and what is laid on the mat.
The Trade Floor's wall of wants, its authentication desk and its Vault Markets ticker (vaultMovers: bookKey, name, label, units, markCents, change24hBps; only the trade-floor place has them).

post.summary: Mint an invite code to one of your rooms (visitor or staff, optional expiry in hours). The code is in this response only: just its hash is stored.

get.summary: Everyone who can currently walk into one of your rooms, and unused invites. Never returns codes.

post.summary: Let a specific user into one of your rooms (visitor or staff), no code needed.

delete.summary: Take somebody's access to your room away, or kill an invite nobody has used yet.

post.summary: Redeem an invite code (dashes optional); returns the room it opens.

get.summary: Rooms other people let you into.

post.summary: Pin an inventory item to a slot in one of your rooms: by warehouse nodeId, or by a collection container key and index.
Clear every pin in one of your rooms, so it arranges itself again.
Add a unit (rack, shelf, bin) to one of your warehouse rooms.

delete.summary: Remove units (by id, up to 500) from one of your warehouse rooms.

patch.summary: Move a rack in one of your warehouse rooms (position in metres).
Redecorate one of your rooms (wall, floor, lighting, trim...). Unknown keys are dropped; the response is what survived. `clear` lists keys to reset.

get.summary: The listings you chose for the street window of your shop, in slot order (left, middle, right; empty = newest first), and `choices`: your listings that can go in it, newest first.

put.summary: Choose up to three of your live Crossly listings for the street window of your shop, in slot order. Picks that sell drop out and the newest fill in; an empty list goes back to newest first.

get.summary: Stock not yet on a shelf in a warehouse room you can arrange (q filters by title).

post.summary: Put an inventory item (or unit) on a rack in one of your warehouse rooms.

delete.summary: Take an inventory item (or unit) off its rack.

put.summary: Save your shop room's sections and displays (validated server-side; the response is the stored layout).

post.summary: Place an inventory item in a section and display of your shop room.

get.summary: One of your interactive designs: its draft source, the last static check, and every submitted version with its review state.

delete.summary: Delete a draft design, or archive a submitted one (off sale; owned copies keep working).

put.summary: Save the draft MML source (up to 64 KB); the response carries its static check.

post.summary: Check the draft: static rules, that every referenced upload exists, and a sandboxed dry run. Budgeted per person.
A private preview token for the draft (author only) and the socket path that runs it. Budgeted per person.
Freeze the draft as a new version and send it to ops review. Up to 10 a day.

Upload one asset: kind glb (4 MB), wav (4 MB) or png (1 MB), the file as base64; purpose product (your designs, the default) or game (Carnival Studio files such as badge icons). Answers its sha256 and the path to reference from MML.
Wipe the stored state of an interactive piece standing in a place you own (a home or your boutique).

get.summary: Your decor designs and their review state. available is false until COSM is provisioned.

post.summary: Author a decor design (what it unlocks, a mesh profile and params, an asking price in COSM base units as a string). Inactive until an operator approves it.
Send one of your decor designs to the review queue.

get.summary: What your held NFTs unlock in Crossly World: each token with the capabilities its collection declared (wear, display, emote, gate, ...). Holding is your verified wallets (their synced tokens); the capabilities of a transferred token go within five minutes.
The capability kinds of spec crossly.nft-capabilities/1: what each does, whether only the creator of the collection may declare it, whether it needs review, and which clients honour it.
Your capability declarations, in every review state (pending, live, rejected with the note from the reviewer).
The live capability declaration of a collection (404 when it has none).

put.summary: Declare what the tokens of a collection can do (the whole declaration, spec crossly.nft-capabilities/1). As its creator (launched on Crossly or claimed) any kind; as a holder, cosmetic kinds only. Replaces your previous declaration; pending if it names an uploaded asset or an always-reviewed kind.

delete.summary: Withdraw your declaration for a collection.

204.description: No Content — the request succeeded and there is no body.

put.summary: Reserve one of your listings for holders of a collection you declared a holders_only perk for (or release it). Checkout refuses anybody else.

get.summary: What you wear from your NFTs and COSM copies: your pick per avatar slot (head, body, legs, feet, back) and what the room sees.

put.summary: Wear a held token on an avatar slot (refId from GET /v1/world/capabilities), or pass refId null to take it off. Its collection must declare a wear capability for that slot.

get.summary: Your COSM designs in the world: popularity toward the free chain unlock a popular limited design earns, whether it is on chain, and your opt-out. Declare what a design does with chain cosm and the design id as the contract.

put.summary: Opt one of your COSM designs in or out of the free chain unlock it earns when popular (on by default). Answers its popularity.

get.summary: Open skill contests on Crossly World games, soonest ending first: entry mode (free, sponsored, paid) and prizes.

post.summary: Set up a skill contest on a game placed in your place: title, game (its instance id), entry { mode, feeCents? }, prizes by place, funder, window, attempts. Paid entry needs the operator to allow it where it runs.

get.summary: Your contest entries (best score, attempts used, payment state) and prizes (granted, or owed until their gate opens).
The standings of a contest now: best score first (or lowest, for a time game), ties to whoever got there first.

post.summary: Enter a contest. Free and sponsored contests take you in at once; a paid one answers a client secret to pay the entry fee.
Read the fee of a paid entry back from Stripe and settle it (safe to repeat).

get.summary: Lend to the Hall: this week's exhibition (key, title, categorySlug, endsAt), your loans on show (id, vaultItemId, skuId, name, credit, since) and the vault pieces you can lend (eligible: vaultItemId, skuId, name, imageUrl, grade) -- held in your Crossly vault, not pledged, in the exhibition's category. perMember is how many you may lend each week.

post.summary: Lend a piece from your vault to this week's Hall of Grails exhibition: { vaultItemId, credit: 'name' | 'anonymous' }. It shows under your plaque until the exhibition ends; it stays in your vault (still listable and withdrawable), and stops showing if it leaves.

delete.summary: Take one of your loans off show in the Hall of Grails.

get.summary: The Game Directory: every live, reviewed game package with its players, places, rewards, contests and the piece people place.
Your game packages, each with its latest version and review state.

post.summary: Submit a game package version for review: files as { path, base64 } (game.json, thumb.png, logic/, scene/, audio/, images/). Checked like the CLI, assets quarantined, the entry document dry-run, then reviewed by a person.

get.summary: One of your game packages with every version, its review state and decision note.
Store sales of one of your game packages, newest first: item, price paid, edition, when. Never who bought. Cursor-paged: pass pagination.nextCursor back as ?cursor=.
Rewards you won in games: granted, or recorded as unfunded for COSM and CBX (a game prints no value).

A fresh game package from a template (table, arena, object; collection is an NFT capability declaration), as { path, base64 } files: the world-kit init, for an agent with no local kit. ?id=my-game&name=My Game.

get.description: A long-lived text/event-stream. Each event is one `data:` line of JSON: {eventName, eventId, createdAt, payload}. Used by `crossly dev` to forward live events to a local URL without exposing the machine to the internet. Does not replay history — you see what happens from the moment you connect.

schema.description: Server-sent events; each `data:` line is one JSON object.

get.summary: Identity check — which merchant this key belongs to, and its terms.
get.description: Returns the economics your merchant is configured with, so an integration can display accurate terms rather than hard-coding ours. Note `claimsEnabled`: off means balances are store credit that cannot leave, which is the default and the smaller regulatory posture.

post.summary: Map one of your user ids to a CBX subject.
post.description: Idempotent. Call it whenever you need a subject id; repeated calls with the same externalUserId return the same subject. Your user ids are opaque to us and unique only within your merchant, so two marketplaces can both have a user "1" without collision.

post.summary: Record cashback a user earned, in cents.
post.description: The accrual is PENDING until its maturation window closes, then converts to CBX at that moment's market price. It is denominated in cents the whole time it is pending, deliberately: quoting a token quantity up front and buying later would leave the reserve short for the length of the window. Send sourceExternalId and a retry is a no-op rather than a double credit.

post.summary: Claw back a pending accrual — a refund, a cancellation, fraud.
post.description: Only works while the accrual is still pending. Once it has converted, the value is tokens in somebody's balance and this is the wrong operation: reversing then is a debit against that balance, which is a different act with different consequences and is not something an integration key can do. This is why the maturation window has to be at least as long as your refund window.

get.summary: What a subject holds: pending cents and available CBX.
get.description: Two numbers because they are two different things. `pendingCents` is cashback earned but still inside its window — reversible, denominated in dollars, not yet tokens. `availableBaseUnits` is CBX they hold now. Amounts are strings because a token balance can exceed what a JSON number represents exactly.

get.summary: A subject's CBX ledger, newest first.
get.description: Append-only. The balance is the sum of these rows and there is no cached balance anywhere that could disagree with them.

get.summary: Your most recent reserve reconciliation.
get.description: Coverage is your reserve measured against what you owe your users, including claims already in flight. Below 100% your conversions stop — we will not credit balances that nothing backs. Claims and spends keep working, because those move value out and improve coverage.

post.summary: Start wallet verification. Returns a message for the user to sign.
post.description: Present the returned `message` verbatim to the user's wallet for signing. It binds your merchant, their subject, the address and a single-use nonce, so the resulting signature is not transferable to another address or account. A signature is required because there is no custody here: a send cannot be undone, so a typo or a swapped address is permanent.

post.summary: Complete wallet verification with the user's signature.
post.description: The signature is checked against the message WE issued and stored, never one supplied here. The nonce is single-use, so the same signature cannot re-verify an address later.

get.summary: The verified payout address for a subject, if any.

post.summary: What a claim would cost, without committing to it.
post.description: Every fee at cost, so a confirm screen can show the breakdown before the user agrees. The network fee is passed through at actual cost and includes the one-time account rent when the recipient has no token account yet — that rent is a recoverable deposit on an account the USER owns, not a fee we keep.

post.summary: Reserve a claim. Debits the balance and queues the transfer.
post.description: The balance is debited here, before anything is sent, which is the only safe order: sending first and debiting after means a crash between the two pays somebody and never charges them, and that is unrecoverable. A crash after this leaves a reserved balance and a pending claim, which is recoverable by looking at the chain. Send the same idempotencyKey to retry safely.

post.summary: Send a reserved claim on chain.
post.description: Re-checks every precondition rather than trusting the reservation: the delegation may have been revoked, the fee payer may have run dry, the address may have been flagged since. A response of `unconfirmed` means the transfer may have landed but confirmation was not observed — do NOT retry it, it needs reconciliation against the chain first.

get.summary: A claim's current state.

post.summary: Register your reserve after granting the payout allowance. Verified on chain: mint, delegate and allowance are read from the token account.

get.summary: Your events-pool balance.
get.description: Funded by the skim on in-marketplace CBX spending, the community share of withdrawal fees, and lapsed balances. Sponsor budgets are tracked separately and are not included here.

post.summary: Create a campaign in draft.
post.description: Nothing is paid until it is previewed, approved and executed. Available metrics: accruals_count, accrued_cents, spend_count, spend_base_units — all of them measure activity inside the window. `capPerSubject` is worth setting on a proportional campaign: without it one large participant can take almost the whole pool, which makes the event pointless for everybody else.

get.summary: Your campaigns, newest first.

post.summary: Compute the recipient list without paying it.
post.description: Returns every recipient and amount, plus a hash of the list. Re-previewing invalidates any prior approval by design — the approver signed off on a specific list, and if it has changed they have not approved what would now happen.

post.summary: Approve the previewed recipient list.
Pay an approved campaign.
post.description: Recomputes the list and refuses if the hash no longer matches the approved one. Payouts credit balances directly rather than transferring on chain, so a distribution to ten thousand recipients costs one internal move and is reversible if it was computed wrong.

get.summary: What a campaign actually paid, with the weight behind each amount.
get.description: The weight is kept so a payout can be explained to the person who received it. "Why did I get this much" should have an answer that is not "the algorithm".

post.summary: Redeem a user's CBX against an order.
post.description: Debits the user exactly what they spent — the skim is never added on top, because making CBX worth less when used than when sold would invert the whole reason to spend rather than liquidate. The skim comes out of YOUR fee on the order and is capped against it, so an order paid entirely in saved-up CBX does not have its whole margin eaten. Idempotent on externalId: a retried checkout returns the original spend rather than debiting twice. Spending is always free and has no minimum — that asymmetry against the withdrawal fee is what steers toward spending without ever telling anyone they cannot have their money.

post.summary: Refund a spend — give the tokens back and claw the skim back.
post.description: Returns the user's tokens AND reverses the skim out of both the community pool and operator revenue. All three move together: returning the tokens while the pool and operator kept their shares would count the same tokens twice against one reserve. The spend also stops counting as activity for campaign weighting, so buy-then-refund cannot farm distributions.

get.summary: Total CBX a subject has spent in your marketplace.
Operator revenue accrued and not yet withdrawn.
get.description: Your share of the spend skim plus your half of withdrawal fees, denominated in CBX. It sits inside the reserve until swept, which is why it is tracked here rather than inferred: without a number saying how much of the reserve is yours, there is no safe amount to take out.

post.summary: Move accrued revenue from the reserve to your revenue wallet.
post.description: Computes what is genuinely free — reserve minus outstanding balances, minus claims in flight, minus the pool, minus unswept revenue — and moves at most that. If the reserve is short it moves NOTHING, whatever the ledger says: an under-covered reserve is not a reason to stop paying users, it is a reason to stop paying yourself. Send dryRun to see the arithmetic without moving tokens.

get.summary: Earn terms on offer — longer maturation, higher rate.
get.description: A term structure on a rebate, not a yield: the user chooses WHEN to be paid for a purchase they already made, and a longer wait earns more. Nothing accrues to a balance for being held. Show these at checkout so the choice is the user's — the rate is snapshot onto the accrual, so a tier edited later never reprices a promise already made.

post.summary: Define an earn term.
post.description: Setting `isDefault` moves the default off whatever held it — exactly one active default per merchant is enforced by a unique index, because two would make "what rate did this user get" depend on row order.

get.summary: Your funded cashback boosts, newest first.
get.description: `spentCents` against `budgetCents` is the live burn. The budget is a hard ceiling enforced inside the accrual transaction, so a boost cannot overspend — when it runs out, matching orders quietly fall back to your base rate rather than failing or accruing zero.

post.summary: Fund elevated cashback on matching items.
post.description: Performance marketing priced in CBX: the spend lands as a durable balance the buyer returns to use, rather than a one-time price cut they pocket. A boost REPLACES the base or tier rate rather than adding to it — you are stating the total you will pay, and it is priced against your margin. Targeting is matched by equality on one facet; most specific wins (sku > collection > category > all). Kinds: all, category, sku, collection.

post.summary: Stop a boost from matching further orders.
post.description: Pausing does not refund anything — already-accrued cashback is a promise already made to a buyer, and unwinding it would take back cashback somebody was shown at checkout. The remaining budget simply stops being spendable.

post.summary: What would this order earn, and why.
post.description: Resolve the rate without accruing anything, so a checkout can show the real number and its reason. `source` tells you whether it came from your base rate, a tier, or a boost; `stakeBoostBps` is the part the user's own stake contributed. Quoting does NOT reserve boost budget — a quote and the subsequent accrual can differ if the budget runs out in between, which is why the accrual response repeats the rate it actually granted.

post.summary: Accrue cashback for an order at the resolved rate.
post.description: Prefer this over POST /accruals when you want us to do the rate maths — it resolves the tier, the boost and the stake boost, charges your boost budget in the same transaction, and records what rate was actually granted. If a matching boost cannot fund the order, the accrual falls back to your un-boosted rate and `boostBudgetExhausted` is true. Idempotent on externalId: a retried webhook neither accrues twice nor charges your budget twice.

get.summary: Staking tiers — what locking tokens buys.
get.description: Staking pays NOTHING. It confers a lower withdrawal fee and a higher earn rate on future purchases: a discount for commitment, not a return on a holding. Staked tokens never leave the user — they stay in their balance and stay backed by the reserve — they simply become unspendable until unstaked.

post.summary: Define a staking tier.
post.description: A user gets the highest tier their amount clears. `cooldownDays` is what makes the discount real: without a wait, a user stakes for the discount and unstakes the moment they want to withdraw, so the commitment it was priced against never existed.

get.summary: A subject's staking state and spendable balance.
get.description: `availableBaseUnits` is the number a checkout must use — balance minus anything locked. `earnBoostBps` reads zero once an unstake has been requested, because the boost ends with the commitment; `feeDiscountBps` survives the cooldown, since withdrawing is exactly what somebody in cooldown is trying to do.

post.summary: Lock a subject's tokens for a tier.
post.description: Refuses an amount that clears no tier — locking tokens for no benefit is never what somebody meant to do. One stake per subject: to change the amount, unstake and wait out the cooldown first.

post.summary: Start the cooldown. Tokens unlock when it elapses.
post.description: The earn boost stops immediately; the tokens stay locked until `unlocksAt`. The cooldown is read from the tier as configured NOW, which is the one place a later config change is allowed to matter — holding somebody to a longer wait the merchant has since abandoned would be the worse behaviour.

get.summary: Services payable in CBX, and the discount each carries.
get.description: Paying in CBX costs less than paying in dollars, which is what makes anybody choose it. These are real services with real cost behind them rather than a sink invented to soak up supply — and sinks matter: supply is fixed, so tokens that only ever accumulate starve the market the protocol has to buy from.

post.summary: What a service costs in tokens right now.
post.description: Refuses with 409 when there is no fresh price. A dollar-priced service has no honest token quantity without a spot, and there is no safe direction to guess in — a guess either overcharges the user or undercharges us.

post.summary: Pay for a service in CBX.
post.description: Idempotent on (serviceKind, externalId) rather than externalId alone: a grading submission and a listing boost can legitimately share an id because they refer to the same item, and without the service in the key, boosting a listing you had already graded would return the grading receipt and never charge for the boost. Staked tokens cannot pay — the debit checks spendable balance, not total.

get.summary: Threshold rules that fire community distributions.

post.summary: Fire a distribution when the events pool crosses a threshold.
post.description: Applies to the EVENTS POOL only — never free reserve surplus. Reserve surplus is the recirculation buffer that funds the next accrual without touching the market, so distributing it would force us to buy the same tokens back at spread plus MEV. `checkCadenceHours` bounds how often the rule may fire even when the pool is over the line: a pure threshold fires at an unpredictable moment, and the pool jumps most after a lapse sweep — precisely when engagement was worst. `distributeBps` is capped under 100% because draining the pool removes the standing balance that makes the next event credible. The rule decides WHEN only: firing opens a campaign that still needs preview, approval and execution. Metrics: accruals_count, accrued_cents, spend_count, spend_base_units.

post.summary: Evaluate a rule now. Fires it if every gate passes.
post.description: Gates in order: cadence, threshold, coverage. `outcome` names the one that stopped it — every evaluation is recorded including the declines, because "why didn't the event happen" is the question people ask and the answer is always a check that ran and said no. A missing or stale treasury snapshot declines on `coverage`: unknown coverage is not healthy coverage. Send dryRun to evaluate without opening a campaign or writing anything.

post.summary: Enable or disable a rule.

get.summary: How close each rule is to firing — the public counter.
get.description: Safe to show users. A climbing counter toward a known number is the reason to prefer cadence-plus-threshold over a pure threshold: people can see the pool rising and know roughly when the next event is possible. A trigger nobody can anticipate generates suspicion rather than anticipation.

get.summary: Unspent advertising credit, in cents.
get.description: Advertising is payable in CBX and nothing else. Your budget is denominated in dollars, priced at the spot when your payment finalized — deliberately NOT held as a token quantity, since a price move would otherwise silently change the budget you prepaid, making you a market participant because you bought ads. Credit is 1:1 with market value: with CBX the only way to pay there is nothing to discount against. Spendable on advertising only, and not refundable.

post.summary: What a given number of tokens buys in ad credit.
post.description: Credit is 1:1 with the market value of the tokens at confirmation. Refuses with 409 when there is no fresh price — pricing an entire prepaid budget off a guess is not something to do quietly.

post.summary: Claim ad credit against a CBX transfer you sent.
post.description: Send CBX to our revenue wallet yourself, then present the signature. We read the actual balance delta at FINALIZED commitment — a confirmed transaction can still be dropped by a fork, and this grants real credit. One signature can be claimed exactly once. Priced at the spot when the claim is processed, not when you signed: pricing at send time would let somebody hold signed transfers and claim only the ones that moved in their favour. A 409 means the transaction has not finalized yet and you should retry; a 400 means it will never be claimable (failed, wrong mint, wrong destination).

post.summary: Consume credit for a billing period.
post.description: Spends what the balance covers and reports the rest as `shortfallCents` — the campaign should stop there rather than running on credit that does not exist. 20% of what is spent moves to the community events pool and 80% is operator revenue; the split happens on SPEND rather than at purchase, because the pool's share is earned when the advertising is actually delivered. Idempotent on externalId: pass your billing-period id so a retried run does not consume the same credit twice.

get.summary: Ad-credit movements, newest first.
get.description: Append-only. `purchase_cbx` and `grant` add; `ad_spend` and `expire` subtract. There is no refund kind and there will not be one: advertising credit exists to buy advertising, and any exit at face value turns it into a currency exchange.

get.summary: All three balances a subject holds.
get.description: EARNED is cashback and affiliate accruals — withdrawable once matured and above the claim floor. GRANTED is ad credit, wholesale draws and promos — spendable in your marketplace only, never withdrawable, so it creates no sell pressure. CONNECTED is the subject's own self-custodied CBX, reachable through a bounded delegation; it was never our liability and does not enter the reserve invariant. `connectedAvailableBaseUnits` is delegation HEADROOM, not a wallet balance — the subject may hold less than they approved, or have revoked on chain without telling us, so treat it as a ceiling and let the spend re-read the chain.

post.summary: Which balances would pay for a spend, and in what order.
post.description: The order is granted → earned → connected and you do not get to choose it. Granted first is a security property, not a preference: if earned spent first, a subject holding both would spend their withdrawable balance down while their non-withdrawable grant sat untouched — converting a grant into a withdrawable balance one purchase at a time. Returns a `shortfallBaseUnits` rather than failing, so a checkout can charge the remainder to a card. Send excludeConnected on a flow that cannot wait for an on-chain transfer.

get.summary: Live grants, soonest-expiring first.
get.description: That ordering is the allocation order: a spend consumes the grant closest to lapsing, so value about to expire is used before value that will not. Grants with no expiry sort last.

post.summary: Issue grant credit — in-platform, non-withdrawable.
post.description: Requires a funding `batchId` for every kind except `grant_makegood`. Grant credit is spendable at merchants who receive real value, so the tokens have to exist — the same rule earned balance obeys. A makegood is exempt because compensating somebody for our failure must not be blocked on treasury state. There is no path that converts a grant to earned balance or pays it to an address, and the database enforces that rather than a comment.

get.summary: A seller's wholesale credit line.
get.description: Trade credit, not token-collateralized lending. The line is secured by receivables we already hold — the payout stream sits under a hold with an exposure ceiling — and secondarily by goods bought from our own wholesale channel. CBX is the alignment mechanism, not the collateral: a stake raises the limit and lowers the rate, bounded to a share of the earned limit so a price collapse can never remove the majority of a facility. The limit may FALL. A drawn balance is never accelerated or margin-called — there is no liquidation engine, no keeper and no oracle trigger anywhere in it.

post.summary: Recompute a limit from trading history and stake.
post.description: The earned limit is a share of trailing SETTLED payout volume — money that actually reached the seller, not listed inventory or projected sales. The stake bonus is capped at a share of that, so a seller with no history gets nothing however much they stake. A frozen line stays frozen: freezing is a credit decision somebody made, and a recompute must not quietly undo it.

post.summary: Draw against a line, receiving grant credit.
post.description: The advance lands as GRANT balance: in-platform only, so it cannot be withdrawn, cannot be turned into cash and absconded with, and adds nothing to the float that could hit an order book. Restricted to wholesale channels — the limit was sized on the theory that the advance buys goods that get sold and generate the payout stream repaying it, and credit spent on a subscription does not create that stream. Refuses if the reserve has no unallocated tokens: credit is real value and cannot be advanced against tokens that do not exist. Idempotent on externalId.

post.summary: Apply a repayment to a line.
post.description: `treasury` scope, which looks backwards next to a draw needing only `spend` and is deliberate: a forged repayment writes off real money owed to us, while a forged draw hands out credit spendable only in our own marketplace. The scope follows the loss. Clamped to what is outstanding — a payout larger than the debt would otherwise push the balance negative and read as credit nobody underwrote.

post.summary: Stop new draws. Leaves the drawn balance on its terms.
post.description: The only lever over a line, and deliberately the only one. A seller who took inventory on Tuesday keeps Tuesday's terms whatever the token does on Wednesday — the only way a credit product sits next to a volatile asset without transmitting its volatility.

post.summary: Build a transfer for the buyer to sign themselves.
post.description: Returns an unsigned, base64 transaction. The buyer's wallet signs and submits it; we never hold a key or a delegation and never submit anything, so the platform has no authority over their tokens at any point. RESERVES NOTHING — no row, no hold, no balance change. The buyer may never sign it. The SIGNATURE is the event, so treat this as a convenience and not a commitment. `lastValidBlockHeight` is when it expires: a wallet prompt left open for a couple of minutes produces a transaction the chain will reject, and you should re-quote rather than retry. `payerCanCover` is a courtesy read of their balance so you can warn before a prompt rather than after a failure; null means we could not read it, which is not the same as "no". The buyer needs no prior wallet registration: a payment proves control of the tokens, which is what a connect-and-verify step would have been proving.

post.summary: Present the signature. Returns a ship / do-not-ship decision.
post.description: Everything is read from the CHAIN at finalized commitment — the amount, the payer, the destination. Nothing you assert about the payment is trusted, because a client that can state its own payment amount can state a larger one. The response `releaseDecision` is about the ORDER, not the payment: by the time we see a signature the tokens have moved and cannot be un-moved, so the only decision left is whether to hand over goods. `release` means ship. `review` means hold — a person needs to look, and that includes the case where no screening provider is configured. `refuse` means do not ship; the payment is still recorded, because we received the tokens and that fact does not go away. Idempotent twice over: on txSig globally, so one payment cannot pay two orders, and on (merchant, externalId), so one order is not paid twice. A 409 means the transaction has not finalized yet and you should retry; a 400 means it never will be claimable.

get.summary: Payments held for a human — the ops queue.
get.description: Every row here is money taken and goods not shipped, which is not a state to leave a buyer in without it appearing on a list. `riskLevel` and `riskExposures` are the verdict as recorded at the time, not re-derived — asking a provider again next month answers a different question than the one already decided.

post.summary: A human decides on a held payment.
post.description: Only moves a payment OUT of `review`, never between the other two. A refusal that could later be flipped to a release is an approval control with no teeth, and a release re-decided as a refusal after the goods shipped is a record that no longer describes what happened. The reviewer and their note are stored on the row, because this is the decision somebody will be asked to justify.

get.summary: Your offsite-ads opt-in and its terms.
get.description: Offsite ads spend your CBX advertising budget on external networks — Google, Meta and similar — at our discretion. Your item gets promoted, and the traffic lands on Crossly. OFF unless you turn it on, and there is no path that enables it on your behalf. Media is passed through AT COST with a separate, disclosed management fee, so you can always see how much of your budget reached the auction. `minReturnBps` is a STOP, not a guarantee: below it, offsite spend auto-pauses and the rest of your budget reverts to on-platform placement. Nobody can honestly promise ad performance; what we can promise is that it stops.

put.summary: Turn offsite ads on or off. Yours alone to set.
put.description: The toggle. Nothing else in the system sets `enabled` — no onboarding default, no bulk enable, no admin override. `maxOffsiteShareBps` caps how much of your budget may leave the platform, so opting in does not mean discovering the whole thing went to Google. `minReturnBps` sets the floor below which offsite spend auto-pauses: 20000 means we must return $2 of attributed revenue per $1 spent over the window. Toggling either way clears any existing auto-pause, so turning it back on later does not inherit a pause from months ago. When one of your ads brings a buyer who purchases somebody ELSE's item, that is reported to you as spillover so you can judge whether offsite traffic is reaching buyers who want YOUR item, and switch it off if not. It is not credited back — you bought clicks, which is how every ad market works.

get.summary: What your offsite budget bought — including the misses.
get.description: Spend, impressions and clicks are reported whether or not anything converted. A report showing only conversions is a report nobody can audit, and this is a feature where you handed over discretion over your money. `mediaCostCents` versus `managementFeeCents` answers "how much of my budget reached the auction" — the two are recorded separately so the answer survives. `spilloverConversions` is sales your ads produced on OTHER sellers' items. Reported so you can see whether offsite traffic is reaching buyers who want your item — a high spillover rate is the signal to turn it off. `returnBps` is attributed revenue as bps of spend; compare it with your `minReturnBps` floor.

post.summary: Clear an auto-pause and resume offsite spend.
post.description: Returns 409 when you are not actually paused. The pause reason is worth reading first — resuming without changing anything will usually just trip the floor again over the next window.

get.summary: Whether an item can run offsite, and why not.
get.description: Reasons: `not_opted_in`, `auto_paused`, `network_not_allowed`, `category_not_allowlisted`, `no_adapter`, `no_budget`. The category check is an ALLOWLIST, so an unclassified category is not eligible. That is not bureaucracy: ad networks suspend the ACCOUNT over a prohibited item, and the account is one shared resource across every merchant using this — so one listing could take offsite ads away from all of them. A blocklist would fail open on the first category nobody thought of.

post.summary: Launch an offsite campaign for an item.
post.description: Creative is built from the structured fields you pass — title, condition as you recorded it, price, image. We generate no prose and invent no claims about condition or authenticity: an ad saying "mint" or "authenticated" when your listing says neither is a misrepresentation we authored and YOU would take the dispute for. Refuses with 403 when no ad network is wired, rather than returning a campaign that does not exist — a campaign row marked live with nothing behind it would read as spending your money when it is not.

get.description: The published terms for a design: resale, price window, secondary royalty and collaborator splits. Also reports the platform rates a designer does not control, and whether the terms are enforceable on chain — inside Crossly every rule is enforced, but a third-party marketplace honours a royalty voluntarily at best.

post.description: Publish terms for a design. Never edits: every change is a new version, and a copy sold under an earlier one keeps those terms forever. Only the designer may call it. Collaborator shares are of the ROYALTY rather than the sale price and may total at most 100%, with the remainder staying with the designer; a total above 100% is refused rather than scaled down.

Burn COSM to make a design mintable on chain. Designer-only and idempotent: paying twice is impossible, and a second call returns the existing unlock without charging. The fee is DESTROYED rather than collected. Limited editions only. Once unlocked, any holder may take their own copy on chain.
Opt a design in or out of the free chain unlock a popular limited design earns (on by default). Designer-only. Answers the popularity of the design toward the bar.

Submit a user-authored design for moderation. Designer-only, and refuses a design with no preview image HERE rather than at approval so the designer learns what is missing while they can still fix it. Submitting twice returns the existing pending review instead of queueing a second one — a moderator facing two reviews of one piece does not know which they are deciding. A design already on sale is refused.

Lock a copy and return an UNSIGNED Metaplex Core mint for the holder to sign. One call: it resolves the designer royalty, locks the copy, publishes immutable content-addressed metadata and builds the transaction — so a lock is never taken without a transaction to go with it, and a failure after the lock releases it. Does NOT void the copy; call confirm once the chain reaches FINALIZED commitment. Every royalty recipient needs a connected wallet first, and the designer must have unlocked the design.

Record a confirmed mint and void the in-world copy, in one transaction. The caller MUST have verified the transaction at finalized commitment first — an NFT recorded against a transaction that never landed cannot be recalled, and the copy it voided is gone. Idempotent on an already-confirmed request.

Release a mint lock that was never signed. The ordinary outcome of somebody closing a wallet prompt, and it leaves the copy exactly as it was. Refuses a request that has already minted, because releasing one would unlock a copy that is on chain.

get.description: Where a copy currently is: held (in-world, wearable, listable for COSM), minting (locked while a mint is in flight) or materialised (an NFT in the holder wallet). A copy is in exactly one of these, never two.

What a designer has earned, in both denominations. COSM royalties come from COSM-priced sales; cash earnings come from cash-priced sales and are funded by the buyer payment itself. The two are never converted into one another, and COSM is never cashed out.

post.summary: Buy a dollar-priced cosmetic, paying in CBX.
post.description: The SKU's `priceCents` is paid from the subject's EARNED CBX at spot. `requestKey` (8-64 chars, one per purchase attempt) makes a retry the same purchase. If the grant fails after payment — sold out, already held — the CBX spend is reversed. Refuses an earned (COSM) or stake-exclusive SKU.

post.summary: Claim a stake-exclusive cosmetic once tenure qualifies.
post.description: Bound forever, and purchasable by nobody at any price in any currency. What people buy in cosmetics is STATUS, and anything purchasable is by definition available to anyone with money — an item money cannot buy is strictly rarer than an expensive one. Tenure is the LONGEST CONTINUOUS active stake, not time since first staking: somebody who staked, unstaked and staked again has not held continuously, and that is the whole claim the item makes. A cooling stake does not count, because the commitment is already being withdrawn. Returns `granted: false` with the tenure and the requirement when it is short — that is the normal answer, not an error. Idempotent: claiming twice while the first copy is held is a no-op.

get.summary: How long a subject has held a stake continuously, in days.
get.description: The figure every stake-exclusive grant is decided on, readable on its own so a UI can show progress rather than only reporting failure at claim time. LONGEST CONTINUOUS active stake — a gap resets it, and a cooling stake does not count.

put.summary: Set (or clear) what a cosmetic unlocks spatially.
put.description: A cosmetic can gate a spatial control — a theme, a prop, a room feature — by naming a key/value pair the scene reads. Both or neither: a key with no value would claim EVERY value of that key and silently gate the whole control, so passing one without the other clears both. Pass two nulls to remove the gate entirely, which makes the control free for everyone. Treasury scope — this changes what every holder can reach, not one subject.

delete.summary: Release a handle. NOTHING IS REFUNDED.
delete.description: The COSM paid for a handle was BURNED, so there is nothing to give back — refunding would mean minting, which no support flow should be able to do. Say that in the UI before calling this; a user who expects a refund will read silence as a bug. The handle returns to the pool and can be claimed by anyone, including somebody else, so releasing is not a way to park one. Returns `released: false` when the subject held none.

post.summary: Claim a vanity handle, burning COSM.
post.description: One live handle per subject, enforced by a unique index. Collecting handles is a land grab that makes the good names unavailable, not a sink. A handle is released rather than deleted when given up, so the record of who held it survives — a handle that silently changed owner is the same impersonation problem from the other direction. There is no refund on release: the COSM was burned, and refunding would mean minting.

get.summary: What one shop-employee conversation will cost, in COSM.
get.description: A quote, priced with the SAME functions the charge uses, so the figure shown is the figure taken. Half of the fee BURNS and half moves to the market pool as a tax; the two always sum to the total exactly, because the split is applied in cents and the remainder is handed to the pool rather than derived from the complementary basis points. A pure burn would make the employee a deflation lever and nothing else; a pure transfer would make it a tax with no sink. Reads nothing and charges nothing — safe to call on every keystroke.

get.summary: A subject's COSM balance and the earn rate in force.
get.description: Balances are STRINGS of base units, and COSM has six decimals — divide by 1e6 to display. They are strings because a JSON number loses precision past 2^53, which is only about nine billion COSM: it would work in testing and corrupt balances at scale. `taper` is the emission step currently in force, which depends on lifetime supply rather than on anything about this subject — two sellers earning the same week always see the same taper.

get.summary: Total supply — minted, burned, circulating.
get.description: The one question a holder of an emitted currency cannot answer for themselves. Every figure is derived from the ledger rather than a cached counter, so it cannot drift from the rows it summarises. `reconciles` is the check you can run against us: minted minus burned minus reversed must equal the sum of every balance, and the auction debit/credit pair must cancel exactly. False means a bug on our side, not stale data. Once COSM is transferable the on-chain `total_minted` emitted by `cosm-minter` is the authoritative figure and this becomes the convenient one.

get.summary: Per-epoch emission against the backstop.
get.description: `demanded` is what activity would have earned at full rate; `emitted` is what was actually credited. Both are reported because storing only the second would make a refusal indistinguishable from a quiet rate cut. `ceilingBound` should be rare — the governor is the emission rate itself, which is a share of transaction value, so the ceiling binding means an anomaly rather than a busy week.

get.summary: The published emission taper. Fixed years ahead.
get.description: Indexed on CUMULATIVE MINTED, which is monotonic and which nothing anybody does can move backwards. Net circulating supply would be self-correcting against a healthy sink and would also be reflexive — burning to hold the taper back would become a strategy. A schedule nobody can game beats a clever loop. The final step is a floor, not zero: a terminating schedule is a loyalty programme with an expiry date, where the last cohort to join earns nothing.

get.summary: The cosmetics catalogue.
get.description: Tiers are DISJOINT and no SKU carries two prices: `premium` is cash only, `earned` is COSM only, `stake_exclusive` cannot be bought at any price in any currency. That is not a presentation choice — pricing one SKU in both currencies would expose a fixed COSM price to a floating market price, which is free money in the gap and hands limited editions to whoever automates it. `priceCents` is set only on premium, `priceBaseUnits` only on earned.

post.summary: Buy an earned-tier cosmetic. The COSM is DESTROYED.
post.description: Not credited to a treasury. Keeping it would make cosmetics a round trip rather than a sink, and the epoch backstop is computed FROM the burn — recycling would quietly uncouple emission from consumption. Refuses a premium or stake-exclusive SKU: those are not sold for COSM. Also counts toward any open community burn goal.

get.summary: Cosmetics a subject holds.
get.description: `bound` is derived from how it was acquired and is enforced by a database CHECK, not set by hand: a stake-exclusive grant and a make-good are bound forever, everything else trades. Bound items cannot be listed on the auction house or used as a fusion input. `editionNumber` identifies the ITEM and travels with it through a sale, because a reissued #7 would falsify every scarcity claim a market has priced.

get.summary: Which spatial cosmetic values this subject may apply.
get.description: Owning a cosmetic is what permits setting the room value it claims. Values no SKU claims — the stock walls, floors and themes — are free and are not listed here. Paint a picker from this rather than discovering a refusal on submit: the redecorate endpoint returns the locked items by name so a swatch can be greyed out instead.

get.summary: Open auction listings, priced in COSM.
get.description: A COSM-denominated peer market: buyers pay COSM, sellers receive COSM, and the 8% fee BURNS. It is not a cash market — a cash resale market for COSM-bought items would reintroduce the arbitrage between a fixed COSM price and a floating market price. `feeBaseUnits` was quoted when the listing was created and is held, because a fee recomputed at sale time is a quote nobody can rely on.

post.summary: List an owned cosmetic for COSM.
post.description: Refuses a BOUND item with 403. The bound flag is CHECK-derived from how the item was acquired, so the refusal cannot be bypassed by writing a different flag. One open listing per item, enforced by a unique index — otherwise the same cosmetic could be listed twice and sold to two buyers. `askBaseUnits` is a STRING of base units and must exceed 1.

post.summary: Buy an open listing.
post.description: Three ledger rows: the buyer is debited the ask, the seller is credited it, and the fee burns against the seller. Net supply falls by exactly the fee. The listing is claimed out of `open` BEFORE any COSM moves, so the loser of a race is refused rather than debited. Buying your own listing is refused by a database CHECK: it would burn the fee for nothing and is the obvious way to fake a market price.

post.summary: Fuse two cosmetics plus COSM into a rarer one.
post.description: The deepest sink available: it destroys on three axes at once — both input items AND the COSM cost — while producing something whose scarcity is real, because a recipe is the only route to it. Inputs must be owned, live, UNBOUND and flagged `fusable`. Stake-exclusive items can never be consumed: there is no way to reissue one without falsifying its scarcity, so the loss would be unrecoverable. An open listing on a consumed input is cancelled, since the owner has just chosen fusion over selling.

get.summary: What an auction listing would cost in fees.
get.description: Quote before committing. The fee is 8% of the ask, rounded UP so a small listing can never pay nothing — a zero-fee listing would be a free transfer channel, which is the one thing the design forbids outright. The seller always nets something, and a database CHECK asserts the same bound.

get.summary: Is this handle available, and what does it cost?
get.description: Reasons for unavailability: `invalid_shape`, `reserved`, `taken`. Handles are lowercased and constrained to a narrow character class, because anything that can be made to LOOK like another handle is an impersonation vector rather than an expressive option. Priced by length: short names are scarcer. Uniqueness is platform-wide, not per merchant — it is a URL namespace.

get.summary: Community burn goal progress.
get.description: Aggregate burn crossing a threshold unlocks a cosmetic for everyone who contributed — scoped to contributors, because a goal that rewarded non-participants makes contributing irrational. Only burns inside the window count; a goal counting all history would complete the moment it was created. `progressBps` is capped at 10000: the total is snapshotted on completion so a bar never reads over 100%.

get.summary: Withdrawal history, and whether withdrawals are open at all.
get.description: COSM does not leave the platform yet. `open` is false and `outstanding` lists the preconditions still to be met: an audited minter, a securities opinion, a money-transmission review, and the emission invariant proven under real volume. None of them has a date, so do not present one. The endpoint exists so a client can show that state honestly rather than hiding the feature and surprising somebody later.

post.summary: Request a withdrawal to your own proven wallet. REFUSES today.
post.description: Returns 409 with the outstanding preconditions until COSM is transferable. Built and switched off deliberately: a withdrawal rail written in a hurry the week it is cleared is the one that ships with mistakes. THE DESTINATION IS NOT A PARAMETER. It resolves to this subject’s own VERIFIED connected wallet, because a per-request destination is how a compromised session drains a balance to somebody else’s address. Idempotent on `externalId`. The debit lands before anything is minted, so a crash leaves a recoverable state rather than tokens in a wallet with no debit behind them.

get.summary: Published Merkle commitments. What you can check instead of trusting us.
get.description: Two claims become verifiable here. `cosm_emission` commits an epoch’s activity claims, so anybody can confirm emission never exceeded the sum of committed real activity — and every input is in the leaf, so the payout arithmetic can be rechecked, not just membership. `cbx_liability` commits every balance, which is the half of proof-of-reserve usually hand-waved. READ `anchoredAt` BEFORE RELYING ON A ROOT. Null means the commitment is computed and stored but NOT yet on chain — which makes it a row we could edit, so it proves nothing to somebody who does not already trust us. `totalBaseUnits` lets you check the sum without rebuilding the tree.

get.summary: A Merkle inclusion proof for one subject, against a published root.
get.description: Returns `canonicalLeaf`, a `proof` of sibling hashes, and the `root`. VERIFY IT YOURSELF rather than trusting `verified`: hash the leaf with a 0x00 prefix, then fold each proof step with a 0x01 prefix, ordering the two hashes lexicographically at each step, and compare to the root. That is sixteen lines in any language and needs nothing from us. The prefixes are not decoration — without them an internal node is indistinguishable from a leaf and membership of uncommitted data can be forged. Returns 409 if the underlying data no longer reproduces the published root. That is a disclosure event, not a retryable error: the published root stands and a proof against a rebuilt one would be worthless.

post.summary: Record a signature for a commitment anchored BY HAND.
post.description: An ops tool, not a trust boundary. Automated anchoring needs an RPC and a dedicated key; until those are wired, `attestationMemo()` emits exactly the bytes to publish, and this records the resulting signature so the verifiable story is available before the automation is. IT VERIFIES NOTHING beyond the signature’s shape — there is no RPC here to confirm the transaction exists or that its memo matches. A wrong signature recorded here produces a commitment that LOOKS anchored and is not, which is worse than unanchored. Refuses to overwrite an existing anchor.

get.summary: CBX-pegged listings and why each last moved.
get.description: A peg holds a CBX ask at a dollar target. `lastReason` says what the last cycle did: repriced, no_rate, below_threshold, clamped_floor, clamped_ceiling or clamped_change. A seller asking why their price has not moved deserves an answer that is not “it should have”. The repricer reads a 24h MINIMUM rate, never spot — tracking spot would let somebody pump CBX, watch the ask drop, and pay with cheaply bought tokens.

put.summary: Set or update a CBX price peg. OFF unless you turn it on.
put.description: Holds a CBX ask at a dollar target, repriced hourly against a 24h MINIMUM rate. Three bounds, each for a different failure: `maxChangeBps` stops one bad reading posting an absurd ask (it converges over cycles instead), `floorBaseUnits` and `ceilingBaseUnits` are YOUR limits so a sustained real move never posts a price you did not consider, and `minChangeBps` stops the ask being rewritten for a fraction of a percent. Accepting CBX means holding CBX. The peg protects the dollar value of the ASK; it cannot protect the value of tokens once you have them.

delete.summary: Stop repricing. The current ask stays where it is.
delete.description: Disabling means “stop moving it”, not “revert to something the buyer never saw”. The terms are kept, so re-enabling later does not mean re-entering them.

get.summary: The proposal queue.
get.description: Staked CBX decides what the events pool funds. Voting power is size x tenure — the same weighting the earn multiplier uses — and it is SNAPSHOTTED when a proposal opens, so staking after seeing one grants no vote on it. `totalVotingPower` is the frozen quorum denominator; recomputing it would let somebody move the bar after votes were cast. Amounts are strings of base units.

post.summary: Raise a proposal. Starts as a draft.
post.description: Requires staked CBX above `minProposeWeight`, and one in-flight proposal at a time. The limits bound a denial of ATTENTION rather than of service — attention is the resource a DAO actually runs on. `beneficiaryKind` is a CLOSED set and there is deliberately no stakers, holders, airdrop or distribution option. A proposal whose beneficiaries are the voters would be a self-payment, and a distribution decided by its own recipients is a dividend whatever it is called. The DAO decides WHAT to fund, never WHO gets paid. A `policy` proposal requests no funds and must omit the amount; every other kind must supply one.

post.summary: Put your draft to a vote. Snapshots voting power.
post.description: ONLY THE PROPOSER may open their own draft. Opening puts something to a binding vote in somebody's name, and authorship and that decision both belong to them. Opening writes a per-subject voting-power snapshot and freezes the quorum denominator. Nothing recomputes either afterwards, which is what stops acquire-vote-sell. Refuses when nobody holds enough staked CBX to vote — opening then would guarantee a failed quorum, waste a week and read as the feature being broken.

delete.summary: Withdraw your own DRAFT.
delete.description: Drafts only. Withdrawing an OPEN proposal would discard votes already cast, which is the proposer overruling the electorate — the thing the whole mechanism exists to prevent. An open proposal runs its window and gets a result. This exists so the one-in-flight limit is not a trap: without it a typo would lock somebody out of governance until the draft expired.

post.summary: Cast or change a vote while the window is open.
post.description: Weight comes from the snapshot taken when the proposal opened, so staking afterwards grants no vote on it. Changing your mind is an UPDATE, not a second vote — a unique index makes double-counting impossible even if this logic were wrong. ABSTAIN counts toward turnout and not toward approval, which is the whole reason to offer it: it lets you help a proposal clear quorum without taking a side.

get.summary: The live count.
get.description: `turnoutBps` is cast power over the frozen total, and counts abstentions. `approvalBps` is FOR over decisive votes, and does not. A proposal that misses quorum reports `expired` rather than `rejected` when finalised — "nobody turned up" and "the room said no" are different outcomes and a proposer deserves to know which happened.

post.summary: Operator block. There is no matching power to PASS.
post.description: DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC. A veto exists for the illegal and the ruinous — funding something unlawful, or emptying the pool in a week. A power to pass would make every vote advisory theatre, because the outcome would always be whatever the operator preferred. An operator who can only say no cannot manufacture an outcome. The reason is MANDATORY and stored: an unexplained veto is indistinguishable from disliking the result, which is exactly what would destroy confidence in the mechanism. Expect it to be read.

post.summary: Close a proposal whose window has passed and record the outcome.
post.description: Normally unnecessary — the hourly sweep does it. Exposed so a result can be published immediately after a window closes rather than waiting for a tick. FINALISING RECORDS AN OUTCOME AND NOTHING ELSE. A passed proposal sets a status; disbursing still requires a campaign with a preview and a human approval, and there is no endpoint here that can move value.
